nodes.title: The Idling Marrowbone
nodes.brief: You stand alone in the soot-choked engine shed of Ashgate, feeling the heavy iron thrum of the Marrowbone beneath your boots while Hesper Quill remains missing.
nodes.page: Ash-grit rasps against the corrugated tin of the engine shed, settling over the grease-puddled floor where Locomotive No. 9 stands shuddering in the dark. You trace the raw brass of the Water Key resting inside its felt-lined cradle, heavy as a dead man's forearm, while the firebox groans with a low, hungry breath. Hesper Quill's stool is tipped on its side in the dust, the driver's cap abandoned beside a cold mug of chicory. Outside, the storm clock's iron tongue hangs motionless, waiting for the first grey gusts of the season to strike the hollow gongs across the yard.

nodes.title: The Ashgate Yards
nodes.brief: The Ashgate Depot: You must prepare the idling locomotive and settle your business in the yards before the boiler pressure forces your hand.
nodes.page: Stranded passenger carriages lean against rusted buffers like broken teeth, their velvet upholstery long since rotted into damp wool and grey mould. Smoke curls lazily from nearby shanties where gangers sharpen picks and argue over coal rations under a sky the colour of wet slate. Every moment you linger lets the firebox hunger grow, burning through precious slack-wax while the Rail Barons' auditors tick their ledgers in the signal box. You must settle your business in this soot-blanketed bowl before the steam pressure mounts to a dangerous shriek and forces your hand toward the open rail.

nodes.title: The Union Locker
nodes.brief: You search Hesper Quill's empty locker for hidden notes, testing your CUNNING against a watchful union clerk to secure a greasy spare regulator valve.
nodes.page: Rusted iron hinges shriek as you pry open Hesper Quill's locker, stirring up a dry cloud of tobacco dust and old rail schedules. Inside, grease-stained logbooks lie piled beneath a heap of spare rags, their margins scrawled with cryptic notes about signal boxes that no longer exist on the company maps. A watchful union clerk lingers by the far doorway, arms crossed over a greasy canvas vest, his yellow eyes tracking your every reach in the gloom. You need to slip your fingers past his suspicious stare to find the spare valve hidden beneath the rubbish.

nodes.title: The Union Locker
nodes.brief: You search Hesper Quill's empty locker for hidden notes, testing your CUNNING against a watchful union clerk to secure a greasy spare regulator valve.
nodes.page: Behind the union clerk's turned shoulder you dig past the grease-stained logbooks and rags until your fingers find the spare valve cool and oily under the rubbish. Hesper Quill's cryptic notes on vanished signal boxes crackle as you shift them aside. Tobacco dust settles on your cuffs while you pocket the valve and ease the locker shut before those yellow eyes look back from the doorway.

nodes.title: The Clerk's Watchful Eye
nodes.brief: You search Hesper Quill's empty locker for hidden notes, testing your CUNNING against a watchful union clerk to secure a greasy spare regulator valve.
nodes.page: Shadows stretch long across the wooden floorboards as you reach deep into the dark metal recesses of the locker, your fingers brushing against cold iron. The clerk steps forward from the doorway, his boots grinding loudly into the ash-grit, demanding to know what business you have prying into company property while Hesper is missing. You slide your hand toward the hidden compartment, timing your movement against his approach, trying to snatch the grease-caked spare valve before his heavy hand clamps down on your wrist.

nodes.title: A Clash of Wits
nodes.brief: You search Hesper Quill's empty locker for hidden notes, testing your CUNNING against a watchful union clerk to secure a greasy spare regulator valve.
nodes.page:
The clerk catches your arm with a grip like a cold rail-clamp, shoving you back against the iron locker until the tin walls rattle in protest. He pockets the greasy spare valve with a dry laugh, muttering about thieves in the depot before turning his back to spit into the cinder-pit. You are left rubbing a bruised shoulder and nursing a sour temper, lighter by a valuable piece of hardware but wiser to the dangers of prying too openly in Ashgate.

The Marrowbone continues to idle outside, its boiler hissing through the safety valve as you make your way back onto the soot-dusted floorboards.

nodes.title: The Greasy Prize
nodes.brief: You search Hesper Quill's empty locker for hidden notes, testing your CUNNING against a watchful union clerk to secure a greasy spare regulator valve.
nodes.page:
Your hand closes on the cold iron of the spare valve just as the clerk's boots stop beside the locker, too late to stop the theft. The brass-threaded piece slides into your coat pocket as you nod politely to his scowl and back away into the haze of the engine shed. The iron piece is yours now, coated in thick machine tallow and smelling faintly of coal-smoke and old ambition.

The Marrowbone waits outside, its rhythmic breathing calling you back to the deck.

nodes.title: Beneath the Firebox
nodes.brief: You crawl beneath the firebox to fix a leaking injector nozzle, testing your MECHANICS against the searing heat to earn a heavy copper wrench.
nodes.page: Heat rolls off the belly of the Marrowbone in thick, shimmering waves that taste of sulfur and boiled brass, stinging the back of your throat. You slide flat onto your back in the gritty ash beneath the ashpan, worming your way toward the weeping injector nozzle where hot water spits in angry, hissing jets. The copper pipe glows dull cherry-red in the gloom, vibrating with the immense pressure building in the boiler just inches above your face. You must work fast in the choking dark before a blown fitting scalds your skin.

nodes.title: The Searing Iron
nodes.brief: You crawl beneath the firebox to fix a leaking injector nozzle, testing your MECHANICS against the searing heat to earn a heavy copper wrench.
nodes.page: Sweat carves clean channels through the soot on your face as you maneuver the heavy spanner into the tight, scorching gap between the ashpan and the frame. The fitting refuses to turn, rusted solid by years of coal-tar and chemical residue from the lower steppe, while the dripping water hisses furiously against your leather gloves. You brace your shoulder against the cold steel of the chassis, throwing your weight into the wrench just as another surge of steam rattles the valves overhead.

nodes.title: A Bitter Cost
nodes.brief: You crawl beneath the firebox to fix a leaking injector nozzle, testing your MECHANICS against the searing heat to earn a heavy copper wrench.
nodes.page:
A sudden drop of scalding water strikes the back of your hand, tearing a raw red blister across your knuckles before you can jerk away into the ash. The wrench slips with a sharp ring against the iron frame, and the injector keeps leaking a hissing stream that eats away at your precious water reserves. You crawl out from beneath the engine coughing and clutching your burnt hand, knowing the repair will cost you dearly in sweat and lost steam before the journey is done.

The Marrowbone hums impatiently above you.

nodes.title: The Heavy Copper Wrench
nodes.brief: You crawl beneath the firebox to fix a leaking injector nozzle, testing your MECHANICS against the searing heat to earn a heavy copper wrench.
nodes.page:
Your muscles strain to their absolute limit until the rusted threads finally give way with a sharp, protesting screech that echoes off the tin roof. You crank the brass nut half a turn home, sealing the weeping joint tight against the pressure and plunging the undercarriage into a sudden, satisfying silence. You crawl out from beneath the engine clutching the copper wrench used for the job, scarred by the heat but richer by a solid tool.

The Marrowbone waits, its boiler pressure steady at last.

nodes.title: The Water-Seller's Ruse
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the water-seller for enough grey water to fill the tender, testing your CUNNING against his lies to acquire a skin of oil.
nodes.page:
Thick grey dust settles on your boots as you approach the collapsible zinc cart where the water-seller sits, his leather skin-bags smelling faintly of stagnant alkali and dead moss. He spits a dark stream into the cinders and swears the grey liquid in his barrels is drawn fresh from the deep mountain wells, though you can see the crust of alkaline salt whitening the seams. You tap the side of your tin measure against his rusted hoop; the hollow clink challenges his boast before you offer a handful of iron nuts for a skin of his best oil.

He squints at the metal, calculating whether your need outweighs his greed, then reaches beneath the canvas flap to haul out a greasy goatskin flask that smells of tallow.

nodes.title: Weighing the Hollow Claims
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the water-seller for enough grey water to fill the tender, testing your CUNNING against his lies to acquire a skin of oil.
nodes.page:
Smoke drifts low across the platform timbers as you lean over the water-seller's counter, fixing your gaze on his shifting eyes while he taps a cracked knuckle against his empty barrel. He swears by the old Rail Barons that his oil is pure goose-grease from the western sheds, but the dark sediment swirling through the neck of his flask tells a different tale of refined coal-sludge. You lean closer, matching his practiced cynicism with a steady stare, turning his own oily exaggerations back upon him until he begins to blink behind his soot-caked spectacles.

Your fingers tighten on the worn handle of your copper spanner as you calculate the exact weight of his lies, waiting for the precise moment to strike your bargain.

check.label: Match his lies with cool cynicism

nodes.title: A Sour Bargain in the Ash
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the water-seller for enough grey water to fill the tender, testing your CUNNING against his lies to acquire a skin of oil.
nodes.page:
The water-seller catches your hesitation and bares yellow teeth in a grin of absolute triumph, slamming his thumb over the neck of the flask to double his price in heavy copper wire. You find yourself conceding the extra turn of wire just to save the hour, your temper flaring hot enough to singe the hairs on your forearms as you hand over the precious metal. When he finally shoves the greasy hide into your chest, the stiff leather seam catches your thumb-joint, carving a raw, bleeding split across the skin that immediately fills with black soot.

You hiss through your teeth, clutching the stinging hand while he cackles and retreats behind his zinc counter, leaving you poorer in wire and thicker in scars.

nodes.title: The Greasy Prize
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the water-seller for enough grey water to fill the tender, testing your CUNNING against his lies to acquire a skin of oil.
nodes.page:
You hold his eye until the water-seller's bluff collapses. He coughs into a rag and slides the goatskin across the zinc counter with a grumpy grunt. You secure the stopper with a twist of hemp string; the dark lubricant inside will keep the Marrowbone's valve-stems sliding smooth against the grit. It is a foul-smelling trade, but the thick, rancid fat will grease a dozen high-stress joints before you reach the edge of the steppes.

You haul the hide onto your shoulder and turn away from the dry carts.

exits.label: Carry the oil to the cab

nodes.title: Behind the Ticket Lattice
nodes.brief: You question the nervous ticket-widow about who was seen leaving Hesper's office, testing your CUNNING against her silence to learn a secret signal-pass.
nodes.page:
Worn brass handles and yellowed timetables frame the small iron window where the ticket-widow keeps her vigil behind a crisscross of rusted wire. Her fingers twitch against a stack of unprinted cardboard passes, her eyes darting constantly toward the stationmaster's locked door down the platform as if expecting a ghost to step through the panels. You place your calloused palm flat against the cold wood of the sill, asking quietly who was seen slipping out of Hesper's office after the midnight bell stopped ringing.

She draws back into the shadows of her little cage, her breath fogging the glass as she weighs the danger of answering against the greater danger of your stare.

nodes.title: Whispers Through the Rusted Wire
nodes.brief: You question the nervous ticket-widow about who was seen leaving Hesper's office, testing your CUNNING against her silence to learn a secret signal-pass.
nodes.page:
Iron wire rattles as the widow leans her forehead against the mesh, her voice dropping to a dry rasp that barely carries over the hiss of steam from the nearby shunt line. She mutters of a tall figure in a grease-stained greatcoat carrying a heavy tin box toward the southern siding just as the moon dipped behind the slag heaps. You nod slowly, filing away the description of the missing stranger while she slides a small, cold brass token across the scarred wooden counter.

There is no time to linger at the wicket now, for the station bells are beginning their erratic evening chime down the line.

nodes.title: Extracting the Ticket-Office Secret
nodes.brief: You question the nervous ticket-widow about who was seen leaving Hesper's office, testing your CUNNING against her silence to learn a secret signal-pass.
nodes.page:
Dust motes dance in the shaft of pale yellow light cutting through the ticket office window while you lean into the iron lattice, pressing the widow for names she swore to take to her grave. She presses her lips into a thin, white line, pretending to sort through stacks of obsolete platform tickets while her knuckles turn bloodless against the tin counter. You keep your voice level and low, tracing the grain of the wood with a blackened thumb as you remind her of the debts her brother ran at the coaling sheds last winter.

Her breath hitches in the dim space behind the mesh as she realizes you hold the ledger of her family's safety in your calloused hands.

check.label: Press her with the old ledger

nodes.title: A Costly Silence
nodes.brief: You question the nervous ticket-widow about who was seen leaving Hesper's office, testing your CUNNING against her silence to learn a secret signal-pass.
nodes.page:
The ticket-widow's jaw sets hard against your pressure, and with a sharp click of her wooden latch, she drops the sliding iron shutter right across your knuckles. The plate catches the side of your hand with a dull thud, scrapes skin from bone, and leaves a purple swelling bruise that throbs with your pulse. You bite back an oath as she calls out through the metal grille that she saw nothing and knows nothing of any midnight visitors.

You pull your injured hand back into the soot-laden air, nursing the throbbing pain while you walk away from the window with empty pockets and a bitter taste in your mouth.

nodes.title: The Scratched Brass Token
nodes.brief: You question the nervous ticket-widow about who was seen leaving Hesper's office, testing your CUNNING against her silence to learn a secret signal-pass.
nodes.page:
The sliding shutter remains open just a crack, and through the gap a small, wedge-shaped piece of stamped brass drops onto the wooden counter with a sharp metallic clatter. You pick it up and run your thumb over the notched edge that marks it as an old signal-pass for the lower maintenance spurs. It is a small key, but it will let you slip past the locked boundary gates without waking the yard wardens.

You slip the token into your waistcoat pocket and turn toward the waiting engine.

nodes.title: Pulling the Heavy Regulator
nodes.brief: You haul the heavy brass regulator forward as the signals drop, dragging the Marrowbone out of the depot and onto the empty rails of the Ashen Steppe.
nodes.page:
Boiler pressure throbs through the iron deck plates beneath your boots as you grip the long brass handle of the regulator and haul it toward your chest with both arms. The Marrowbone gives a deep, shuddering groan that rattles the rivets in her smokebox, her heavy drive-wheels spinning once against the greased rails before biting hard into the grit. Steam roars from the cylinder cocks in a blinding white cloud, swallowing the depot platforms and the silent figures watching from the coaling stage.

You lean out of the cab window into the rushing wind of your own making, watching the last signal-box recede into the grey haze as the engine plunges out onto the empty, ash-choked expanse of the Steppe.

nodes.title: The Union Locker
nodes.brief: You search Hesper Quill's empty locker for hidden notes, testing your CUNNING against a watchful union clerk to secure a greasy spare regulator valve.
nodes.page:
The iron hinges complain as you pry open Hesper Quill's rusted locker, and a grey flurry of old coal-dust and grease-stained manifests lifts into the air. Across the narrow aisle, a union clerk narrows his eyes behind tinted spectacles, pencil poised above a tally sheet to catch any pilfering hands. You slide your fingers past crumpled work-shirts and empty tobacco tins until they brush against cold, machined metal wedged deep behind the back panel. You pull it free: a greasy spare regulator valve, packed in tallow and ready for the long road.

You pocket the brass piece before the clerk can look up from his ledger, then turn your back on the office and stride toward the idling engine.

exits.label: Slip the heavy brass valve into your pocket

nodes.title: Beneath the Firebox
nodes.brief: You crawl beneath the firebox to fix a leaking injector nozzle, testing your MECHANICS against the searing heat to earn a heavy copper wrench.
nodes.page:
Soot flakes drift down like black snow as you squeeze your shoulders under the iron belly of the Marrowbone, crawling into the choking dark directly beneath the roaring firebox. Scalding drops of rusty water hiss against your knuckles, and the radiant heat from the ash-pan bakes your skin until your breath catches dry in your throat. Reaching blindly through the acrid steam, your fingers locate the loose injector nozzle vibrating violently against its copper seat. With a sharp twist and sheer stubborn grit, you wedge your wrench into the gap and haul until the leaking joint seals tight.

You scramble back out into the cool depot air, wiping black grease from your brow as you claim the heavy copper wrench left behind by the fitters.

exits.label: Crawl out from beneath the engine deck

nodes.title: The Ticket-Widow's Whisper
nodes.brief: You question the nervous ticket-widow about who was seen leaving Hesper's office, testing your CUNNING against her silence to learn a secret signal-pass.
nodes.page:
Through the narrow brass slit of the ticket office, the widow's eyes dart toward the empty corner where Hesper Quill's coat used to hang before the disappearance. Her fingers drum a nervous tattoo against the scarred wood of the counter, refusing to meet your eyes as the station clock ticks in the gloom. You lean in close, lowering your voice beneath the hiss of distant steam lines to match her cautious rhythm. Slowly, her resistance crumbles into a dry whisper, and she passes a scratched tin token across the ledge along with the secret signal-pass used by the night-shifters.

You memorize the cadence of the low whistle before turning away from the window into the crowded soot-choked platform.

exits.label: Pocket the token and leave the window

nodes.title: Searching the Iron Locker
nodes.brief: You search Hesper Quill's empty locker for hidden notes, testing your CUNNING against a watchful union clerk to secure a greasy spare regulator valve.
nodes.page:
Iron panels rattle as you force Hesper Quill's personal locker door open, disturbing a nest of dry roach-wings and stale pipe smoke. In the adjacent watch-box, a watchful union clerk taps his wooden ruler against the partition, keeping a sharp eye on your movements to ensure no company property vanishes. You ignore his suspicious glare, sliding your palm along the dark timber lining until your fingertips graze a cold, oiled lump wedged in the corner. It is a greasy spare regulator valve, tucked away behind old route maps and forgotten overtime chits.

You withdraw your hand smoothly, tucking the heavy metal prize into your work-trousers just as the clerk turns his back.

exits.label: Secure the valve and step away

nodes.title: Questioning the Widow
nodes.brief: You question the nervous ticket-widow about who was seen leaving Hesper's office, testing your CUNNING against her silence to learn a secret signal-pass.
nodes.page:
Pale light catches the edge of the ticket-widow's brass spectacles as she stares past your shoulder, pretending your urgent questions about Hesper are merely wind in the eaves. Her knuckles whiten where she grips the edge of her wooden ledger, guarding the depot's gossip like a dragon over cold coals. You press your advantage with a low, unhurried question about who was seen slipping out the back gate after midnight. Reluctantly, she leans forward, her papery lips brushing the brass grille to murmur a secret signal-pass that unlocks the guarded side-tracks.

You nod your thanks to the shadowed glass and walk out into the hissing steam.

exits.label: Walk out into the hissing steam

nodes.title: The Water-Seller's Skin
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the water-seller for enough grey water to fill the tender, testing your CUNNING against his lies to acquire a skin of oil.
nodes.page:
Barrels of thick, grey ditch-water line the platform where the water-seller hawks his lukewarm draughts to weary gangers with parched throats. You tap the side of his largest canvas skin with your knuckle, challenging his tall tales about mountain springs and untainted runoff from the upper ridges. He squints at you with rheumy eyes, spinning another impossible yarn about where he hauled it from, but your knowing stare pins him down. He grumbles, drops his price, and tosses you a small, tightly sewn skin of lubricating oil instead of the foul water you refused.

You heft the oily container, testing its weight against the swing of your arm before heading for the tender.

exits.label: Take the oil skin and turn away

nodes.title: Rafters of Ashgate
nodes.brief: You search Hesper Quill's empty locker for hidden notes, testing your CUNNING against a watchful union clerk to secure a greasy spare regulator valve.
nodes.page:
Dust motes dance in the shaft of amber light piercing the depot roof as you finish sorting through Hesper Quill's abandoned effects. The union clerk across the platform clears his throat with a dry rattle, folding his ledger shut to signal that your time at the locker has drawn to a close. You grip the greasy spare regulator valve tightly in your hand, feeling the cold weight of the metal anchor you against the mounting panic of the yard. There is nothing more to find among the old rosters and rusted padlocks, leaving only the iron road stretching south toward the grey horizon.

You swing down from the locker staging and head toward the footplate of the Marrowbone.

exits.label: Step down from the locker staging

nodes.title: Tending the Tender
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the water-seller for enough grey water to fill the tender, testing your CUNNING against his lies to acquire a skin of oil.
nodes.page:
Sludge-filled buckets clatter along the platform edge as the water-seller retreats into the shadows, leaving you alone with your prize beside the towering iron flanks of the Marrowbone. You unstopper the skin of oil, sniffing the thick, dark fluid to verify its purity before pouring it carefully into the main lubricator cup. Every joint and bearing along the valve gear must run smooth if you are to beat the coming ash-storms down the line. The engine responds with a low, contented shudder as the fresh oil reaches its thirsty brass journals.

You wipe your hands on an oily rag and climb up the iron ladder to the deck plates.

nodes.title: Under the Boiler Deck
nodes.brief: You crawl beneath the firebox to fix a leaking injector nozzle, testing your MECHANICS against the searing heat to earn a heavy copper wrench.
nodes.page:
Condensation dripping from the boiler shell plasters your hair to your forehead as you wriggle out from under the iron chassis. Your fingers ache around the handle of the heavy copper wrench, the metal still warm from the relentless radiated heat of the fire-bed. Down the line, a distant signal arm drops with a hollow clank, reminding you that the schedule waits for no one, not even a stalled engine with a bleeding injector. You stash the wrench in the tool box by the coal bunker, ready to throw the boiler feeds whenever the pressure calls for it.

You stand tall on the iron deck and check the water glass.

exits.label: Stand tall on the iron deck

nodes.title: Filling the Tender
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the water-seller for enough grey water to fill the tender, testing your CUNNING against his lies to acquire a skin of oil.
nodes.page:
Grey ripples settle inside the Marrowbone's massive tender tank as the last drop of liquid sloshes home against the riveted iron plates. You secure the heavy canvas hatch cover, lashing it down with a damp hemp cord so the dust of the Cinder Steppe cannot foul the reserves. The oil skin rests safely in your kit bag, its contents promising smooth running through the dry miles ahead where grease is worth more than gold. Ashgate Junction slumbers beneath its blanket of soot, indifferent to the single engine preparing to break the baronial blockade.

You take the iron fire-rake in hand and check your ash-pan.

exits.label: Reach for the heavy iron fire-rake

nodes.title: Beneath the Firebox
nodes.brief: You crawl beneath the firebox to fix a leaking injector nozzle, testing your MECHANICS against the searing heat to earn a heavy copper wrench.
nodes.page: Heat pours off the ash-clogged grate like an open furnace door as you squeeze into the narrow gap beneath the Marrowbone. Soot cakes your eyelashes and sweat carves clean channels through the grime on your cheeks. You reach blindly past the weeping copper unions until your fingers find the loose injector nozzle, vibrating and hissing live steam into the dark. Working by touch alone against the blistering iron, you twist the seating until the shriek cuts off into a dry, obedient cough. Your palm comes away blackened and scored, but clamped in your fist is a heavy copper wrench that fits the valve-shafts with a solid, satisfying weight.

exits.label: Slide back into the depot gloom

nodes.title: The Empty Locker
nodes.brief: You search Hesper Quill's empty locker for hidden notes, testing your CUNNING against a watchful union clerk to secure a greasy spare regulator valve.
nodes.page: Iron panels rattle under your fist as you yank open Hesper Quill's metal locker in the deserted depot back-office. Dust motes dance in the shaft of grey light cutting through the grime-caked window, settling over empty tunic hooks and discarded tea tins. A watchful union clerk lingers by the doorway, his boots scuffing the floorboards with rhythmic impatience, pretending not to watch your fingers slip along the false bottom of the shelf. You slide your nails into the hidden rebate just as he turns his head, hooking out a greasy spare regulator valve wrapped in an old manifest.

exits.label: Pocket the valve and turn away

nodes.title: Checking the Empty Locker
nodes.brief: You search Hesper Quill's empty locker for hidden notes, testing your CUNNING against a watchful union clerk to secure a greasy spare regulator valve.
nodes.page: Shadows stretch long across the wooden floorboards of the clerk's office as you pry open the latch on Hesper Quill's rusted locker. The union clerk stands just outside the perimeter wire, leaning heavily on a rolled ledger and watching your every move with dull suspicion. You ignore the weight of his gaze, sliding your fingers along the dark internal seam until they catch on a loose bolt. With a quiet snap of old pine, the false back drops forward, revealing a greasy spare regulator valve left tucked out of sight.

exits.label: Slip the valve into your coat

nodes.title: The Water-Seller's Barrel
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the water-seller for enough grey water to fill the tender, testing your CUNNING against his lies to acquire a skin of oil.
nodes.page: The water-seller leans against his empty iron drum, spitting dark juice into the grey dust while he swears by the old line that every drop he sells is sweet spring water hauled from the hills. You sniff the tin mug he holds out, smelling only sulphur and stagnant marsh-rinse from the ditches behind the dead carriage sidings. Catching his eye, you name the exact weight of the dregs sitting at the bottom of his barrel and watch his stubborn jaw slacken. He grumbles, spits again, and reaches behind his crate to shove a greasy skin of oil into your hands instead.

exits.label: Take the skin and leave him

nodes.title: The Ticket-Widow's Ledger
nodes.brief: You question the nervous ticket-widow about who was seen leaving Hesper's office, testing your CUNNING against her silence to learn a secret signal-pass.
nodes.page: Brass ticket wickets rattle in their grooves as the old window-glass slides back an inch, letting out the smell of stale tallow and cold tea. The ticket-widow stares past your shoulder at the silent tracks, her lips pressed into a thin, bloodless line of practiced indifference. You lean close, dropping your voice to match the hiss of the Marrowbone's cooling cylinders until she finally meets your gaze. Slowly, she traces a coded pattern against the scarred wood of the counter, whispering the secret signal-pass that opens the outer gantry gates.

exits.label: Memorize the pass and step back

nodes.title: Trading at the Siding
nodes.brief: You negotiate with the water-seller for enough grey water to fill the tender, testing your CUNNING against his lies to acquire a skin of oil.
nodes.page: Grey ripples settle in the bottom of the water-seller's tin cup as he insists the yellow liquid came straight from an upstream spring untouched by the ash-storms. You tilt the vessel toward the pale light, pointing out the dark film of coal-dust floating on the surface and the oily ring around the rim. He narrows his eyes, sizes you up against the idling engine, then shrugs in resignation. He reaches under the counter and trades his exaggerated claims for a skin of oil that smells of axle-grease and cold iron.

exits.label: Secure the oil and move on

nodes.title: Beyond the Wicket
nodes.brief: You question the nervous ticket-widow about who was seen leaving Hesper's office, testing your CUNNING against her silence to learn a secret signal-pass.
nodes.page: Cold draughts whistle through the ticket hall where hand-bills lie plastered to the walls in stiff layers of old paste. The ticket-widow keeps her eyes fixed on her ink-stained ledger, her fingers hovering nervously over the brass date-stamp. You lean against the iron grille, dropping a quiet word about the missing driver into the silence between you. She stops her stamping, swallows hard, and raps her knuckles twice against the wood to signal the secret password needed for the night shift.

exits.label: Pocket the secret and walk out

nodes.title: The Grille in the Wall
nodes.brief: You question the nervous ticket-widow about who was seen leaving Hesper's office, testing your CUNNING against her silence to learn a secret signal-pass.
nodes.page: Peeling timetables curl away from the plaster around the ticket window like dead birch bark. The widow behind the iron bars refuses to look up, her thumbs worrying the edge of a blank passenger card while the storm clock ticks heavily overhead. You slide a brass token across the scarred ledge, naming a train that hasn't run since the Great Burn. She flinches at the number, glances left and right down the empty platform, and rasps out the secret signal-pass through the wire mesh.

exits.label: Take the pass and turn away

nodes.title: Whispers at the Window
nodes.brief: You question the nervous ticket-widow about who was seen leaving Hesper's office, testing your CUNNING against her silence to learn a secret signal-pass.
nodes.page: The ticket-widow's lamp sputters in the draught, throwing long, jittery shadows across the rows of uncollected luggage stacked against the wall. She shakes her head slowly before you even speak, her fingers tightening around a brass tally-counter in her apron pocket. You match her silence, waiting out the slow throb of the Marrowbone's boiler until her resistance crumbles under the steady pressure. With a nervous glance at the ceiling, she leans into the iron mesh and breathes the secret signal-pass into the cold air.

exits.label: Leave the window with the pass

nodes.title: The Cold Depot
nodes.brief: You wake in the cold depot of Ashgate Junction beside the idling Marrowbone while the storm clock ticks.
nodes.page: Frost glitters across the massive iron flanks of the Marrowbone where she stands idling in the half-light of Ashgate Junction's dead terminal. The storm clock on the central gantry ticks with a slow, heavy pulse, counting down the hours before the grey skies break and choke the iron road with drifting dunes. You pull your collar high against the biting draft, staring down at the sealed orders left crumpled on the driver's seat by Hesper Quill. The depot is utterly empty save for the rhythmic shudder of the water-pumps and the distant, lonely clank of a switch-lever settling into place in the dark.

exits.label: Leave the platform for the stationmaster's office

nodes.title: The Iron Office
nodes.brief: The Iron Office: You search the stationmaster's abandoned office for missing papers concerning Hesper.
nodes.page:
Dust hangs thick in the abandoned stationmaster's office, coating the brass inkwells and the green-shaded desklamps in a fine grey silt. Through the cracked windowpanes, the silent bulk of the Marrowbone broods against the platform edge, her boiler ticking softly as she cools in the draft. Every surface bears the stale imprint of authority abandoned in haste, from ledger-stacks tumbling across the floorboards to the iron-bound door standing slightly ajar. Somewhere down the line, a signal-wire pings a thin, metallic warning into the empty air, drawing your gaze toward the paths waiting to be walked.

Shadows pool deep beneath the mahogany shelving where private correspondence lies half-shredded by mice and time. The air tastes of dry paper, old tobacco, and the faint, bitter tang of coal-gas leaking from a neglected stove. You can linger here among the ghosts of management, or step back out into the soot-stained corridors of Ashgate Junction where other interests stir.

nodes.title: Ledgers of Ashgate
nodes.brief: You sift through discarded ledgers using quick wits to find a hidden timetable noting Hesper's secret night route, gaining a coded destination memo.
nodes.page: Yellowed leaves of heavy rag paper flutter beneath your fingers as you turn back the moldering covers of the dead stationmaster's personal log. Ink smeared by old moisture tells a story of midnight amendments, unofficial coal allocations, and private memos concerning Hesper Quill's movements through the junction's western switches. A folded leaf of cardstock slips from the binding, bearing a series of railway shorthand marks that hint at a destination far beyond the ordinary timetables. You pocket the scrap just as a floorboard groans overhead, signaling that your time in the office is running short.

nodes.title: Decoding the Night Route
nodes.brief: You sift through discarded ledgers using quick wits to find a hidden timetable noting Hesper's secret night route, gaining a coded destination memo.
nodes.page: Candlelight flickers low against the grease-stained margin where Hesper's hurried hand has scrawled a sequence of switching codes over the printed timetable. Every fiber of your training warns you that a single misread symbol will send the Marrowbone hurtling down a dead-end spur into the ash-dunes. Your eyes track the looping pencil lines, searching for the hidden pattern among the canceled runs and ghost-train arrivals. You press your thumb hard against the paper edge, squinting through the gloom as the depot clock strikes eleven, and begin to puzzle out the sequence.

nodes.title: A Costly Cipher
nodes.brief: You sift through discarded ledgers using quick wits to find a hidden timetable noting Hesper's secret night route, gaining a coded destination memo.
nodes.page: A sudden gust rattles the window frame, blowing a cloud of fine soot across the desk and obscuring the vital marks just as your mind struggles to grasp them. You blink away the sting of ash, but precious seconds slip through your fingers while the candle sputters and dies in its own grease. By the time you force the meaning from the smeared ink, a throbbing headache beats behind your temples like a runaway piston, and your knuckles are stained black with soot that will not wash out. You stumble backward from the desk, bruised by frustration and poorer by a span of lost time.

nodes.title: The Clean Thread
nodes.brief: You sift through discarded ledgers using quick wits to find a hidden timetable noting Hesper's secret night route, gaining a coded destination memo.
nodes.page: Patience and sharp observation peel back the layers of bureaucratic deceit until the true rhythm of Hesper's route lies exposed beneath your palm. Genuine departures now stand clear of the Rail Barons' deliberate falsehoods, the secret pattern laid open under your palm. You tuck the recovered schedule safely inside your waistcoat pocket, feeling the reassuring weight of knowledge that belongs to no one else in Ashgate. A quiet satisfaction warms your chest against the chill of the dead depot.

nodes.title: Smoke and Cinders
nodes.brief: You face an angry union steward while maintaining steady composure to avoid a brawl, earning the respect of the local gangers.
nodes.page: Heavy boots grind against the grit of the platform as three members of the Gangers' Union step out from the shadow of the water crane. Their leather waistcoats are stiff with old grease and copper-riveted at the seams, and their scarred knuckles rest heavily upon the handles of iron pinch-bars. They are in no mood to welcome strangers nosing about the administrative quarters while the ash-storms gather on the horizon. You hold your ground near the station doorway, letting the steam vent softly from your coat cuffs while you measure the distance between you.

exits.label: Meet the gangers with steady words

nodes.title: The Union's Claim
nodes.brief: You face an angry union steward while maintaining steady composure to avoid a brawl, earning the respect of the local gangers.
nodes.page: Iron plates rattle on the walkway overhead as the senior ganger spits a brown stream of tobacco juice into the grey dust at your feet. He narrows his eyes at the brass valve-key tucked beneath your arm, recognizing the unmistakable stamp of the locomotive deck. The air between you grows thick with the smell of sweat, cheap grease, and mutual distrust that has kept Ashgate divided since the Long Fire. You keep your hands visible and loose at your sides, refusing to take the bait of their hostile posturing.

nodes.title: Holding the Line
nodes.brief: You face an angry union steward while maintaining steady composure to avoid a brawl, earning the respect of the local gangers.
nodes.page: Silence stretches taut between you and the gathered track-crew, broken only by the rhythmic throb of the Marrowbone idling in the distance. The union steward steps closer, his face shadowed beneath a grease-stained cap, testing your nerve with a slow, deliberate glare meant to provoke a rash move. Every instinct urges you to tense your muscles or reach for a weapon, but you force your breathing to remain slow and even. You keep your gaze on the steward's eyes, offering neither submission nor defiance as the tension reaches its breaking point.

nodes.title: A Grazed Pride
nodes.brief: You face an angry union steward while maintaining steady composure to avoid a brawl, earning the respect of the local gangers.
nodes.page: A sharp retort slips past your teeth before you can check it, shattering the fragile truce and sending a murmur of anger rippling through the gathered gangers. The steward lunges forward, shoving you hard against the brick pillar and leaving a jagged scrape along your shoulder where an iron bolt protrudes. You catch your balance before you hit the ground, but the momentary lapse in your temper has cost you dearly in mutual respect. They let you step away at last, though they leave behind a lingering debt of bad blood.

nodes.title: Earning Their Nod
nodes.brief: You face an angry union steward while maintaining steady composure to avoid a brawl, earning the respect of the local gangers.
nodes.page: Quiet endurance turns the edge of their hostility, softening the hard lines around the steward's mouth into a reluctant, weather-beaten grin. However narrowly you held your temper against their provocation, your refusal to flinch or reach for steel has earned their hard-won respect. The steward claps a coal-blackened hand onto your shoulder, and the grease-smudge he leaves carries a promise of safe passage through the yards. You step back into the main office with a valuable ally notched into your belt.

nodes.title: The Iron Office Files
nodes.brief: You inspect the locked filing cabinets under intense pressure with calm composure, recovering a grease-stained manifest of barred supplies.
nodes.page: Iron drawers shriek open on dry runners, cutting through the whistling wind outside the derelict station. Dust motes dance in the shaft of grey light piercing the cracked windowpane as your fingers sift through damp stacks of paper. Outside, boots crunch on the cinders. Time is a luxury you do not possess.

nodes.title: Calm Amid the Dust
nodes.brief: You inspect the locked filing cabinets under intense pressure with calm composure, recovering a grease-stained manifest of barred supplies.
nodes.page: Footsteps echo in the corridor outside, drawing closer by the second as a shadow stretches across the frosted glass of the office door. You steady your breathing, smoothing the ruffled edges of the manifests while your hands move with practiced precision among the rusting iron tumblers. The bolt gives a sharp warning click beneath your fingers just as the handle begins to turn.

check.label: Steady your nerves against the door //

nodes.title: A Costly Silence
nodes.brief: You inspect the locked filing cabinets under intense pressure with calm composure, recovering a grease-stained manifest of barred supplies.
nodes.page: A sudden clatter outside startles your hand, and a ledger crashes to the floor, shattering the fragile quiet. The door flies open before you can retrieve the fallen papers, and an angry clerk demands an immediate explanation for your intrusion. You slip away into the soot-stained shadows clutching the grease-stained manifest, though the delay costs you a precious hours-worth of coal and leaves a jagged scratch along your forearm.

nodes.title: The Smuggled Manifest
nodes.brief: You inspect the locked filing cabinets under intense pressure with calm composure, recovering a grease-stained manifest of barred supplies.
nodes.page: Fingers move with absolute stillness through the final stack of documents, bypassing the decoy files to unearth the grease-stained manifest hidden beneath. Footsteps pause outside the threshold and then fade away down the platform, and you stay undisturbed in the dim light. You tuck the damp paper inside your jacket, securing a vital piece of the puzzle that points directly toward the closed fueling yards.

nodes.title: Blockade on the Line
nodes.brief: A Gangers Union patrol stops you on the soot-caked platform demanding to inspect your heavy brass-handled valve.
nodes.page: Iron lanterns swing from the gantries. A dozen gangers fan out across the soot-caked platform and block every exit with crossed iron bars. Their union steward steps forward, face etched with soot and suspicion, and his eyes fix on the brass-handled valve sticking from your canvas sack. The ambient roar of the junction fades into an expectant hush as he demands to inspect your cargo under the authority of the track crews. You tense your muscles, weighing the merits of a sharp retort against a careful explanation of your hurried errand. Cold valve metal digs into your ribs as the crowd leans closer, watching for yield or fight.

exits.label: Step forward and present the valve

nodes.title: Smoke and Small Beer
nodes.brief: The Cinder Tap: You visit the local watering hole where off-duty firemen share rumors about missing drivers.
nodes.page: Warm steam and the sharp stench of cheap sulphur hang heavy inside the low-ceilinged room where off-duty firemen huddle around scarred wooden tables. Lanterns flicker through the haze, casting long shadows across walls stained by decades of tobacco smoke and coal dust. Rumors drift between mugs of bitter small beer like drifting ash, offering several promising paths through the troubled junction.

exits.label: Listen in on the corner table
Tinker with the broken draught pump
Endure the taunts of rival crewmen

nodes.title: Whispers in the Haze
nodes.brief: You listen to drunk track-hands using sharp cunning to separate truth from boasts, learning where Hesper bought extra fuel.
nodes.page: Glasses of bitter small beer clink softly against scarred oak as exhausted track-hands lean close to exchange hushed grievances. You keep your head down, letting the rhythm of their rough laughter mask your deliberate listening. Fragments of conversation piece themselves together through the tobacco smoke, pointing directly toward a clandestine meeting held near the old coal chutes.

exits.label: Follow the lead to the chutes

nodes.title: Shadows Behind the Chutes
nodes.brief: You listen to drunk track-hands using sharp cunning to separate truth from boasts, learning where Hesper bought extra fuel.
nodes.page: Rusting iron girders tower overhead like the skeleton of some prehistoric beast, dripping with oily condensation from the damp night air. Footsteps crunch softly upon the ash-strewn ballast as you stalk the periphery of the abandoned loading bays. A low murmur of voices drifts from behind a stack of rotting sleepers, confirming that the men you seek are resting just out of sight.

nodes.title: Sifting the Rumors
nodes.brief: You listen to drunk track-hands using sharp cunning to separate truth from boasts, learning where Hesper bought extra fuel.
nodes.page: Drunken arguments flare up around the scarred oak table, blurring the line between honest recollections and boastful tall tales. You sift through the conflicting stories with practiced care, watching every shift of eye and gesture to catch the ring of truth. The air grows thick with stale tobacco as you press for details regarding Hesper's secret transactions, risking a swift escalation if your questions prove too sharp.

nodes.title: A Broken Trust
nodes.brief: You listen to drunk track-hands using sharp cunning to separate truth from boasts, learning where Hesper bought extra fuel.
nodes.page: A sudden burst of misplaced laughter shatters your concentration, sending a cascade of spilt ale across the table and ruining your careful questioning. The track-hands turn hostile at your persistence, shutting their mouths and fixing you with cold, suspicious stares. You retreat into the noisy crowd empty-handed, nursing a bruised shoulder from an abrupt shove and vowing to find another way to trace the missing driver.

exits.label: Fade back into the tavern crowd

nodes.title: The Ganger's Whisper
nodes.brief: You listen to drunk track-hands using sharp cunning to separate truth from boasts, learning where Hesper bought extra fuel.
nodes.page: Words weave together through the haze of cheap tobacco until the stray fragments snap into a clear, undeniable pattern. A grizzled track-hand slides a grease-stained slip of paper across the scarred wood, marking the exact shed where Hesper bartered for extra fuel. You pocket the scrap with a quiet nod of thanks, securing a valuable secret that cuts straight through the local deception.

exits.label: Return to the main taproom floor

nodes.title: The Copper Hearth
nodes.brief: You tinker with a broken draught-pump using fine mechanics to earn free coal rations from the grateful tavern keeper.
nodes.page: Grease cakes your knuckles as you probe the rusted bowels of the tavern hearth's auxiliary draught-pump, coaxing a choked copper valve back to life with a brass-bladed screwdriver. The publican watches from behind a stacked tier of clouded mugs, his face soot-creased and hopeful as the stubborn iron diaphragm finally gives way with a deep, shuddering sigh of clean air. A greasy cloud of soot lifts toward the crooked stove-pipe, leaving the kitchen warm and the grease-traps clear of clinkers.

nodes.title: The Seized Valve
nodes.brief: You tinker with a broken draught-pump using fine mechanics to earn free coal rations from the grateful tavern keeper.
nodes.page: Sweat stings your eyes while you lean into the rusted seating-ring of the pump-gland, applying a delicate torque with your fingers to free the jammed pin without shearing the soft brass threads. The metal groans under the strain, teetering on the edge of a clean turn or a catastrophic fracture that would jam the mechanism forever.

nodes.title: A Bitter Toll
nodes.brief: You tinker with a broken draught-pump using fine mechanics to earn free coal rations from the grateful tavern keeper.
nodes.page: The thin brass pin snaps clean against the seating-ring with a sharp, sickening crack that sends a shower of metal splinters into your palm. The publican sighs, docking your promised coal rations by half to pay for a replacement peg from the smiths down the line, leaving your hands smarting from a fresh, jagged scratch that oozes dark grease.

nodes.title: The Draft-Pump Repair
nodes.brief: You tinker with a broken draught-pump using fine mechanics to earn free coal rations from the grateful tavern keeper.
nodes.page:
Working the seized brass valve with a slender pin and your knuckles black with graphite, you coax the stubborn draught-pump back into rhythmic life with a dry, satisfying chuff that draws a nod from the tavern keeper. He heaves a heavy sack of graded coal-nuggets across the scarred boards to reward your grease-stained labor, muttering that a good draft keeps the ale-smoke out of his eyes and the hearth honest.

Pocketing a grease-paper parcel of tallow-bread he slips you alongside the fuel, you feel the weight of a reliable debt settled in soot and warmth.

exits.label: Inspect the turnout switches blocked by the clerk

nodes.title: The Smoke-Room Taunts
nodes.brief: You endure the taunts of rival crewmen with cold composure until they back down, winning a round of bitter small beer and local sympathy.
nodes.page: Jeers drift across the sawdust-strewn floor from a knot of rival gangers nursing lukewarm cider by the coal-bunker. You keep your eyes fixed on your mug, breathing in the stale tang of cheap tobacco and cold iron while their barbed remarks bounce off your silence like gravel against a boiler plate. After a tense stretch, the mockers turn away, leaving a grudging sort of peace in the dim tap-room.

nodes.title: The Staring Match
nodes.brief: You endure the taunts of rival crewmen with cold composure until they back down, winning a round of bitter small beer and local sympathy.
nodes.page: A heavy-shouldered ganger leans over your bench, breathing fumes of sour mash into your face while the other drinkers fall silent to watch how much insult a Marrowbone man can swallow without swinging a fist. Your pulse hammers against your ribs, but your features remain as blank and grey as the ash-dunes outside the window.

nodes.title: A Flawed Stride
nodes.brief: You endure the taunts of rival crewmen with cold composure until they back down, winning a round of bitter small beer and local sympathy.
nodes.page: A sudden drop in your nerve betrays you, a brief twitch of the jaw that the lead ganger catches with a cruel, broken-toothed grin. They shove your shoulder hard enough to send your mug spilling across the table, costing you a copper coin dropped to cover the mess and a lingering bruise on your collarbone.

nodes.title: Silence Wins the Yard
nodes.brief: You endure the taunts of rival crewmen with cold composure until they back down, winning a round of bitter small beer and local sympathy.
nodes.page: Stone-cold patience settles over the table like a blanket of fresh ash, wearing down the swagger of the rival crew until they mutter into their beakers and look away. One older ganger tosses a tarnished token onto the wood, a grudging badge of local respect for a guard who knows when to keep his temper cool.

nodes.title: The Barons' Padlock
nodes.brief: A Barons' clerk blocks the turnout switches with a padlock and a stamped requisition demand.
nodes.page: Heavy iron chains loop through the turnout levers of the south siding, secured by an official brass padlock stamped with the crest of the Rail Barons. A stiff parchment notice hangs from the shackle, warning that all unauthorized movements out of Ashgate Junction are forbidden until the regional audit concludes. Hesper's engine sits silent behind the barrier, its safety valve weeping a faint wisp of steam into the grey evening air while you stare down the cold metal obstacle.

nodes.title: The Ticket Window
nodes.brief: The Ticket Window: You approach the barred glass partition where the ancient ticket-widow hoards forgotten messages.
nodes.page: Iron bars divide the soot-stained waiting hall from the ticket office, where the ancient widow sorts bundles of damp, yellowed telegrams by the dim glow of an oil lamp. A draft rattles the loose panes of the booking hall, carrying the dry scent of old paper and coal-dust from the tracks outside. You stand before the scarred wooden counter, where every shadow seems to hide a forgotten message or a fresh complication.

exits.label: Request a forgotten message from Hesper
Secure a brass platform pass for the yard
Ask about the upcoming ash-storm warnings
Tend to the Marrowbone's clogged water injector

nodes.title: The Widow's Ledger
nodes.brief: You withstand the widow's sharp tongue with unwavering composure until she slips you a forgotten telegram from Hesper.
nodes.page:
Grey dust lies on the oak counter while the ticket-widow taps a yellowed telegram against her teeth. Her rheumy eyes narrow behind wire spectacles, searching your face for any sign of fracture or impatience. You keep your shoulders level, letting the rhythmic pounding of a shunting engine outside fill the silence between you.

Beneath the iron bars, her wrinkled hands slide a bundle of damp papers aside to reveal a corner of faded parchment tucked beneath an inkpot.

exits.label: Return to the ticket window hall

nodes.title: The Widow's Ledger
nodes.brief: You withstand the widow's sharp tongue with unwavering composure until she slips you a forgotten telegram from Hesper.
nodes.page:
Grey dust coats the wooden ledge where the ticket-widow rests her mottled hands, her fingers twitching among damp bundles of telegrams that smell of stale tallow. She rasps a complaint about the soot settling on her counter, her voice like gravel shifting under a boot-heel. You meet her milky glare without flinching, absorbing every barbed word in heavy silence while the oil lamp flickers against the grease-stained walls.

Slowly, her chin trembles and the hostility drains into the floorboards as she reaches beneath the partition to slide a forgotten scrap of paper across the wood.

nodes.title: Reaching Across the Glass
nodes.brief: You withstand the widow's sharp tongue with unwavering composure until she slips you a forgotten telegram from Hesper.
nodes.page: Sudden commotion rattles the station rafters as a squad of the Barons' yard police tramps down the outer corridor, iron-shod boots pounding the floorboards. The old woman's eyes widen in terror and she starts to snatch the yellowed message back from the slit in the glass before your fingers can close around it. Your breath catches in your throat, and you force yourself not to flinch against the rising panic of the moment while the shouting draws dangerously closer to the ticket wicket.

nodes.title: A Slip of the Tongue
nodes.brief: You withstand the widow's sharp tongue with unwavering composure until she slips you a forgotten telegram from Hesper.
nodes.page: Panic snatches at your breath just as the iron-shod boots halt directly outside the window, and your hand jerks back, knocking a heavy brass inkwell across the counter. Dark ink floods the wooden boards, soaking into the widow's precious bundles of damp telegrams and drawing an immediate, furious shriek from behind the iron bars. The yard police hammer their truncheons against the exterior wall to investigate the racket, costing you precious minutes and leaving your fingers permanently stained with violet ink before you manage to slip away into the smoky shadows.

nodes.title: The Hidden Dispatch
nodes.brief: You withstand the widow's sharp tongue with unwavering composure until she slips you a forgotten telegram from Hesper.
nodes.page: Despite the sudden shouting in the corridor and the heart-stopping clatter of the Barons' patrol outside, your fingers hold firm, slipping through the iron bars to snatch the scrap of paper just as the widow lets go. You tuck the damp dispatch into your greasy jacket lining, however narrowly escaping notice as the heavy footsteps pass the window without stopping to peer inside. The paper is cold to the touch, bearing Hesper Quill's hurried handwriting in grease-pencil.

nodes.title: Beneath the Iron Awning
nodes.brief: You sit quietly through her endless complaints maintaining deep composure, securing a brass platform pass that bypasses the yard police.
nodes.page: Shadows lengthen across the platform as coal dust drifts through the rusted girders overhead, settling on the brim of your cap like a fine grey snow. The ticket-widow continues her endless monologue about the rising price of lamp oil and the laziness of the track crews, expecting an argument to fuel her afternoon. You lean against the stained brick pillar, your face a mask of dull obedience, offering neither agreement nor insult to break the steady rhythm of her complaining.

nodes.title: The Heavy Air of Ashgate
nodes.brief: You sit quietly through her endless complaints maintaining deep composure, securing a brass platform pass that bypasses the yard police.
nodes.page: Time stretches thin in the stagnant heat of the station hall, thick with the smell of scorched coal and damp wool. The old woman pauses to hawk up a mouthful of phlegm and wipe her spectacles on her apron, watching you closely for any sign of rebellion or impatience. You keep your shoulders loose and your breathing slow, matching the steady, mournful wheeze of a distant shunt-engine idling on the middle line.

nodes.title: The Inspector's Shadow
nodes.brief: You sit quietly through her endless complaints maintaining deep composure, securing a brass platform pass that bypasses the yard police.
nodes.page: Heavy footsteps crunch upon the gravel outside the ticket office as a senior inspector from the Rail Barons approaches, swinging a brass-capped cane with an aggressive rhythm. The ticket-widow freezes mid-sentence, her rheumy eyes darting toward the open door where the inspector's shadow falls long and sharp across the threshold. Your posture stays serene and your breathing even, the trembling of your hands hidden behind your back while footsteps draw closer to the counter.

nodes.title: A Costly Hesitation
nodes.brief: You sit quietly through her endless complaints maintaining deep composure, securing a brass platform pass that bypasses the yard police.
nodes.page: A sudden gust of wind rattles the corrugated tin roof, blowing a cloud of stinging ash through the ticket window and causing you to blink sharply at the worst possible second. The movement catches the inspector's eye, and he raps his brass-capped cane hard against the wooden counter, demanding your travel papers and docking a day's wages for loitering near the restricted platforms. You swallow the bitter taste of defeat as he pockets your coinage, leaving you poorer and nursing a dull ache in your shoulder where his guard shoved you aside.

nodes.title: The Brass Token
nodes.brief: You sit quietly through her endless complaints maintaining deep composure, securing a brass platform pass that bypasses the yard police.
nodes.page: Through the rising cloud of soot and the sharp rap of the inspector's cane, your composure remains unbroken, projecting the dull, indifferent air of a worker beneath notice. The inspector grunts in disappointment, turns on his heel, and marches away down the platform without demanding your papers. The ancient widow, grudgingly impressed by your iron patience, reaches into a rusted tin box and slides a heavy, notched brass token across the wood that opens the yard gates.

nodes.title: The Widow's Counsel
nodes.brief: You absorb her cryptic warnings about the upcoming ash-storm with steady composure, earning an old oil-skin coat for the road.
nodes.page:
Saliva collects in the back of your throat as the wind howls against the iron grating, carrying tiny shards of grey mineral that bite at your exposed skin. The ticket-widow leans closer, her rheumy eyes narrowing behind thick spectacles mended with greasy twine, while her papery fingers drum a slow, hollow tattoo upon the varnished counter. She speaks of the great grey squalls that rise unbidden from the southern flats, scouring the track clean of both rail and sleeper before a man can even reach for his shovel. You listen without flinching, letting her bitter talk wash over your shoulders like cold boiler-water.

Satisfied by your granite stillness, she reaches beneath the scarred ledge and drags forth a heavy oil-skin coat stiffened by decades of grease and weather, shoving it across the wooden sill towards your waiting hands.

nodes.title: Beneath the Tin Roof
nodes.brief: You absorb her cryptic warnings about the upcoming ash-storm with steady composure, earning an old oil-skin coat for the road.
nodes.page:
Condensation drips against the rusted corrugated iron above, smelling sharply of damp soot and old coal-gas. The widow's warning hangs heavily in the gloom, filled with dark tales of signal-wires snapping under the strain of frozen ash and engines found cold and empty miles out on the barren steppes. You nod slowly, keeping your weight balanced evenly on the balls of your boots, neither rushing her words nor offering false comfort. Beneath the battered counter, her hand rummages among dusty ledgers before emerging with a garment that smells powerfully of mutton fat and paraffin.

She drops the heavy oil-skin onto the scratched wood between you, a tangible shield against the coming gales.

nodes.title: Holding the Line
nodes.brief: You absorb her cryptic warnings about the upcoming ash-storm with steady composure, earning an old oil-skin coat for the road.
nodes.page: A sudden, violent gust rattles the station's timber frames, wrenching a loose shutter from its rusted hinges and sending a cloud of blinding grit straight into your eyes. The senior inspector's heavy boots scrape loudly on the gravel platform just beyond the frosted glass, pausing as if he smells your hesitation through the very walls. Every instinct urges you to dart away or curse aloud at the sudden onslaught, but you force your breathing to remain deep and measured, anchoring your gaze upon the ticket-widow's yellowed fingers.

check.label: Maintain absolute silence against the ash

nodes.title: Scoured by Grit
nodes.brief: You absorb her cryptic warnings about the upcoming ash-storm with steady composure, earning an old oil-skin coat for the road.
nodes.page: The stinging grit finds the corners of your eyes, forcing a sharp, involuntary blink and a sudden, ragged cough that rattles in your raw chest. Outside on the gravel, the inspector's cane hits the stones with an angry double-rap, and boots swing toward the little wicket window. You stumble backward against a stack of discarded mail crates, knocking a tin box of spare nibs clattering across the floorboards. The noise draws an immediate, sharp hiss from the widow, who ducks below her counter with a curse. You snatch up the dropped oil-skin just as a fist rattles the locked outer door. The price is a bruised shoulder and a racing pulse.

nodes.title: The Oiled Wool
nodes.brief: You absorb her cryptic warnings about the upcoming ash-storm with steady composure, earning an old oil-skin coat for the road.
nodes.page: You weather the sudden squall without a single flinch, letting the blinding grit sting your eyelids until the wind passes over and the station roof settles back into sullen creaking. The inspector's footsteps crunch away down the platform, their menacing rhythm fading into the general hum of the junction. The ticket-widow lets out a dry, rattling chuckle, her initial suspicion melting into a grudging, iron-hard respect that binds her fortunes to yours for whatever lies down the line. She pushes the grease-soaked oil-skin across the wood and finishes with a firm nod of comradeship among the rails.

nodes.title: The Stubborn Die
nodes.brief: You fix her jammed ticket-stamping press using clever mechanics, receiving a stamped pass that grants access to the restricted sidings.
nodes.page:
Brass filings gleam like gold dust beneath your fingernails as you probe the delicate brass housing of the ancient ticket-stamping press, finding a sheared pin wedged deep in the cog-teeth. The machine has served this lonely junction since the old Board days, and its bronze gears are choked hard with decades of impacted graphite and dry soot. You reach into your pocket for the narrow needle-file, working the cramped metal levers with practiced patience until the jammed cylinder gives a sharp, metallic click and slides smoothly home.

The widow watches your handiwork with narrowed, calculating eyes, then reaches for a brass-faced punch and stamps a heavy cardboard slip.

nodes.title: The Jammed Cogs
nodes.brief: You fix her jammed ticket-stamping press using clever mechanics, receiving a stamped pass that grants access to the restricted sidings.
nodes.page: Your thumb guides the slender steel file into the heart of the brass mechanism, scraping away a jagged ridge of copper burr that has locked the stamping die fast. The metal is freezing cold to the touch, and the dim light from the grease-lamp flickers dangerously as another tremor shakes the station floorboards from the yards outside. If you press too hard, the delicate tooth will snap off entirely, leaving the press an inert lump of scrap and cutting off your only legal route through the restricted sidings. You hold your breath, steadying the tiny file against the palm of your hand as you apply the final, delicate pressure to the stubborn bronze pawl.

nodes.title: A Broken Tooth
nodes.brief: You fix her jammed ticket-stamping press using clever mechanics, receiving a stamped pass that grants access to the restricted sidings.
nodes.page: The file slips with a harsh screech against the hardened brass, biting deep into the soft meat of your thumb and shearing the tip of the delicate tooth right off the cog. A bead of dark blood wells up instantly, staining the greasy metal frame as the machine emits a dull, metallic thud and locks tighter than before. The ticket-widow snorts with disgust, snatching the ruined tool from your grasp and tossing it into a drawer of broken scrap. Though she still hands you the stamped pass with a muttered insult about clumsy firemen, the delay costs you precious minutes while the station yard grows restless outside.

nodes.title: The Stamped Brass
nodes.brief: You fix her jammed ticket-stamping press using clever mechanics, receiving a stamped pass that grants access to the restricted sidings.
nodes.page: The delicate steel file bites true, clearing the impacted soot and copper filings from the bronze housing with a soft, satisfying hiss of released tension. The stamping die springs back into its proper vertical groove, ready to press ink onto any surface set before it. The widow lets out a low whistle of appreciation and reaches into her leather apron to hand you a brass-rimmed token notched with the private mark of the restricted sidings. It is a small key to closed doors, won by keeping your hands from shaking and listening for the music of machinery.

nodes.title: The Choked Injector
nodes.brief: The Marrowbone's water injector clogs with dry ash just as you prepare to clear the yard.
nodes.page: You climb back onto the footplate of Locomotive No. 9, wiping the coal dust from your brow as the brass boiler throws comforting heat against the chill of the yard. You reach for the water injector valve to prime the feed before building up a full head of steam for the run to the steppes, but your hand pauses at the strange, dead silence of the pipework. Instead of the familiar high-pitched hiss of rushing water, there is only a dull, choked gurgle and a plume of dry, grey dust puffing out from the overflow cock. Fine ash has drifted into the tender tank during the night, baking hard within the copper feed-tubes into a stubborn plug of grey cement. The Marrowbone stands helpless with an empty belly, and the steam gauge climbs steadily toward the red line while the yard signals begin to drop for your departure.

nodes.title: The Stranded Carriages
nodes.brief: The Stranded Carriages: You explore a row of abandoned passenger coaches rusting on a weed-choked siding.
nodes.page: Rotting teak coaches lean against one another on the weed-choked siding like exhausted draft horses past their prime, their faded crimson paint blistered by decades of alkaline wind. Tarnished brass window frames peer blindly into the grey ash-dunes while rusted iron vestibules gape open to the biting draft, inviting you to wade deeper into the forgotten debris of wealthier years. You can pick your way past shattered mahogany paneling toward the forward compartments, squeeze through a narrow corridor choked with drifted silt, or turn your attention elsewhere along the sprawling railway yard.

exits.label: Search through the shattered first-class compartments
Pry open the rusted luggage van doors
Investigate the dark shadows near the guards van
Overhaul the steam heating valves on the floor
Approach the Barons inspection carriage on the main line

nodes.title: Velvet and Silt
nodes.brief: You search through luxury compartments using clever cunning to find a hidden cache of tallow and spare gaskets.
nodes.page: Fine grey dust coats the deep maroon upholstery like powdered bone and muffles your boots as you step gingerly into the first-class saloon. Shattered crystal drops from the ceiling sconces crunch beneath your soles, glittering faintly in the pale light filtered through grime-caked windows. Beneath a collapsed side-table, a brass-bound tin box catches your eye, half-buried under water-stained velvet curtains and discarded timetables. You kneel in the choking gloom, prying at the swollen wooden lid with your bare fingers while checking the corridor behind you for falling debris.

exits.label: Lift the latch and inspect the interior

nodes.title: The Hidden Cache
nodes.brief: You search through luxury compartments using clever cunning to find a hidden cache of tallow and spare gaskets.
nodes.page: The brass latch yields with a sharp click, swinging open to reveal a neat tier of compartments lined with faded green baize. Inside lie several thick rolls of waxed tallow and a handful of pristine copper pipe gaskets, preserved from the damp air by layers of oily rag. These are proper engine-stores, dry and serviceable, salvaged from an era when carriages carried more than ghosts and rust. You gather the precious supplies into your canvas apron, tying off the corners securely against the rising draft that whistles through the splintered window frame.

exits.label: Return to the rusted siding junction

nodes.title: Picking the Seam
nodes.brief: You search through luxury compartments using clever cunning to find a hidden cache of tallow and spare gaskets.
nodes.page: Iron luggage racks overhead groan under drifted ash, ready to drop a cascade of rusted debris onto your stooped shoulders as you reach deeper into the recessed wall panels. Your fingertips brush against a hidden spring-catch behind the velvet trim, but the mechanism is jammed solid with decades of compacted soot and dried grease. With the timber bulkhead creaking ominously in the wind, you must rely on nimble wits and delicate pressure to coax the recalcitrant latch without snapping the rusted linkage inside.

check.label: Probe the recessed latch with careful fingers

nodes.title: A Slip in the Dark
nodes.brief: You search through luxury compartments using clever cunning to find a hidden cache of tallow and spare gaskets.
nodes.page: The rusted pin snaps under your hurried pressure with a sharp, metallic ping that echoes hollowly down the empty corridor. A shower of sharp-edged wood splinters and cold ash cascades down from the luggage rack, biting deep into the exposed skin of your forearm and leaving a jagged, stinging scratch. You stumble backward against the mahogany partition, clutching your bleeding arm while the stubborn panel remains stubbornly locked shut against further inspection.

nodes.title: Spoils of the Saloon
nodes.brief: You search through luxury compartments using clever cunning to find a hidden cache of tallow and spare gaskets.
nodes.page: Your fingertips catch the stubborn brass spring just as it threatens to bind, easing the rusted tongue back with a smooth, silent slide that leaves the hidden compartment gaping wide. In the dark recess lies a small leather pouch filled with tallow cakes and several unblemished sealing washers, untouched by the creeping damp of the steppes. You slip the prize into your coat pocket, your fingers brushing against the cool, oily leather of your new acquisition.

exits.label: Return to the main line inspection point

nodes.title: The Stubborn Link
nodes.brief: You repair a jammed vestibule coupling using solid mechanics to free an old cargo truck loaded with dry briquettes.
nodes.page: A cargo truck sits marooned between two listing timber wagons, coupling locked solid by years of rust and grit. On your knees in the grey ballast, you wedge a pinch-bar into the iron jaw of the draw-gear and test the strain with your shoulder. The thick metal pins refuse to budge, locked tight by an ancient strain that demands more than raw muscle to overcome. You tap the housing smartly with a brass-faced hammer, listening to the dull thud of solid iron ringing through the dead air.

exits.label: Apply leverage to the frozen draw-bar

nodes.title: Briquettes in the Dust
nodes.brief: You repair a jammed vestibule coupling using solid mechanics to free an old cargo truck loaded with dry briquettes.
nodes.page: The coupling pin rises with a reluctant groan of strained metal, freeing the old freight wagon to roll a few inches down the sloping grade before settling against the brake shoes. You haul back the rusted side-flap, releasing a cloud of fine coal dust as the heavy wooden wall drops open to reveal neat stacks of compressed peat briquettes. They are dry and dense, smelling faintly of ancient bog-moss and resin, ready to feed the ravenous firebox of the Marrowbone when the steam pressure begins to drop.

exits.label: Haul the fuel crates toward the tender

nodes.title: The Frozen Pin
nodes.brief: You repair a jammed vestibule coupling using solid mechanics to free an old cargo truck loaded with dry briquettes.
nodes.page: The wedge-pin of the vestibule coupling is welded together by decades of rust and expansion, resisting every ounce of force you put into the brass-faced mallet. You brace your boots against the rotting wooden buffer-beam, heaving upward with both hands while driving the heavy drift-punch squarely into the seized pivot hole. The metal screeches in protest, sending hot vibrations up your forearms as the rusted collar threatens to shear off entirely inside the sleeve.

check.label: Drive the seized coupling pin home

nodes.title: Hammer and Rust
nodes.brief: You repair a jammed vestibule coupling using solid mechanics to free an old cargo truck loaded with dry briquettes.
nodes.page: The drift-punch slips sideways on the slick, greasy metal surface, catching your knuckles a glancing blow against the jagged iron edge of the brake-standard. A dull, throbbing ache flares through your hand as skin splits against the cold steel, leaving a dark bruise that blooms beneath the soot. You drop the hammer with a curse and shake your throbbing fingers while the jammed coupling stays as fixed as the bedrock beneath the track.

exits.label: Pick up your tools and limp away

nodes.title: Cleared Metal
nodes.brief: You repair a jammed vestibule coupling using solid mechanics to free an old cargo truck loaded with dry briquettes.
nodes.page: Your hammer blow lands square and true, driving the rusted wedge-pin cleanly through the housing with a satisfying crack of fracturing scale. The jammed iron jaws fall apart into your waiting palm, releasing the trapped cargo truck and leaving the pathway clear for you to haul the fuel supplies back toward the depot. You wipe the sweat from your forehead with a soot-stained sleeve, carrying your prize away from the rusting iron skeletons.

exits.label: Return to the central depot siding

nodes.title: Shadows in the Siding
nodes.brief: You outmaneuver scavengers hiding in the dark using sharp cunning, discovering a heavy leather pouch of grease-pencils.
nodes.page:
Shadows stretch long across the ballasted gravel as you skirt the perimeter of the dormant coal stage. Beneath the skeletal frame of an upturned water crane, grease-slick footprints leave a faint, dark trail in the grey dust. Someone has been rifling through the abandoned oil lockers, hunting for anything that burns or trades.

Keeping low against the rusted flank of a ballast wagon, you weigh your options and step cautiously toward the narrow gap between the bogies.

exits.label: Slip past the dark coal stage

nodes.title: The Oil Locker
nodes.brief: You outmaneuver scavengers hiding in the dark using sharp cunning, discovering a heavy leather pouch of grease-pencils.
nodes.page:
Footsteps echo softly against iron sheeting ahead, rhythmic and cautious, matching your own pace through the labyrinth of dead rolling stock. A sliver of lantern light flickers from the ventilation slit of an unlatched stores van, catching the amber glint of spilled tallow on the sleepers. Whoever is hiding inside is listening just as intently for the rattle of your regulator key.

You test the heavy iron latch with a gloved thumb, finding it unsealed and waiting for a shove.

nodes.title: Scavengers in the Dark
nodes.brief: You outmaneuver scavengers hiding in the dark using sharp cunning, discovering a heavy leather pouch of grease-pencils.
nodes.page:
