nodes.page: Muscles strain against the unyielding metal as you wedge your boot-heel into the mounting bracket and pull back with every ounce of power in your shoulders and spine. The seized valve refuses to budge, holding fast while the pressure needle in the cab ticks dangerously toward the red line of warning. You lean harder into the lever, your breath hissing through clenched teeth as the frame of the Marrowbone shudders in response to your desperate, straining effort.

nodes.title: Strained Muscle and Steam
nodes.brief: Wrestling a stuck intake valve clear of sulfur crust prevents a blockage, earning a sealed flask of clean distilled boiler water.
nodes.page: The wrench slips with a sharp metallic shriek that sets your teeth on edge, sending you stumbling backward against the hot boiler casing. A searing scrape burns across your knuckles, leaving a dark red line that beads quickly through the grey soot on your skin. You catch your breath against the pain, pressing your bleeding hand into your trousers as the engine settles back into its steady, exhausted rhythm. Valuable minutes have slipped away into the empty waste, and your knuckles throb with a dull, persistent ache that will stay with you long after the journey ends.

exits.label: Tend your raw knuckles and press on

nodes.title: The Pure Reserve
nodes.brief: Wrestling a stuck intake valve clear of sulfur crust prevents a blockage, earning a sealed flask of clean distilled boiler water.
nodes.page: With a sharp, cracking snap, the yellow crust shatters away from the housing, leaving the intake spinning freely under your grip just as the danger passes, however narrowly. A hidden latch within the housing clicks open, releasing a small, leather-strapped flask of clear distilled water that has been sealed against the sulfur fumes since the old days. You lift the cool metal container away, pocketing it alongside your tools as a precious shield against the dry ash of the steppes.

exits.label: Return to the steaming sulfur sinks

nodes.title: Sinking Ballast
nodes.brief: Shoveling heavy gravel ballast to shore up a sinking rail bed secures a rusted iron wedge for tightening tender couplings.
nodes.page:
The steel rails tilt ominously toward a patch of soft grey silt where the track-bed has dissolved into fine, shifting ash. You drop from the cab with an iron shovel in your grip, wading into the loose grey dust to dig deep beneath the sleepers before the locomotive drags its wheels off the iron line entirely. You haul stones and slag from the tender and pack them back into the trench by hand.

The work goes on without end, each shovel-load vanishing into the grey void until you wedge a solid length of rusted iron firmly beneath the tilting rail-joint.

nodes.title: Shoveling the Sinking Grey
nodes.brief: Shoveling heavy gravel ballast to shore up a sinking rail bed secures a rusted iron wedge for tightening tender couplings.
nodes.page: You shovel iron plate and broken stone into the slurry beneath the ties, driving the blade down in frantic urgency as the engine tilts further toward the sulfur pool. The ground shifts treacherously under your boots, threatening to slide away and drag you down into the warm, bubbling mire. You brace your legs wide against the sliding ash, heaving a massive block of basalt into place to shore up the rail before the whole embankment gives way beneath the heavy locomotive.

nodes.title: The Slumping Embankment
nodes.brief: Shoveling heavy gravel ballast to shore up a sinking rail bed secures a rusted iron wedge for tightening tender couplings.
nodes.page: The shifting grey earth gives way entirely beneath your right boot, plunging your leg knee-deep into the warm, sulfurous sludge before you can catch yourself. You haul yourself out with a breathless heave, leaving your boot stuck deep in the mire and your shin scraped raw against jagged ballast stone. The engine sits crooked now, canted heavily to one side on the uneven track, costing you precious time and leaving a dull, throbbing ache in your bruised limb as you limp back to the deck.

exits.label: Climb back onto the tilting deck

nodes.title: The Iron Wedge
nodes.brief: Shoveling heavy gravel ballast to shore up a sinking rail bed secures a rusted iron wedge for tightening tender couplings.
nodes.page: Your frantic shoveling wedges the basalt blocks into the mud just in time, bracing the track against the Marrowbone. Deep in the ballast bed, your boot strikes something solid and metallic, buried beneath decades of cinders and old ballast. You pull free a heavy, rusted iron wedge, perfectly shaped for tightening loose tender couplings when the vibrations start shaking the coal car apart.

exits.label: Return to the steaming sulfur sinks

nodes.title: The Vapour Peddler
nodes.brief: Outwitting a scavenging trader hiding among the vapours lets you acquire a pouch of sweet-smelling tallow for the valve gear.
nodes.page:
A hooded figure crouches behind a rusted coal hopper half-buried in the ash dunes, watching your approach with dark, calculating eyes. Empty glass bottles dangle from their belt, clinking softly against one another like dry bones in the wind. You slow your pace, keeping your hands in plain sight while trading slow, measured nods with the scavenger who knows every trick of the low wastes.

They reach into their ragged coat and produce a small, greasy leather pouch tied with sinew, muttering about the high cost of grease in a world made entirely of dry bone and burnt wood.

nodes.title: The Hollow Bargain
nodes.brief: Outwitting a scavenging trader hiding among the vapours lets you acquire a pouch of sweet-smelling tallow for the valve gear.
nodes.page:
Yellow vapors swirl around the base of the abandoned hopper car, blurring the scavenger's silhouette into a shifting grey phantom against the dunes. You offer a handful of heavy iron washers from your kit, holding them out flat on your palm so the metal catches the pale, brassy glare of the low sun. The peddler tests the weight of the iron with a grey fingernail, nodding slowly as they slide the pouch across the rusted rail toward your boots.

It smells faintly of rendered mutton and sweet resin, exactly what the groaning valve gear needs if you are to stop the shrieking metal from seizing up in the dry heat.

nodes.title: Outwitting the Salt-Ghost
nodes.brief: Outwitting a scavenging trader hiding among the vapours lets you acquire a pouch of sweet-smelling tallow for the valve gear.
nodes.page: You tap the side of the brass oil-can against the rail, feigning a sudden, urgent interest in the pressure gauges back on the locomotive to trick the cautious trader into showing their hand. The scavenger hesitates, half-stepping back into the yellow fog before realizing your ruse, their narrow eyes narrowing further in silent estimation of your wits. You step closer before they can retreat into the dunes, cutting off their escape route along the abandoned string of carriages.

nodes.title: The Slippery Trade
nodes.brief: Outwitting a scavenging trader hiding among the vapours lets you acquire a pouch of sweet-smelling tallow for the valve gear.
nodes.page: The scavenger slips through the dense sulfur vapors like smoke between your fingers, vanishing into the maze of abandoned carriages before you can close your hand around the pouch. You find only a greasy rag left behind in the dirt, smelling faintly of rendered fat and old regret. The loss costs you valuable time in the gathering gloom, leaving you empty-handed and listening to the mournful whistle of the wind through the skeleton trains.

exits.label: Return empty handed to the engine

nodes.title: Tallow in the Dark
nodes.brief: Outwitting a scavenging trader hiding among the vapours lets you acquire a pouch of sweet-smelling tallow for the valve gear.
nodes.page: Shadows stretch long across the rusted ballast as you secure the small canvas sack from where it slipped behind the bulkhead, feeling its dense, fatty weight against your palm. The prize is yours: a generous lump of sweet-smelling animal tallow, thick and yellow, suited for greasing the stubborn valve gear when the heat climbs. Beneath the grease-stained wrapping, a scrap of paper scrawled by an old track-walker marks where the sub-bed of the line runs dry and brittle near the salt-pans, whispering of how a handful of sulphur-soaked rags and a stray spark could turn miles of iron ties into a roaring wall of fire.

exits.label: Follow the steaming track toward the Sulphur Sinks

nodes.title: Hissing in the Cinder
nodes.brief: Mapping the subterranean sulfur vents by their rhythmic hissing grants a shortcut token through the hazardous steam-marshes.
nodes.page:
Sulfur vapors rise from the crust of the earth in rhythmic pulses, matching the steady thrum of the engine beneath your boots. Every hiss from the yellow vents tells a story of underground pressure and shifting heat, mapping a perilous corridor through the steaming marshes where a careless wheel will bog down in grey mire. You trace the cadence with the edge of your boot and note how the vents blow clear in three-beat intervals. That window is your footing across the scalded flats.

Mineral damp coats your throat in dust as you guide the frame forward, keeping close to the steaming bank where the ground holds firm under the iron.

exits.label: Pick a path between the steaming vents

nodes.title: Steam-Marshes and Smoke
nodes.brief: Mapping the subterranean sulfur vents by their rhythmic hissing grants a shortcut token through the hazardous steam-marshes.
nodes.page:
Low clouds of grey steam drift across the tracks, obscuring the rusted skeleton of a derailed coal hopper that lists sharply toward the bog. The rhythmic hissing of the vents guides your eyes through the white haze, revealing patches of firm basalt ballast amid the treacherous quagmire of sulfur-mud. The regulator stays notched just so as you nurse a head of steam, and the firebox roars behind you with a dry, hungry appetite.

Every yard gained through the mist feels earned, measured in the steady drop of the water gauge and the comforting rattle of copper pipes in the cab.

exits.label: Advance deeper into the sulfuric haze

nodes.title: Reading the Sulfur Vents
nodes.brief: Mapping the subterranean sulfur vents by their rhythmic hissing grants a shortcut token through the hazardous steam-marshes.
nodes.page: The ground ahead shimmers beneath a dense blanket of yellow vapor, hiding the treacherous chasms where boiling mud meets the iron rails. You lean out from the narrow cab doorway, squinting against the acrid sting in your eyes to match the rhythmic gasps of the earth with the pulsing tremor of the boiler plates. A miscalculation here will sink the driving wheels into a scalding mire from which no engine can haul itself back alone. You gather your focus, weighing the steam pressure against the shifting echoes of the vents to find the hidden stone bridge beneath the drift.

check.label: Read the vent rhythms to cross safely

nodes.title: Mires of the Steppe
nodes.brief: Mapping the subterranean sulfur vents by their rhythmic hissing grants a shortcut token through the hazardous steam-marshes.
nodes.page: A sudden shift in the underground pressure catches you off guard, sending a dense plume of scalding vapor directly into the cab window and blinding you to the alignment of the rails. The engine's forward wheels lurch sickeningly sideways and sink deep into a hidden pocket of boiling sulfur-mud with a blunt thud. You scramble to reverse the gear and shovel frantic loads of dry sand beneath the slipping treads, coughing bitterly as the grey dust coats your tongue. At last the machine comes free, though your left shoulder is bruised against the iron bulkhead and the tender runs short on precious water.

exits.label: Pull the groaning engine back onto solid ballast

nodes.title: The Vent-Master's Token
nodes.brief: Mapping the subterranean sulfur vents by their rhythmic hissing grants a shortcut token through the hazardous steam-marshes.
nodes.page: Steam swirls lazily around the running board as the engine steadies itself upon solid stone, leaving the worst of the bubbling quagmire behind. You emerge with a small forged tin token bearing the notched stamp of the old track-finders, pressed into your hand by a silent figure fading back into the grey mist. It is a simple piece of stamped tin, yet it carries the unspoken weight of safe passage through the lower marshlands, recognized by every signalman and ganger who still honors the old road.

exits.label: Return to the main line near the Sulphur Sinks

nodes.title: The Grey Wall Rolls In
nodes.brief: The storm clock on the backhead ticks louder as a wall of grey ash-dust rolls across the steppe, blotting out the distant horizon.
nodes.page:
High above the jagged horizon, the storm clock's brass face clicks with a sharp, metallic finality that carries across the silent steppe. A towering wall of grey ash-dust, miles wide and dark as a winter twilight, swallows the distant telegraph poles one by one as it sweeps down upon the track. You slam the cab doors shut against the rising gale; the locomotive's iron frame trembles as the first dry particles strike the boiler jacket like handfuls of buckshot. The world shrinks to the circle of light cast by the flickering headlamp and the red glow of the open firebox door.

There is no turning back now, nor any shelter to be found across the open flats; you must drive straight into the heart of the grey haze before the storm seals the cutting for good.

exits.label: Drive straight into the oncoming ash-storm

nodes.title: The Ribcage of Iron
nodes.brief: The Ribcage: Ribs of collapsed iron rolling stock form a twisted tunnel where the wind howls like a lost express train.
nodes.page:
Twisted ribs of collapsed rolling stock loom out of the swirling ash like the skeleton of some ancient leviathan, forming a sheltered tunnel where the wind shrieks through rusted gaps with the voice of a lost express. The air inside smells of old grease and dry soot, undisturbed for years save for the drifting grey silt that carpets the buckled floorboards. Shadows stretch long and strange beneath the iron arches, and every choice forward offers a different gamble against the rising storm and the failing light.

You can inspect the tangled wreckage for salvage, venture into the deeper shadows where the wind howls loudest, or keep the fire hot and push onward through the howling dark.

exits.label: Pick a path deeper through the rusted iron ribs
Rewire the dead telegraph pole inside the wreck
Patch the blown steam line with asbestos tape
Drop the canvas cab curtains against the grit

nodes.title: Shadows in the Skeleton
nodes.brief: Bracing a sagging iron beam with your shoulder keeps the tunnel from collapsing, earning a sturdy brass grease-gun.
nodes.page:
Iron beams overhead groan under drifted ash, and they shift a little with every gust that sweeps across the skeletal remains of the carriage. You wedge your shoulder beneath a sagging cross-brace, throwing your weight against the cold metal to keep the buckling roof from crashing down onto the tender's coal-bunk. The strain makes your muscles burn, but the gap holds long enough for you to scramble clear into the darker reaches of the wreck.

Among the splintered wood and twisted brackets, something small and sturdy catches the amber gleam of your lantern, half-buried in dry soot.

exits.label: Reach into the gloom for the hidden tool

nodes.title: Bracing the Falling Iron
nodes.brief: Bracing a sagging iron beam with your shoulder keeps the tunnel from collapsing, earning a sturdy brass grease-gun.
nodes.page: The rusted roof-beam slips another half-inch with a sharp shriek of stressed metal, threatening to bring the entire side of the collapsed carriage down across the running board. You brace your boots firmly against the uneven ballast, thrusting your shoulder upward into the angle of the joint to bear the crushing weight before the whole structure folds. The iron bites hard through your coat, demanding every ounce of strength you possess to keep the passage clear for the engine. You must hold the line against the falling steel or risk pinning the locomotive beneath a ton of jagged scrap.

check.label: Brace the sagging beam with your shoulder

nodes.title: Crushed Iron and Bent Metal
nodes.brief: Bracing a sagging iron beam with your shoulder keeps the tunnel from collapsing, earning a sturdy brass grease-gun.
nodes.page: The rusted cross-beam gives way with a deafening screech, slamming downward and catching your shoulder a glancing blow that sends you sprawling hard into the grit. Dust and dry flakes of paint fill the air, blinding you as you scramble back from the debris with a torn coat and a dull, throbbing ache in your arm. The wreckage settles into a permanent, crooked hunch, blocking the direct path and forcing you to claw your way out through a narrow gap in the rusted siding. You survive the collapse, but the delay costs precious minutes against the storm clock and leaves you nursing a deep, bruised stiffness.

exits.label: Crawl clear of the fallen wreckage

nodes.title: The Grease-Gun's Weight
nodes.brief: Bracing a sagging iron beam with your shoulder keeps the tunnel from collapsing, earning a sturdy brass grease-gun.
nodes.page: The heavy iron beam settles only a fraction before locking solid against a stout steel stanchion, leaving a narrow, safe archway through which you tumble safely into the dim interior. Clutched in the dust near your boot is a sturdy brass grease-gun, its lever smooth and its reservoir still half-full of clean, golden lubricant. The tool is yours now, a solid piece of gear salvaged from the old maintenance trains that will keep the driving rods sliding smooth when the sand gets into the bearings.

exits.label: Return to the Ribcage and weigh your next move

nodes.title: The Silent Wire
nodes.brief: Rewiring a dead telegraph pole inside the wreck restores a faint clicking signal that reveals a clear block ahead.
nodes.page:
Copper threads hang like dead serpents from the cross-arms of the telegraph pole, grey with generations of soot. Inside the rib-cage of the wrecked carriage, you strip back the brittle gutta-percha insulation with your pocket-knife, twisting the live ends together until a faint, rhythmic clicking begins to stutter through the tin receiver. The instrument remembers old messages from Ashgate and taps out confirmation that the line ahead is clear of derailed bogies.

Shifting your grip on the iron casing, you listen to the mechanical pulse fade and return, mapping the open miles between the stalled hulks toward the deeper shadow of the valley.

nodes.title: Splicing the Circuit
nodes.brief: Rewiring a dead telegraph pole inside the wreck restores a faint clicking signal that reveals a clear block ahead.
nodes.page: Sparks spit from the frayed terminal box as you wedge your fingers into the cramped casing, trying to bridge the gap before the heavy iron roof-strut shifts its weight and crushes your knuckles against the timber sill. Sweat cuts clean channels through the soot on your forehead while the electrical surge hums low and angry through the copper strands, threatening to throw your hands back against the jagged bulkhead. You grit your teeth and press the stripped wire hard into the brass terminal block.

nodes.title: Scored by the Surge
nodes.brief: Rewiring a dead telegraph pole inside the wreck restores a faint clicking signal that reveals a clear block ahead.
nodes.page: A vicious blue arc leaps from the terminal box, burning a jagged red line across your forearm and shaking the iron rib-work of the carriage. You stumble backward into the choking dust, clutching your scorched skin while the telegraph instrument falls silent once more, leaving only the dull roar of the ash-wind outside. The delay eats precious minutes from the storm clock, and the stinging burn leaves a stiff, throbbing reminder of how easily the road breaks those who rush it.

exits.label: Crawl back to the running board

nodes.title: The Tapped Message
nodes.brief: Rewiring a dead telegraph pole inside the wreck restores a faint clicking signal that reveals a clear block ahead.
nodes.page: Your fingers hold the copper firm until the screw bites home, locking the connection against the vibration of the steppes and securing a steady, faultless pulse that tells you the block ahead is clear. The wire yields its secret, and a slim brass adjuster-key rests where some long-dead linesman dropped it years ago. It slips easily into your breast pocket, cold brass that hints at future access.

nodes.title: Sealing the Vent
nodes.brief: Patching a blown steam line with asbestos tape and copper wire secures a spare pressure gauge for the cab roof.
nodes.page: Steam hisses from the fractured pipe-joint like an angry adder, filling the dim service alcove with blinding white mist that smells of boiled grease and old scale. Wrapping layers of sticky asbestos tape around the weeping metal, you haul the copper wire tight with your pliers until the pulsing leaks choked into silence. The repaired line holds firm against the rising pressure, steadying the gauge needle as the engine thrums beneath your boots.

nodes.title: Assessing the Gauge
nodes.brief: Patching a blown steam line with asbestos tape and copper wire secures a spare pressure gauge for the cab roof.
nodes.page: Pale light filters through the grease-filmed glass of the side window, illuminating the spare pressure dial resting on a discarded parts rack inside the rusted tool locker. You lift the brass-rimmed instrument, wiping away a thick crust of grey ash to test the internal spring with a gentle prod of your thumb. It ticks with a clean, healthy resonance that promises reliable readings when the storm closes in over the lower cuttings.

nodes.title: Bracing the Hot Line
nodes.brief: Patching a blown steam line with asbestos tape and copper wire secures a spare pressure gauge for the cab roof.
nodes.page: Boiling water spits from the fracture as you struggle to slip the split-collar clamp over the vibrating pipe, your fingers slipping against the slick, superheated metal in the cramped gloom. The entire junction shudders violently with every stroke of the eccentric rod, threatening to blow the temporary patch wide open before the locking bolts can bite into the copper wall. You throw your weight against the wrench, muscles straining against the sudden rush of scalding steam.

nodes.title: Scalded and Spent
nodes.brief: Patching a blown steam line with asbestos tape and copper wire secures a spare pressure gauge for the cab roof.
nodes.page: A sudden surge of pressure blows the clamp askew, blasting a stinging cloud of hot mist across your knuckles and leaving a angry red scald that throbs with every beat of your heart. You jerk your hand back with a sharp intake of breath, watching the precious steam vent uselessly into the ballast while the engine coughs and loses a fraction of its forward momentum. The delay costs you dear in water and patience, adding another bitter weight to the journey.

exits.label: Wipe the steam from your eyes

nodes.title: The Quiet Siding
nodes.brief: Patching a blown steam line with asbestos tape and copper wire secures a spare pressure gauge for the cab roof.
nodes.page: Your wrench turns the final nut home, locking the copper sleeve tight and reducing the angry hiss to a faint, orderly whisper that satisfies the engine's iron heart. The repair holds, and tucked behind the old parts rack you uncover a forgotten switch-lever pointing toward an overgrown timber spur that leads away into the silent ash-dunes. It is a quiet, empty place where a man could simply drop his fire-shovel and let the roaring world pass him by.

nodes.title: Dropping the Canvas
nodes.brief: You drop canvas curtains over the cab windows as fine volcanic grit begins to scour the brasswork and choke the injector valves.
nodes.page: Outside the cab, the grey horizon dissolves into a howling wall of fine volcanic grit that scours the brass handrails with a high, abrasive whistle. You pull the canvas drop-curtains down along the cab frame and lash the hemp ties fast against the wind while the injector valves sputter and choke on the blowing ash. The engine stumbles in its stride, swallowing the foul air as you work the lubricator pumps by touch alone in the sudden, yellow-tinted gloom.

nodes.title: The Grey Bazaar
nodes.brief: The Grey Bazaar: A sprawling marketplace built inside stalled goods wagons where desperate merchants barter scraps for water and tallow.
nodes.page: Hollowed-out freight wagons form a crooked labyrinth of commerce amid the grey dunes, their iron ribs draped in oil-stained canvas and fluttering strips of parchment. Traders hawk lukewarm tallow and bitter well-water from repurposed tender tanks while soot-choked lanterns sway in the ash-laden wind. Music wheezes from a cracked accordion somewhere down the line, competing with the Marrowbone's idle knock on the parallel track. Every shadow in this sprawling marketplace hides a bargain or a blade, and the low roar of the approaching storm urges you toward whatever shelter or advantage you can snatch before the air turns solid with grit.

nodes.title: The Peddler's Dust
nodes.brief: Staring down a nervous peddler trying to sell fake boiler compound wins his respect and a bag of dry pit-coal.
nodes.page:
Grey canvas flaps slat against a rusted iron counter where a hump-backed peddler hawks grey bricks of supposed boiler compound. He taps a lumpy grey packet against his palm, swearing by the old track that it will clean any scaled-up firebox from Ashgate to the wall. You cross your arms on the brass sill of the Marrowbone and watch him through the blowing grit.

The man wilts under your soot-streaked stare, drops his voice from a greasy roar to a dry wheeze, then slides a genuine sack of dry pit-coal across the planks. You lean out to scoop the fuel up.

exits.label: Haul the pit-coal aboard the cab

nodes.title: Weighing the Grey Dust
nodes.brief: Staring down a nervous peddler trying to sell fake boiler compound wins his respect and a bag of dry pit-coal.
nodes.page: Dust devils flick grey ash against the cab windows while the peddler shuffles his remaining packets with nervous, soot-blackened fingers. He tries to palm a lighter, crumbly brick of common earth off as high-grade flux, watching your eyes for a flicker of doubt. You hold his gaze across the iron counter, breathing shallow through the wool rag tied over your mouth, keeping your face flat and your posture braced against the rolling deck. Every second drags like a rusted valve needing grease.

nodes.title: A Sour Bargain
nodes.brief: Staring down a nervous peddler trying to sell fake boiler compound wins his respect and a bag of dry pit-coal.
nodes.page: Your nerve wavers for a heartbeat, a sudden twitch of the eye letting the peddler see your doubt, and he seizes the moment to short-weight your sack with a smug grin. He pockets your copper token before you can hook a thumb into the twine, leaving you with a bag of half-crushed shale that will slag your grates instead of clearing them. The disappointment leaves a dry, coppery taste at the back of your throat. You haul the inferior sack up anyway, paying for the lapse with ruined draft and lost hours.

exits.label: Kick the engine back into gear

nodes.title: Respect in the Ash
nodes.brief: Staring down a nervous peddler trying to sell fake boiler compound wins his respect and a bag of dry pit-coal.
nodes.page: Steel meets bone as you hold your ground, your steady stare boring into the peddler until his watery eyes drop to the planks and he shuffles backward with a mutter. He recognizes your iron grip and shoves the full sack of dry pit-coal into your hands without another word of protest.

exits.label: Take the road to the ridge

nodes.title: Maps in the Smoke
nodes.brief: Trading a spare oil-can for information about washed-out culverts gains a hand-drawn parchment map of the lower rail.
nodes.page:
A greasy oil-can from the spare locker attracts a toothless scout leaning against a stalled coal tender. He traces crooked lines in the fine ash coating a buffer-beam, sketching out the washed-out culverts where the rails hang over hollow drops of grey mud. You listen closely to his gravelly warnings about shifting dunes and sunken sleepers.

The scout pockets the tin with a toothy grin and hands over a stiff square of yellowed parchment marked with red grease-crayon.

exits.label: Roll away from the stalled tender

nodes.title: The Scout's Riddle
nodes.brief: Trading a spare oil-can for information about washed-out culverts gains a hand-drawn parchment map of the lower rail.
nodes.page: Yellowed parchment crinkles in your gloved hand while the scout points a grease-blackened finger toward a maze of sunken rails half-buried in the dunes. He demands double oil for a secret route around the worst of the wash-outs, his eyes darting toward the horizon where the storm clouds thicken. You weigh his crooked map against your dwindling stores, trying to puzzle out if his marks are real track or just traps set to bleed a passing engine.

nodes.title: Misread Rails
nodes.brief: Trading a spare oil-can for information about washed-out culverts gains a hand-drawn parchment map of the lower rail.
nodes.page: The map leads you straight into a choked cutting where the ballast has washed away, leaving the rails sagging like dead snakes over a pit of wet silt. The Marrowbone dips alarmingly to the port side, groaning as mud slumps against the ash-pans and chokes the draft. You spend a grueling hour jacking the chassis clear with heavy timbers and cursing the scout's deceptive ink-lines.

exits.label: Clear the silt and press on

nodes.title: The Price of Grease
nodes.brief: Trading a spare oil-can for information about washed-out culverts gains a hand-drawn parchment map of the lower rail.
nodes.page: A dry trade across a greasy workbench leaves you poorer by one spare oil-can and richer by something far more stubborn: a hand-drawn parchment map of the lower rail, inked in squid-brown and stained with old tea. The vendor's squinting nod confirms that the washed-out culverts ahead are at least navigable if you keep the regulator light and your eyes on the ballast. You roll the parchment tight, tucking it inside your woolen waistcoat against the chill of the steppe wind.

exits.label: Take the parchment and push on toward the bazaar

nodes.title: The Crane's Teeth
nodes.brief: Repairing a broken hand-cranked crane for a grateful vendor earns a heavy steel pinch-bar for unseating jammed switches.
nodes.page:
Iron cables groan as you heave on the greasy wooden levers of an abandoned loading crane, coaxing its seized brass gears back into a slow, protesting rotation. A nearby vendor watches with wide eyes as the rusted arm swings clear of a jammed switch-point, freeing the track for the Marrowbone's passage. You wipe black grease from your forehead with a dirty sleeve while the vendor nods in silent gratitude.

A steel pinch-bar lands on the footplate as payment for the labor.

exits.label: Secure the pinch-bar on the rack

nodes.title: Clearing the Path
nodes.brief: Repairing a broken hand-cranked crane for a grateful vendor earns a heavy steel pinch-bar for unseating jammed switches.
nodes.page:
Steam hisses from a leaky union near your knee while you hammer a stubborn wedge back into its chair with sharp, rhythmic strokes. The surrounding rail-yard is quiet save for the wind whistling through empty cattle-trucks and the distant rattle of distant hoists. You pause to catch your breath, listening to the firebox keep the water hot with its familiar knock.

The track ahead is clear of debris, inviting you to heave the regulator open and roll forward.

nodes.title: The Gripping Gear
nodes.brief: Repairing a broken hand-cranked crane for a grateful vendor earns a heavy steel pinch-bar for unseating jammed switches.
nodes.page: Teeth screech against dry bronze inside the winch-box as you force the jammed hand-crank to turn against a mountain of rusted slag. The rusted pinions bind tight, threatening to snap the main shaft and spray red-hot iron shards across your knuckles. You brace your shoulder against the iron housing, throwing your weight into the crank while the metal screeches in protest.

nodes.title: The Slipped Gear
nodes.brief: Repairing a broken hand-cranked crane for a grateful vendor earns a heavy steel pinch-bar for unseating jammed switches.
nodes.page: The seized bronze tooth of the winch-box refuses your persuasion, snapping with a sound like a pistol shot and catching your knuckle a glancing, skin-splitting blow against the iron frame. Steam hisses from a nearby union in a mocking whistle as you suck the salt-blood from your thumb, staring at the ruin of the gear with dry resignation. Time slips through your fingers like dry ash while you bind the scrape with a dirty rag, leaving you short on minutes and carrying a fresh, throbbing ache that will remind you of the Cinder Steppe long after the engine reaches the water gate.

exits.label: Pocket the heavy steel pinch-bar and move forward

nodes.title: The Crane's Keepsake
nodes.brief: Repairing a broken hand-cranked crane for a grateful vendor earns a heavy steel pinch-bar for unseating jammed switches.
nodes.page: Iron grease smears your palms as the freed winch settles with a solid thud into its seating, the cable still intact. The vendor, a woman wrapped in soot-caked wool, spits into the dust and shoves a heavy tool into your grip, muttering that the Cinder Prophets are right when they say the fire teaches what steel forgets, and that when the Water Gate falls she intends to use the flood to wash away every ledger the Barons ever forged. You slide the cold iron into your coat.

nodes.title: The Iron Sledge
nodes.brief: Hauling crates of rusted scrap metal for a market boss secures an emergency voucher for fresh lubricating grease.
nodes.page: Stacks of corrugated plate iron demand two strong shoulders and a steady footing across the warped floorboards of the boxcar. Dust gets behind your teeth, tasting of sulphur and ancient coal-smoke while the market boss watches from a dry-box with narrowed eyes, weighing your pace against the sun's slow dip toward the ash-dunes. You heave the final crate onto the pallet, wiping sweat with a sleeve already stiffened by brine and soot. The boss tosses a greasy paper slip onto the counter, grunting that it will keep your pistons from screaming until the next siding.

nodes.title: Heaving the Dead Weight
nodes.brief: Hauling crates of rusted scrap metal for a market boss secures an emergency voucher for fresh lubricating grease.
nodes.page: Staggering under the shift of an iron-strapped crate that threatens to burst its wooden seams upon the rusted coupling-pin, you drop your center and lock your knees against the rolling sway of the stagnant train. The rusted metal groans like an old hinge, its dead weight threatening to pin your forearm against the iron sill unless your muscles hold the line against the slide. Every sinew in your neck knots tight as the corner tilts another fraction of an inch toward the gravel.

nodes.title: The Slipped Iron
nodes.brief: Hauling crates of rusted scrap metal for a market boss secures an emergency voucher for fresh lubricating grease.
nodes.page: Pain flares hot across your knuckles as the crate slips its binding and slams into the floorboards, scraping a deep, raw purple bruise across your wrist. You hiss through your teeth, swallowing the curse before the market boss notices the dented corner and docked tally. Time slips away while you wrestle the spilled scrap back into order under the low, merciless sky, leaving your ribs aching and your breath tasting of dry grey dust long after the work is done.

nodes.title: Grease and Gratitude
nodes.brief: Hauling crates of rusted scrap metal for a market boss secures an emergency voucher for fresh lubricating grease.
nodes.page: Fingers stiff and aching from the dead-lift, you pocket the small grease-voucher with a slow nod to the sullen clerk. The slip of paper is gray with thumb-prints and smells faintly of rendered mutton fat, but it represents twenty miles of quiet bearings and cool journals when the Marrowbone starts screaming for oil in the deep cuttings. You fold it into your waistcoat pocket alongside the stub of a tallow candle.

nodes.title: The Collector's Coat
nodes.brief: Spotting a disguised Rail Baron tax collector slipping through the stalls lets you lift a sealed transit permit from his coat.
nodes.page: Velvet lapels look entirely out of place amidst the rusted ribs of the freight wagons, worn by a man whose boots are far too clean for the Cinder Steppe. He slips between two timber-cars with a ledger tucked tight against his ribs, pausing only to check a brass pocket-watch that ticks with infuriating precision. You step into his shadow with practiced lightness, your fingers brushing the stiff wool of his outer pocket where a corner of heavy cream paper catches the dim, sulphurous light.

nodes.title: Lifting the Permit
nodes.brief: Spotting a disguised Rail Baron tax collector slipping through the stalls lets you lift a sealed transit permit from his coat.
nodes.page: Slender fingers brush the stiff wool of the hidden pocket while the tax man turns to bargain with a merchant over the price of salt-beef. Your pulse knocks against your ribs as you slip the corner of the cream paper between your knuckles, waiting for the marketplace noise to swell and cover the small rasp of fabric. The slightest twitch of his elbow will bring his signet ring down upon your wrist.

nodes.title: Caught in the Cuffs
nodes.brief: Spotting a disguised Rail Baron tax collector slipping through the stalls lets you lift a sealed transit permit from his coat.
nodes.page: Brass buttons scrape against your knuckles as the collector whips around with a sharp, bird-like cry, catching your wrist in a grip surprisingly hard for a man who lives behind ink-pots. You wrench your arm free with a harsh twist of your shoulder, leaving a scrap of your shirt sleeve caught in his brass cuff-link while he shouts for the station-watch. You scramble over a coupling-chain and into the maze of rusted boxcars, your lungs burning with cold ash as footsteps clatter on iron behind you.

nodes.title: The Stolen Seal
nodes.brief: Spotting a disguised Rail Baron tax collector slipping through the stalls lets you lift a sealed transit permit from his coat.
nodes.page: Cream paper rests in your palm, smelling faintly of imported ink and vinegar, clear of the man's sharp gold-nibbed pen. The red wax seal bears the double-eagle stamp of the Rail Barons, granting unhindered passage through every checkpoint between here and the Cinderfall Water Gate. You tuck the folded document deep inside your greasy jacket next to the brass valve-key, feeling the quiet weight of official immunity against your ribs.

nodes.title: The Ash-Mound Strike
nodes.brief: The engine shudders violently as the front bogie strikes a mound of hardened ash, threatening to lift the drive wheels off the rails.
nodes.page: Iron plates shriek in protest as the Marrowbone's front bogie strikes a high drift of hardened ash left by the burning of the lower yards. The engine rears upward like a startled beast, steam coughing white and hot from the cylinder cocks as the drive wheels lose their grip and spin screaming against the polished railheads. For a terrifying heartbeat the world tilts toward the embankment. The boiler wants to lift clean off its pins and pitch the coal-tender into the ditch. You throw your weight onto the regulator arm while the whole frame shudders from kelson to smokebox.

nodes.title: Prophet's Cairn
nodes.brief: Prophet's Cairn: A towering pyre of charred railway sleepers where Cinder Prophets chant hymns to the purifying flame of the Steppe.
nodes.page:
Charred railway sleepers stack high into a brooding spire of soot and ash, casting long, wavering shadows across the grey dunes. Cinder Prophets sway within the blistering heat, their robes stiff with salt and grease as they chant hymns to the purifying flame that devoured the Steppe. You pause near the edge of the pyre, feeling the dry wind whistle through the iron ribs of stalled tenders. Every path out of this smoky labyrinth demands a choice, whether you seek counsel among the zealots or haul obstacles from the track.

Smoke stings your eyes while the storm clock ticks away precious minutes in your breast pocket. To the left, a narrow path winds directly toward the heart of the chanting monks where the heat beats like a hammer. Straight ahead, iron censers swing from rusted gantries, marking a route through the sputtering shrines. You might also consult a blind prophet for the secrets of the iron gates, heave an iron fire-basket clear of the cowcatcher, clear a collapsed timber crossbeam for the wandering monks, or swing your water-scoop into a shallow tank-car to cool the boiling engine.

exits.label: Pick a path past the smoking censers
Scoop grey water from a tank-car

nodes.title: Heat of the Pyre
nodes.brief: Enduring the blistering heat of the prayer-fire without flinching wins the zealots trust and a heavy tin of fire-clay.
nodes.page: Waves of searing air ripple across your skin as you step closer to the towering cairn of charred sleepers. Cinder Prophets chant in low, rattling cadences, ignoring the blistering embers that drift down like black snow. Your boots crackle upon crusts of saltpetre while you steady your breathing against the suffocating sulphur fumes. The zealots watch you with unblinking, ash-dusted eyes, testing your resolve with every breath you draw in the furnace-wind. You must step forward now into the shimmering haze before the oppressive heat overcomes your senses entirely.

exits.label: Step closer to the blazing shrine

nodes.title: Trial by Cinder
nodes.brief: Enduring the blistering heat of the prayer-fire without flinching wins the zealots trust and a heavy tin of fire-clay.
nodes.page: Blistering air wraps around your throat like a hot iron collar, threatening to force a cough from your lungs and break your stance before the pyre. Sweat carves clean channels through the soot on your cheeks while the Cinder Prophets inch closer, their rhythmic chanting swelling into a steady, deafening roar. You lock your jaw against the searing gale, forcing your muscles to remain rigidly still despite the agony crawling across your skin. Every instinct screams at you to step back and shield your face from the blinding white glare of the core.

check.label: Endure the furnace heat without flinching

nodes.title: Scorch and Scour
nodes.brief: Enduring the blistering heat of the prayer-fire without flinching wins the zealots trust and a heavy tin of fire-clay.
nodes.page: Lungs burning and skin blistering, you stumble backward from the searing core with a harsh gasp that fills your mouth with dry ash. The Cinder Prophets murmur low condolences, their voices sounding like grinding stones as they watch you clutch your reddened forearms. You lose precious minutes scraping soothing mud from a cracked cistern just to cool the angry burns. The ordeal leaves a raw, pink scar across your wrist and a bitter taste of defeat, yet the Marrowbone still waits on the trembling rails nearby.

nodes.title: The Sealer's Tin
nodes.brief: Enduring the blistering heat of the prayer-fire without flinching wins the zealots trust and a heavy tin of fire-clay.
nodes.page: You stand against the roaring wall of heat until the Cinder Prophets grant you their grudging respect. One elder steps forward through the swirling smoke and presses a heavy, grease-sealed tin of fire-clay into your blistered palm. The grey compound inside smells of crushed slate and boiled fat, perfect for patching a leaking boiler seam when the pressure mounts. You stow the tin in your locker and turn back toward the waiting engine.

nodes.title: Smoke and Iron
nodes.brief: Adjusting the smoking iron censers to keep the holy fire burning earns a consecrated brass tallow-dipper for the cylinders.
nodes.page: Rusted iron censers hang from crooked chains above the line, sputtering green-tinged flames that smell of burning pitch and old railway ties. You reach out with a leather-gloved hand to steady a swinging vessel before its searing rim strikes the side of a stalled coal tender. Ash flakes drift thickly through the air, settling upon your cap and shoulders like a shroud of fine grey dust. The mechanism of the hanging burner groans in protest, rusted joints binding together under layers of accumulated soot. You need to adjust the flow before the entire apparatus jams fast.

nodes.title: The Censer Chain
nodes.brief: Adjusting the smoking iron censers to keep the holy fire burning earns a consecrated brass tallow-dipper for the cylinders.
nodes.page: Heavy links clink against one another as you guide the smoking iron censer back into its proper alignment above the track. Sulphur smoke swirls around your wrists, stinging minor cuts and coating your skin in a greasy film of black soot. The ground beneath your boots vibrates with the distant, ghostly pulse of an oncoming train that never quite arrives. You wipe your brow with a soiled sleeve, leaving a dark smudge across your forehead while the air grows heavier still. A final adjustment remains before the mechanism runs true.

nodes.title: Tallow and Grit
nodes.brief: Adjusting the smoking iron censers to keep the holy fire burning earns a consecrated brass tallow-dipper for the cylinders.
nodes.page: Grime grinds into the brass joints of the smoking censer as you force the jammed regulating screw with a worn spanner. The metal screeches sharply against the heat, threatening to snap the internal pin and spill burning pitch across your boots. You press on, feeling the tiny teeth of the gear slip and catch within the blackened housing. A single miscalculation will strip the thread entirely and freeze the apparatus solid in a cloud of choking smoke.

nodes.title: A Frozen Valve
nodes.brief: Adjusting the smoking iron censers to keep the holy fire burning earns a consecrated brass tallow-dipper for the cylinders.
nodes.page: Metal screams in protest and the regulating screw shears clean off, showering your boots with sharp iron splinters and hot soot. You jerk your hands back too late, a jagged burr slicing open your thumb to leave a slow-beading crimson line across your knuckle. The censer lists dangerously to one side, spilling a foul-smelling stream of burning pitch onto the ballast below. You waste valuable time smothering the small grease fire with a handful of damp sand while your shoulders ache from the strain.

exits.label: Gather your tools and move on

nodes.title: The Tallow-Dipper
nodes.brief: Adjusting the smoking iron censers to keep the holy fire burning earns a consecrated brass tallow-dipper for the cylinders.
nodes.page: You turn the regulating screw until the iron linkage runs smooth and true, and free the smoking censer. A Cinder Prophet nods in silent approval from the shadow of a stalled carriage and hands you a heavy, consecrated brass tallow-dipper. The small instrument bears ritual scorch-marks along its handle, perfectly balanced for ladling thick cylinder grease into the Marrowbone's steaming chest. You slip the dipper into your breast pocket and make your way back toward the waiting engine.

nodes.title: Voices in the Smoke
nodes.brief: Listening to a blind prophet recite the schedule of the dead secures a whispered password for the iron gates ahead.
nodes.page:
Ash drifts across the blackened cinders like grey snow as a blind prophet chants the timetable of the dead from atop a stalled tender. Their cracked voice rises above the rhythmic hiss of the Marrowbone, reciting every train that never reached Cinderfall and every driver lost to the Long Fire. You listen closely to the cadence of the morbid litany, catching the whispered phrase buried between the names of forgotten locomotives. That murmured password hangs in the air, offering safe passage through the iron gates ahead if you dare use it.

Stepping back onto the iron deck, you weigh the value of the secret against the low rumble of the engine.

nodes.title: Words in the Ash
nodes.brief: Listening to a blind prophet recite the schedule of the dead secures a whispered password for the iron gates ahead.
nodes.page: Grey flakes settle upon your collar as the blind chanter rattles off the hours of the long-dead trains with terrifying precision. You listen closely to the rhythm of the lament, catching the cadence hidden beneath the soot-clogged verses. A low whisper brushes your ear like hot steam, offering the secret word needed to pass the iron gates without drawing the wrath of the watchmen. You commit the phrase to memory just as the chanter falls silent, turning a sightless face toward the distant smoke of the Steppe.

exits.label: Step past the chanter into the grey

nodes.title: Listening to Ghosts
nodes.brief: Listening to a blind prophet recite the schedule of the dead secures a whispered password for the iron gates ahead.
nodes.page: Cold sweat cuts through the soot on your brow as the blind chanter's rhythmic rattling threatens to draw unwanted attention from the patrolling zealots in the ash-dunes. You force your breathing to slow down, locking your gaze onto the rusted rails while your mind sifts the whispered syllables from the meaningless drone. Every muscle wants to bolt, but you plant your hands on the hot plating of the tender and strain to catch the full sequence before the patrol rounds the stalled carriage.

check.label: Hold your nerve against the noise

nodes.title: The Price of Panic
nodes.brief: Listening to a blind prophet recite the schedule of the dead secures a whispered password for the iron gates ahead.
nodes.page: Your nerve snaps under the endless chanting, and a sudden start knocks an iron lantern from the bracket with a sharp, echoing clang. Zealots emerge from the grey haze like shadows, demanding an immediate toll in stolen coal and precious water before they let you crawl away with your skin intact. You leave behind a full skin from your private reserve and a fair portion of your best fuel, watching them swallow the supplies into the ash. The delay costs you precious time against the storm clock, but you manage to scramble back onto the deck of the Marrowbone.

nodes.title: The Whispered Key
nodes.brief: Listening to a blind prophet recite the schedule of the dead secures a whispered password for the iron gates ahead.
nodes.page: Through focus and iron nerve, you hold your ground while the chanting swells and fades around you like wind through a broken tunnel. The final syllables settle cleanly into your mind, forming the precise combination required to slip past the locked barriers without raising an alarm. You nod once to the blind figure, receiving a faint, knowing tilt of the head in return as the reward for your patience.

nodes.title: Clearing the Track
nodes.brief: Lifting a heavy iron fire-basket out of the way of the cowcatcher secures a bundle of dry kindling-wood.
nodes.page: Twisted iron frames litter the permanent way ahead and block the Marrowbone's path with scrap left behind by the last derailed goods train. You climb down from the warm footplate into the ankle-deep ash, eyeing the bulk of a discarded fire-basket that rests directly against the cowcatcher. Tugging at the rusted metal, you shift the obstacle inch by inch until it rolls clear of the rails, revealing a buried cache of dry kindling-wood preserved beneath the debris.

nodes.title: Lifting the Iron
nodes.brief: Lifting a heavy iron fire-basket out of the way of the cowcatcher secures a bundle of dry kindling-wood.
nodes.page: Muscles strain against the dead weight of the iron fire-basket as you wedge a pinch-bar beneath its rim and lean your entire weight into the lift. The rusted iron resists with a groaning screech that vibrates up through your boots into your shins, threatening to slip and pin your fingers against the ballast. You dig your heels deeper into the grey soot, bracing your back to heave the obstruction completely clear of the track before the boiler pressure drops too low.

check.label: Heave the iron from the rails

nodes.title: Strain and Rust
nodes.brief: Lifting a heavy iron fire-basket out of the way of the cowcatcher secures a bundle of dry kindling-wood.
nodes.page: The heavy metal slips from your grip at the worst possible moment, crashing back down onto your boot and sending a white-hot spike of pain up your leg. You bite back a curse, dragging your bruised foot away from the debris and nursing a deep, angry purple bruise that will slow your steps for hours. The struggle costs you precious minutes and leaves your muscles trembling with exhaustion as you finally manage to kick the wreckage aside.

nodes.title: Fuel for the Fire
nodes.brief: Lifting a heavy iron fire-basket out of the way of the cowcatcher secures a bundle of dry kindling-wood.
nodes.page: With a mighty heave, you flip the heavy iron fire-basket off the permanent way and watch it tumble down the ash-dune into the grey waste. Beneath where it lay, a dry bundle of resinous pine sleepers emerges intact from the drift, untouched by the damp rot of the Steppe. You sling the good wood over your shoulder and carry it back to the tender, securing a welcome addition to your dwindling fuel reserve.

exits.label: Head back to the main track

nodes.title: Clearing the Altar
nodes.brief: Dragging a collapsed timber crossbeam away from the holy altar gains a debt of honour from the ragged wandering monks.
nodes.page: Ragged figures in soot-stained robes hover anxiously near a fallen timber crossbeam that blocks the approach to a makeshift shrine among the stalled carriages. Stepping forward, you grab the rough-hewn wood and begin to drag it away from the holy ground with slow, deliberate effort. The wandering monks murmur low blessings in the ash-choked air, watching your labour with grateful eyes as the blocked path opens once more to the open rail.

exits.label: Leave the monks to their prayers

nodes.title: The Debt of Ash
nodes.brief: Dragging a collapsed timber crossbeam away from the holy altar gains a debt of honour from the ragged wandering monks.
nodes.page: Dust swirls around your boots as you haul the second heavy timber clear of the altar, setting it neatly alongside the rusted chassis of an old passenger car. The robed elders step forward to touch your sleeve in silent gratitude, pressing a small, soot-stained token into your palm as an earnest of their future help. You pocket the token without a word, knowing that a debt of honour from the wandering folk of the Steppe might prove worth more than water before the journey ends.

nodes.title: Shifting the Beam
nodes.brief: Dragging a collapsed timber crossbeam away from the holy altar gains a debt of honour from the ragged wandering monks.
nodes.page: You wedge your shoulder against the water-swollen timber, throwing your weight forward to dislodge the heavy beam from where it pins the sanctuary's corner post. The wood groans and shifts sluggishly in the ash, threatening to slide back and trap your arm against the iron stays of the carriage framework. You grit your teeth, muscles burning as you push through the sudden pain of a wrenched shoulder to roll the timber completely out of the way.

check.label: Muscle the timber from the altar

nodes.title: A Wrenched Shoulder
nodes.brief: Dragging a collapsed timber crossbeam away from the holy altar gains a debt of honour from the ragged wandering monks.
nodes.page: The heavy beam rolls unexpectedly, catching your shoulder a glancing blow that drops you hard into the gritty ash and leaves your arm hanging limp and throbbing. The monks rush forward to help you up, murmuring apologies and binding the joint with a strip of oiled canvas while you struggle to catch your breath. The mishap costs you precious time and leaves you nursing a dull ache in your shoulder joint, but the altar is finally clear and the debt is sealed.

exits.label: Accept the debt and move on

nodes.title: A Debt of Ash
nodes.brief: Dragging a collapsed timber crossbeam away from the holy altar gains a debt of honour from the ragged wandering monks.
nodes.page:
Timbers groan beneath your boots as you heave the charred crossbeam clear of the holy altar and free the trapped wanderer. The ragged monks murmur low canticles into their cowls, their faces blackened by soot and devotion. They press a heavy brass medallion into your palm, promising that wherever their fires burn along the line, your engine shall find sanctuary.

You climb back onto the footplate of the Marrowbone, feeling the weight of the new debt settle into your bones as the low sky presses down upon the Steppe.

nodes.title: Drinking from the Siding
nodes.brief: You swing the water-scoop down into a shallow tank-car left on a siding, gulping precious grey liquid to cool the smoking firebox.
nodes.page: Scalding steam hisses from the leaking regulator as you swing the heavy iron water-scoop down into the belly of a shallow tank-car abandoned on the rusted siding. The liquid that splashes into the tender is thick and grey, smelling of sulphur and old rust, but the ravenous appetite of the boiler demands it. You watch the pressure gauge tick upward through a film of grime as the thirsty iron drinks its fill, cooling the glowing heart of the Marrowbone just enough to keep the cylinders from seizing. There is no time to waste before the rising ash-storm finds you here.

nodes.title: Siding Nine
nodes.brief: Siding Nine: A tangle of rusted sidings where abandoned carriages serve as a sprawling dormitory for displaced track maintenance gangs.
nodes.page: Rusted carriages lean at drunken angles across the choked tracks, their shattered windows stuffed with oily rags and greasy sacking to keep out the stinging wind. This sprawling dormitory shelters bands of displaced track maintenance gangers who squat over smoking braziers, watching you with weary, dust-rimmed eyes. The air smells of charred fat and cheap chicory. Every pathway between the sleeping cars offers a choice of desperate labor or quiet danger, and the low rumble of distant thunder warns that the storm clock is running down.

exits.label: Pick a path through the sleeping cars
Share an oil-rag with the gangers

nodes.title: The Jammed Point
nodes.brief: Realigning a jammed spring-switch with a cold chisel and hammer clears the track and earns a box of matches.
nodes.page: Iron filings grate against your knuckles as you drop to your knees beside the spring-switch, finding the mechanism choked solid with hard-baked ash and grit. A cold chisel from your belt rings sharp against the frozen metal, sending sparks dancing into the gloom like dying fireflies. Every hammer blow echoes off the rusted ribs of stalled carriages nearby, punctuated by the mournful whistle of the wind through the dunes. You drive the chisel deeper into the stubborn joint until the mechanism shudders and finally yields to your hand.

nodes.title: Clearing the Rails
nodes.brief: Realigning a jammed spring-switch with a cold chisel and hammer clears the track and earns a box of matches.
nodes.page: Sweating through your woollen shirt despite the biting chill, you lever the heavy steel tongue back into alignment with a groaning heave. A small wooden box rattles loose from beneath the sleepers, spilling dry matches into your palm with a dry wooden clatter. You pocket the matches quickly, knowing the value of a reliable flame in a world where wet coal and damp timber are the death of engines. The iron road stretches ahead once more, a grey ribbon cutting through the endless dunes of ash.

nodes.title: Testing the Point
nodes.brief: Realigning a jammed spring-switch with a cold chisel and hammer clears the track and earns a box of matches.
nodes.page: Every muscle strains as you drive the cold chisel into the rusted hinge of the stubborn spring-switch, tapping the iron with measured force while the heavy freight carriage above groans on its rotting bogies. The rusted tongue resists, wedged tight by decades of accumulated ash and frozen grease. You must time your final blow precisely with the settling of the track bed, or the iron will snap under the hammer.

nodes.title: A Shattered Chisel
nodes.brief: Realigning a jammed spring-switch with a cold chisel and hammer clears the track and earns a box of matches.
nodes.page: A sharp crack splits the air as the cold chisel snaps in two, sending a jagged piece of steel whistling past your ear to bury itself in the grey bank of an ash-dune. The spring-switch remains locked solid, and the sudden jolt sends a stinging pain shooting up your forearm while your knuckles scrape raw against the ballast. You stumble back, sucking at the torn skin as precious minutes slip away into the ash-choked wind. The Marrowbone waits, her boiler groaning under the strain of delay.

nodes.title: The Unlocked Way
nodes.brief: Realigning a jammed spring-switch with a cold chisel and hammer clears the track and earns a box of matches.
nodes.page: With a final, satisfying ring of steel against iron, the stubborn switch gives way and slides smoothly into its groove. You wipe the sweat from your forehead with a soot-stained sleeve, retrieving a small, grease-stained box of matches that was wedged beneath the rail base. It is a meager prize, but every dry match is a victory against the damp cold of the Steppe. You pocket the box and turn back to the idling engine.

nodes.title: The Broken Pump
nodes.brief: Fixing a broken water pump for the exhausted gangers secures two leather buckets of brackish cooling water.
nodes.page: A rhythmic squeak echoes across the silent siding where the gangers' rusted water pump stands abandoned, its leather seals cracked and dry as old parchment. Gloves come off, and you set to work with grease-gun and spanner, coaxing life back into the frozen plungers. After a tense struggle against stubborn brass fittings, dark brackish water begins to gurgle into the leather buckets you set beneath the spout. Minerals cloud it thick, but the Marrowbone will drink it without complaint.

exits.label: Carry the buckets to the tender

nodes.title: Pumping the Sump
nodes.brief: Fixing a broken water pump for the exhausted gangers secures two leather buckets of brackish cooling water.
nodes.page: Your fingers freeze against the wet brass of the pump handle as you throw your weight into the stroke, trying to draw moisture from the dead sump below. The leather plunger slips with a dry wheeze, refusing to catch the prime, while the rusty intake pipe groans under the suction. You have to balance the pressure perfectly or the entire casting will crack in the bitter air.

nodes.title: A Split Seam
nodes.brief: Fixing a broken water pump for the exhausted gangers secures two leather buckets of brackish cooling water.
nodes.page: A dull thud echoes through the pump housing as the water-starved brass casing splits down the side, spraying a fine mist of foul-smelling grease and rusty water across your face. You leap back with a curse, wiping the greasy filth from your eyes as the last hope of an easy fill drains away into the ash. The lost time weighs heavier than any physical blow, and your shoulders ache with the cold.

nodes.title: The Brackish Haul
nodes.brief: Fixing a broken water pump for the exhausted gangers secures two leather buckets of brackish cooling water.
nodes.page: The pump handle finally kicks back with a solid, reassuring thud and draws up two leather buckets of dark, mineral-stained water from the deep sump below. You hoist the dripping straps over your shoulders and carry them carefully across the uneven cinders to the waiting tender. The liquid is far from pure, but it will keep the water gauge safely above the danger line as you steam out across the grey expanse.

nodes.title: The Greasy Rag
nodes.brief: Calming a fight between tired gangers over a shared oil-rag earns a warm cup of chicory and a spare wick.
nodes.page:
Two gangers from the track crews crouch beside a cooling firebox, shouting over a tattered piece of greasy cotton waste they both claim by seniority. Their tempers fray thin as dry rope in the biting wind off the ash-dunes, and their fingers twitch near the iron wrenches tucked in their belts. You step between their raised shoulders, letting the steam-whistle hiss a low warning note while you remind them how far Ashgate lies behind and how cold the night will grow.

One ganger spits into the grey dust and curses your interference, but the other catches your eye, nods slowly, and lets go of the rag to reach for a dented tin pot resting near the embers.

nodes.title: Steaming Chicory in the Ash
nodes.brief: Calming a fight between tired gangers over a shared oil-rag earns a warm cup of chicory and a spare wick.
nodes.page: Hot, dark liquid swirls in a cracked ceramic mug handed over with a gruff grumble about meddling firemen who don't know when to keep their boots out of track brawls. You cup your frozen palms around the warmth, feeling the bitter chicory bite the back of your throat as the gangers slump back against a discarded coal tender. Beside the empty tin, a length of fresh hemp wick lies coiled like a sleeping adder, soaked in tallow and ready for trimming. The older ganger pushes it toward your knuckles with the toe of his boot and offers a grunt of grudging truce.

nodes.title: Tensions by the Boiler
nodes.brief: Calming a fight between tired gangers over a shared oil-rag earns a warm cup of chicory and a spare wick.
nodes.page: The lingering argument threatens to flare up again as another track hand joins the circle, casting suspicious glances at your brass-trimmed jacket and the Water Key strapped securely beneath your oilskin. You need to keep the peace without reaching for iron or letting your own voice crack under the mounting pressure of the schedule. You even your breathing, matching the idle engine's beat behind you, and fix the newcomer with a cold, level stare that brooks no further shouting.

nodes.title: A Flash of Temper
nodes.brief: Calming a fight between tired gangers over a shared oil-rag earns a warm cup of chicory and a spare wick.
nodes.page: A sudden shove catches you off balance, sending your shoulder hard against the jagged iron corner of a rusted ballast wagon and leaving a deep, purple bruise beneath your woolen waistcoat. The gangers scatter into the grey gloom before you can recover your footing, leaving you alone with your throbbing arm and a half-empty mug spilled across the frozen ties. You salvage what you can from the dirt, nursing your bruised pride and your aching shoulder as you climb back up onto the iron deck of the Marrowbone.

nodes.title: A Cup Shared in Silence
nodes.brief: Calming a fight between tired gangers over a shared oil-rag earns a warm cup of chicory and a spare wick.
nodes.page: Your calm voice takes the raw edge off their exhaustion, turning the rising brawl into a sullen, weary quiet broken only by the crackle of burning coke-dust. The older ganger respects a cool head in a tight spot and presses both the warm mug and a small token of alliance into your gloved hands. You pocket the prize and prepare to cast off from the siding before the low sky darkens further.

nodes.title: The Weeping Gland
nodes.brief: Repacking a leaking steam gland on a stranded shunting engine gains a set of heavy brass spanners for your kit.
nodes.page: A stalled shunting engine settles into the ash-drift a few yards down the line, its high-pressure steam gland weeping a steady, hissing stream of white vapor into the freezing air. You approach the abandoned iron beast with your hammer ready, tapping the casing to gauge the thickness of the corroded metal and finding the packing completely rotted away by years of neglect and bad water. The rusted bolts resist your first three pulls, screaming in protest against the salt-crust holding their threads fast.

nodes.title: Wrenching the Iron Free
nodes.brief: Repacking a leaking steam gland on a stranded shunting engine gains a set of heavy brass spanners for your kit.
nodes.page: You throw your full weight against the rusted lever, grunting as the stubborn bolt finally yields with a sharp crack that echoes across the empty rail yard like a pistol shot. Scalding mist billows around your wrists, smelling of old oil and sulfur, but you keep your grip while you strip the ruined packing ring with the tip of your pocket-knife. A set of heavy brass spanners, stamped with the old mark of the Gangers' Union, lies neatly looped over a nearby grease-bucket just waiting to be claimed.

nodes.title: Bending the Seized Valve
nodes.brief: Repacking a leaking steam gland on a stranded shunting engine gains a set of heavy brass spanners for your kit.
nodes.page: The replacement graphite packing resists being hammered into the narrow slot of the valve housing, threatening to wedge crookedly and ruin the seal entirely if you force it with too much speed. You adjust your grip on the spanner, forearms straining as you turn the main gland nut while the steam pressure gauge flickers on the bulkhead.

nodes.title: A Scorched Wrist and Lost Time
nodes.brief: Repacking a leaking steam gland on a stranded shunting engine gains a set of heavy brass spanners for your kit.
nodes.page: A sudden drop in boiler pressure causes the valve to buck violently, spitting a jet of boiling water that slips past your leather glove and leaves a painful, angry scald across your wrist. You jerk your hand back with a sharp intake of breath, watching precious minutes slip away into the grey fog as the pressure bleeds out into the ballast. You manage to finish the job eventually, but the delay costs you dear in fuel and patience.

nodes.title: Tightened to True
nodes.brief: Repacking a leaking steam gland on a stranded shunting engine gains a set of heavy brass spanners for your kit.
nodes.page: Your wrench turns the final nut home with a clean, satisfying bite, sealing the high-pressure steam completely and leaving only a faint smell of warm oil behind in the crisp air. The repair holds firm against the surging pressure of the boiler, iron and brass doing their work. You gather your tools and claim the heavy set of spanners as your own, knowing they will serve you well before the line reaches Cinderfall.

nodes.title: The Sleeping Foreman
nodes.brief: Stealing past the sleeping foreman to retrieve a stolen ledger reveals the hidden combination to the supply locker.
nodes.page:
Canvas flaps keep the biting grit of the Cinder Steppe out of the Union bunkhouse, trapping a fog of cheap tobacco and tallow smoke. Near the cold cast-iron stove, the shift foreman snores heavily into his rolled-up wool coat, a brass pocket-watch chain glinting across his stained waistcoat. Beneath his dangling hand rests the stolen timber ledger, its leather cover cracked and gray with fine mineral dust. You slip inside on silent boots, keeping your eyes fixed on the rhythmic rise and fall of his broad chest as you reach down to slide the heavy book from his grasp without waking him.

The pages flutter slightly in the draft, revealing a series of neat tally marks beside a pencilled sequence of numbers that outline the tumblers of the rear locker.

exits.label: Lift the ledger from his fingers

nodes.title: Secrets in the Dust
nodes.brief: Stealing past the sleeping foreman to retrieve a stolen ledger reveals the hidden combination to the supply locker.
nodes.page: Sunlight filters through the begrimed clerestory windows, casting long, dusty shafts across the cluttered interior of the supply car. Holding the recovered ledger close to your face, you squint against the gloom to decipher the faded pencil notes left by the night clerks. The combination is scribbled across the margin in a hasty, slanted hand, tucked beneath a freight manifest for heavy slag-irons. Every floorboard beneath your boots groans at the slightest shift of your weight, threatening to alert the sleeping crew in the adjoining compartment. You memorize the numbers quickly, turning the sequence over in your head until it burns into your memory like hot coals.

nodes.title: Turning the Iron Dial
nodes.brief: Stealing past the sleeping foreman to retrieve a stolen ledger reveals the hidden combination to the supply locker.
nodes.page:
The heavy steel door of the supply locker stands before you, its brass combination dial pitted with green corrosion and stubborn age. Breathing even through your nose to quiet your racing pulse, you set your fingers on the cold metal ring and click through the combination found in the ledger. Each notch falls into place with a dry, metallic thud that sounds unnaturally loud in the silent car. From the corner, the foreman shifts his bulk on the cot, letting out a low, gravelly grunt that freezes your hand mid-turn on the final digit.

You must commit to the last click before he wakes fully.

check.label: Twist the dial to final drop

nodes.title: A Clattering Mistake
nodes.brief: Stealing past the sleeping foreman to retrieve a stolen ledger reveals the hidden combination to the supply locker.
nodes.page: Your thumb slips on the greasy rim of the brass dial at the worst possible moment, sending a sharp, echoing snap through the hollow metal casing. The foreman jolts upright with a hoarse curse and dives a hand beneath his wool pillow for his iron spanner. You wrench the locker door open in a desperate rush, grabbing whatever loose supplies your fingers find before diving out through the narrow freight hatch into the blinding ash-light. An iron spanner strikes the steel wall just inches above your shoulder and digs a deep, ringing dent as you tumble headfirst into the grey drifts below.

nodes.title: Cleanly Picked
nodes.brief: Stealing past the sleeping foreman to retrieve a stolen ledger reveals the hidden combination to the supply locker.
nodes.page: The brass mechanism yields with a smooth click, and the iron door swings open on well-oiled hinges. Inside, neat rows of wrapped tallow candles, fresh gasket cord, and sealed tins of machine grease wait in the dimness. You reach past the ordinary stores to claim a compact, brass-cased pocket level left behind by an itinerant surveyor, sliding it quietly into your canvas jacket. The foreman stirs on his cot, then sinks back into sleep without discovering the breach. You retreat into the grey haze of the yard, carrying your prize without a sound.

nodes.title: The Carcass of the Tender
nodes.brief: A flock of soot-gulls startles from the carcass of an overturned tender, wheeling wildly into the ash-choked grey sky above.
nodes.page: A sudden flurry of slate-grey wings erupts from the rusted ribs of an overturned coal tender, scattering a fine cloud of old soot into the freezing air. The skeletal iron frame lies half-buried in the shifting dunes like the carcass of some prehistoric leviathan, its water tanks split wide by ancient frost. As the soot-gulls wheel wildly into the leaden sky, a low, metallic groaning reverberates through the ground beneath your boots, reminding you how thin the crust of civilization is out here on the Cinder Steppe. You pause beside the rusted ruin, wiping a film of greasy black dust from your goggles while the wind howls through the twisted stays. Ahead, the tracks curve away toward the distant murmur of the Grey Bazaar, where smoke curls lazily from thousands of makeshift chimneys built into stalled freight cars.

nodes.title: The Water-Wagon Cistern
nodes.brief: The Water-Wagon: A massive rusted tender converted into a communal cistern guarded by armed men with thirsty, hollow eyes.
nodes.page: A massive bogie-tender, stripped of its wheels and shored up with timber blocks, dominates the centre of the sprawling camp as a communal water tank. Armed guards with hollow, thirsty eyes pace the perimeter catwalks, resting their hands on heavy iron wrenches and watching every stranger with unwavering suspicion. The air smells of wet rust, boiled salt, and the sharp tang of sweat. Down in the muddy trenches around the base of the iron giant, people barter desperately with chipped tokens and scraps of copper for a single dripping measure of liquid. The entire settlement hums with a desperate, pent-up energy under the low, bruised sky.

exits.label: Wait in line for the heavy mallet
Siphon extra water from the camp boiler
Calibrate the brass float-valve for tokens
Clear the blocked drainage pipe beneath
Listen to the storm clock groan

nodes.title: Weeping Rivet
nodes.brief: Patching a weeping rivet on the cistern wall with lead solder earns a full leather skin of sweet well water.
nodes.page:
You climb the slick iron ladder of the great water-tender, balancing against the damp side plate where a stubborn rivet weeps a thin stream of precious moisture. Pulling a stick of lead-tin solder and a small paraffin torch from your tool kit, you clear away the crust of green oxidation with a wire brush until clean metal shows. The flame roars softly in the wind, casting a warm, flickering light against the towering iron wall as the solder flows smoothly into the gap. When you test the seal with the flat of your thumb, the leak is gone entirely, leaving only a dark, damp stain on the dry plate below.

The grateful guard leaning against the valve-housing tosses you a heavy leather skin filled with cool, sweet well water in payment.

exits.label: Return to the central water platform

nodes.title: Sealing the Seam
nodes.brief: Patching a weeping rivet on the cistern wall with lead solder earns a full leather skin of sweet well water.
nodes.page:
The metal is dangerously thin around the corroded seam, and the heat of your torch threatens to blow out a larger hole in the ancient plate if you linger a second too long. Sweat runs down your forehead, stinging your eyes as you feather the flame with one hand while pressing the solder stick firmly into the joint with the other. The pressure inside the cistern groans against the interior walls, vibrating through your fingertips like a living pulse that refuses to be tamed.

You hold your breath, waiting to see whether the metal holds or gives way under the thermal shock.

check.label: Melt and hold the lead seal

nodes.title: Blown Solder
nodes.brief: Patching a weeping rivet on the cistern wall with lead solder earns a full leather skin of sweet well water.
nodes.page: The brittle iron plate gives way with a sharp hiss of escaping steam, blasting a shower of molten lead solder directly across your knuckles. You pull your hand back with a sharp gasp, dropping your torch into the grey mud below as a stinging, red burn flares across your skin. The guard above mutters a dry curse at the wasted water leaking from the fresh breach, tossing you a dirty rag and ordering you off the ladder before you do any more damage. You nurse your scorched hand in the cold wind, poorer by a tool and richer by a painful lesson in haste.

nodes.title: A Full Leather Skin
nodes.brief: Patching a weeping rivet on the cistern wall with lead solder earns a full leather skin of sweet well water.
nodes.page: The solder cools to a dull grey finish, perfectly sealing the weeping seam against the constant internal pressure of the giant tank. The guard nods in grim approval, unhooks a plump leather skin from the rail, and drops it into your waiting arms.
