Water sloshes cool inside the leather, and the dry ache in your throat eases at the sound alone. You sling the strap over your shoulder, feeling the solid value of honest work well done as you climb back down to the crowded yard.

exits.label: Return to the central water platform

nodes.title: The Line of Eyes
nodes.brief: Enduring the armed guards hostile stares while waiting in line secures a heavy wooden mallet for driving track pins.
nodes.page:
Wool coats and grease-stained caps do little against the hostile stares of the guards posted along the staging rail. They lean against stacked crates of ballast rock, fingers hooked casually into their belts, watching every shift you make in the queue. The metallic tang of sulphur hangs thick between your teeth as the line inches forward toward the quartermaster's counter, where tools are traded under the glare of unblinking lanterns.

Chin tucked into your collar, you time your breath to the distant pumps until the sergeant at the desk jerks his thumb toward the timber rack.

exits.label: Step forward to claim the mallet

nodes.title: The Quartermaster's Stare
nodes.brief: Enduring the armed guards hostile stares while waiting in line secures a heavy wooden mallet for driving track pins.
nodes.page: The sergeant's eyes remain fixed on your knuckles while you reach out toward the hickory-handled mallet resting among the rusted spikes on the zinc table. A sudden murmur ripples through the guard detail behind you, and a heavy hand grips the flat of a bayonet blade with a dry rasp of steel against leather. Heat climbs the back of your neck. You clamp down on your pulse and keep your fingers from twitching under the sharp scrutiny. A single false move will bring the iron down upon your wrists before your palm can close around the seasoned wood.

nodes.title: A Heavy Toll
nodes.brief: Enduring the armed guards hostile stares while waiting in line secures a heavy wooden mallet for driving track pins.
nodes.page: Your fingers jerk against the zinc edge, knocking a loose drift-pin clattering across the iron floorboards and drawing a sharp bark of laughter from the sergeant. The guard closest to you shoves you hard against the bulkhead, leaving a jagged scrape along your ribs and stealing the breath from your lungs with a dull thud. You bite your tongue until you taste copper, clutching your bruised side while the laughing guard kicks the heavy mallet further out of your immediate reach. They let you take it in the end, but the pain in your ribs throbs in time with your boots as you limp back toward the siding.

nodes.title: The Weight of Iron
nodes.brief: Enduring the armed guards hostile stares while waiting in line secures a heavy wooden mallet for driving track pins.
nodes.page:
Your fingers close around the seasoned hickory handle of the mallet, the balanced weight reassuring against your palm despite the hostile glares burning into your back. You lift it clear of the zinc counter without a single tremor in your wrist, earning a grudging nod from the sergeant as he swipes a greasy ledger shut. The tool is scarred with old burn marks and notched from driving countless thousands of track pins into the frozen ash-beds, but the grain is solid and true.

You tuck the heavy head beneath your arm and turn away into the grey gloom before anyone can change their mind.

nodes.title: The Siphon's Whisper
nodes.brief: Trickling extra water into the camp boiler while no one looks lets you siphon off a double ration of drinking water.
nodes.page:
Steam hisses softly from the auxiliary belly-cock of the camp boiler, masking the gentle gurgle of the rubberized tube you lower into the overflow basin. The gangers are all crowded around the far side of the tender, arguing over a handful of salt-cured beef and greasy tobacco leaves. Every drop counts out here on the dry flats, and the secondary line fills with sweet condensation while the attendants turn their backs to warm their hands over a brazier.

You pinch the rubber shut with your thumb and slip the dripping hose into your canvas kit before anyone glances back.

nodes.title: Beyond the Boiling Vats
nodes.brief: Trickling extra water into the camp boiler while no one looks lets you siphon off a double ration of drinking water.
nodes.page:
Steam curls in lazy plumes from the safety valves of the station boilers, casting long, wavering shadows across the gravel bed where the supply teams camp. You shoulder your canvas kit, feeling the satisfying shift of the extra water bladder against your spine as you navigate the narrow gap between two rusted coal hoppers. The air tastes of scorched grease and wet iron, and the low murmur of the card players fades behind the rattling rhythm of a shunting crane further down the line.

You follow the rusted spur curving away toward the silent water-wagon.

nodes.title: The Guarded Basin
nodes.brief: Trickling extra water into the camp boiler while no one looks lets you siphon off a double ration of drinking water.
nodes.page: The brass valve wheel turns with a dry, protesting squeak that sounds deafening against the background drone of the camp generators. You keep your eyes fixed on the reflection in the oily puddle below, watching for the swinging lanterns of the patrol detail while you coax the stubborn tap another fraction of an inch. A fraction too wide and the hiss will carry across the yard; a fraction too slow and the heavy boots will round the corner before the bladder is full. You hold your breath, your fingers slick with condensation and soot as you wait for the stream to steady.

nodes.title: Caught in the Spill
nodes.brief: Trickling extra water into the camp boiler while no one looks lets you siphon off a double ration of drinking water.
nodes.page: The hose slips from the nozzle with a sharp hiss of atomized spray, splashing a dark circle of moisture across the dry dust right at the feet of the roundsman. A heavy hand drops onto your shoulder before you can snatch the bladder away, spinning you around to face a lantern-jawed overseer with vinegar in his eyes. He relieves you of the extra water ration on the spot, adding a sharp cuff to your ear for your trouble and leaving your knuckles scraped against the rough iron plating. You limp away empty-handed, poorer in water but richer in caution.

nodes.title: A Stolen Drought
nodes.brief: Trickling extra water into the camp boiler while no one looks lets you siphon off a double ration of drinking water.
nodes.page:
The hose runs silent and heavy until the canvas side swells tight against your ribs, plump with cool condensation scavenged from the station boilers. You snap the brass clip home just as boots crunch on the gravel behind you, but the roundsman only grunts and passes without a second glance. The extra water sloshes against your spine, a precious little reserve against the dry miles ahead on the Cinder Steppe.

You secure the neck of the bladder with a stout hemp cord and merge back into the shifting crowd.

nodes.title: The Brass Float
nodes.brief: Calibrating the cistern's brass float-valve earns a handful of copper washers and a tin of anti-friction grease.
nodes.page:
Small adjustments ask for a sure hand and a fine ear for the way metal sings under pressure when the valve-seat settles into its groove. You kneel beside the massive brass housing of the cistern, tapping the linkage gently with the flat of a small wrench until the high-pitched whistle settles into a low, contented purr. The overseer watches from the edge of the staging, sour-faced until he checks the gauge and finds the fluid level climbing.

He tosses you a greasy tin and a handful of washers as his sole acknowledgment of honest work.

nodes.title: Along the Siding
nodes.brief: Calibrating the cistern's brass float-valve earns a handful of copper washers and a tin of anti-friction grease.
nodes.page:
Out of the grey haze, iron wheels rise like monuments to forgotten timetables, journals caked in black grease and dry alkali dust. You pick your way along the ballast shoulder, swinging the small tin of anti-friction grease in your palm as the copper washers chink softly inside your pocket. Every carriage here bears the scars of the Long Fire, scorched ribs and buckled window frames standing empty against the low, bruised sky.

You round the corner of a tilted dining car and spot the low brick profile of the pump-house.

nodes.title: The Binding Pin
nodes.brief: Calibrating the cistern's brass float-valve earns a handful of copper washers and a tin of anti-friction grease.
nodes.page: The threaded collar of the float-valve is crusted with blue-green verdigris that threatens to strip the ancient brass threads at the slightest wrench twist. You apply a dab of thick grease and apply steady, measured pressure to the lever, feeling the microscopic give of the metal through the handle of your tool. If the pin shears now, the entire cistern will drain into the ballast before you can drive a wooden plug into the feed-pipe. You ease off a hair's breadth and tap the housing again with a lighter touch.

nodes.title: Stripped Threads
nodes.brief: Calibrating the cistern's brass float-valve earns a handful of copper washers and a tin of anti-friction grease.
nodes.page: The ancient brass thread gives way with a sudden, grating screech, showering your knuckles in sharp metal flakes and hot, greasy water. You curse under your breath as the packing nut spins loose, venting a plume of scalding steam that leaves a stinging red welt across the back of your hand. You spend a frantic ten minutes wrapping the ruined joint in hemp twine and yellow soap before the leak finally subsides to a sullen weep. The task is done, but your hands are smarting and the grease tin took a nasty dent in the scuffle.

exits.label: Gather your tools and move on

nodes.title: The Repaired Valve
nodes.brief: Calibrating the cistern's brass float-valve earns a handful of copper washers and a tin of anti-friction grease.
nodes.page: Perseverance pays against the stubborn friction of rusted metal, leaving the float-valve seated true and firm within its housing. Hot water ceases its wasteful hiss. Pressurized quiet takes its place, and the boiler gauge holds true. A handful of heavy copper washers and a stout tin of yellow anti-friction grease are your reward for the trouble, tucked safely into the tool-chest before you step back onto the footplate.

nodes.title: Beneath the Iron Tank
nodes.brief: Clearing a blocked drainage pipe beneath the iron tank gains a rusted but serviceable brass grease-gun.
nodes.page: Thick crusts of grey alkali flake away beneath your scraper as you clear the choked drainage pipe beneath the roadside water tank. Stagnant moisture breaks free at last with a foul, heavy gurgle, spilling into the dry ballast below and clearing the drain-hole at long last. Probing the recess reveals a stout, oil-stained tool wedged in the mud, which proves upon inspection to be a rusted but serviceable brass grease-gun.

nodes.title: The Clogged Drain
nodes.brief: Clearing a blocked drainage pipe beneath the iron tank gains a rusted but serviceable brass grease-gun.
nodes.page: Sludge and cinders have packed the overflow channel beneath the massive tender until it resembles hard cement. Working the bent iron poker back and forth loosens the plug of debris, letting foul water drain away from the axle-boxes where it might otherwise cause dangerous rot. The cleared pipe breathes out a damp, mineral smell of sulfur and cold earth into the dry wind.

nodes.title: Clearing the Blocked Pipe
nodes.brief: Clearing a blocked drainage pipe beneath the iron tank gains a rusted but serviceable brass grease-gun.
nodes.page: Stubborn corrosion locks the lower drain-cock tight, threatening to twist the copper feed-line right off its mounting brackets if you apply too much force. Boot braced on the iron chassis plate, you take the pipe-wrench in both hands and lean into a slow, measured torque while the ancient metal groans under the strain.

nodes.title: The Snapped Feed-Line
nodes.brief: Clearing a blocked drainage pipe beneath the iron tank gains a rusted but serviceable brass grease-gun.
nodes.page: The seized brass fitting shears clean off with a sharp crack, spraying a jet of scalding, greasy water across your sleeve and scalding your wrist before you can wrench the shut-off valve closed. Precious steam pressure bleeds away into the alkali dust, and you are left binding the weeping joint with soaked hemp cord and cursing the unforgiving metal.

nodes.title: The Grease-Gun
nodes.brief: Clearing a blocked drainage pipe beneath the iron tank gains a rusted but serviceable brass grease-gun.
nodes.page:
Thick rust flakes fall from the drainpipe into your palm as the choked channel finally spits its foul sediment into the ash-dune below. The pressure gauge on the side of the boiler settles into a steadier rhythm, sighing with relief as the trapped water finds its proper course. Among the grit and discarded scrap beneath the valve housing, your fingers close around a heavy iron cylinder wrapped in greasy rag. It is a battered but serviceable brass grease-gun, its leather plunger still supple enough to force lubricant into stubborn journal-boxes when the mileage mounts.

Wiping the nozzle on your trouser leg, you secure the tool in the cab locker alongside the spare oil can.

nodes.title: Midnight on the Steppe
nodes.brief: The storm clock clicks toward midnight as a low, metallic groaning echoes across the dunes from the direction of the viaduct.
nodes.page:
The storm clock hanging above the fire-door clicks its heavy iron tooth toward midnight, shaking loose a fine drift of grey soot across the brass dial. Far across the grey flats, from the direction of the towering viaduct, a deep metallic groaning rolls through the ground like the turning of a subterranean engine. The horizon shivers under a low bank of bruised purple clouds where the ash-storm season gathers its strength.

You check the water glass one more time, feeling the steady thrum of the copper boiler against your palms as the Marrowbone waits for the signal to move.

nodes.title: The Iron Scriptorium
nodes.brief: The Iron Scriptorium: A derelict telegraph carriage where a lone clerk still records the passage of trains that never arrive.
nodes.page: A derelict telegraph carriage sits abandoned beside the tracks, its windows frosted with alkali and salt, yet a single yellow lamp still burns behind the warped wooden door. Inside, a lone clerk in a frayed uniform records the passage of phantom trains in a ledger that never ends, surrounded by ticking sounders and mountains of damp paper. The place smells of stale tobacco and ozone, offering shelter from the rising wind and multiple paths deeper into the ash-steppeland.

nodes.title: The Flickering Sounder
nodes.brief: Decoding a flickering telegraph message about patrol movements earns an advance warning of Rail Baron blockades.
nodes.page: Brass arms twitch erratically across the glass-covered dial as the telegraph key chatters out a rapid, fractured sequence of dots and dashes. By watching the rhythm of the stuttering needle, you piece together a warning meant for the patrol posts up-line about railhead blockades and armed patrols moving out from the viaduct. The knowledge rests heavy in your mind as the paper ribbon falls silent.

nodes.title: The Flickering Needle
nodes.brief: Decoding a flickering telegraph message about patrol movements earns an advance warning of Rail Baron blockades.
nodes.page: Glass tremors in the brass frame as the telegraph relay chatters out a frantic staccato against the wooden wall of the waystation. The paper tape uncoils in a jerky dance, punching neat holes that spell out the movements of the armored patrol cars stationed three miles up the line. Every strike of the armature sounds like a dry knuckle rapping on a coffin lid, marking the precise hours the Barons intend to lock the junction switches. You commit the sequence of dots and dashes to memory, watching the ink fade into the cheap pulp paper as the needle finally falls still.

exits.label: Pocket the decoded slip and run

nodes.title: Decoding the Wire
nodes.brief: Decoding a flickering telegraph message about patrol movements earns an advance warning of Rail Baron blockades.
nodes.page: The paper ribbon feeds through the embossing machine too fast, smudging the ink dots into an unintelligible blur of Morse code while the signal needle chatters frantically against its brass stop. You squint through the dim lamplight, trying to isolate the code-groups for military patrols from the random static of the atmospheric storm before the needle drops dead.

nodes.title: The Static Blur
nodes.brief: Decoding a flickering telegraph message about patrol movements earns an advance warning of Rail Baron blockades.
nodes.page: Static discharge leaps from the brass sounder with a sharp snap, charring the paper tape to black ash and leaving your ears ringing with a high, thin whine. You stumble back against the shelving, scattering a dozen outdated waybills across the floorboards and losing precious minutes to the confusion before you can steady your breathing.

nodes.title: The Scriptorium Ink
nodes.brief: Decoding a flickering telegraph message about patrol movements earns an advance warning of Rail Baron blockades.
nodes.page: Blue ink dries slowly on the damp parchment of the ledger while the telegraph key chatters its warning from across the deserted carriage. You trace the freshly stamped route manifest with a soot-stained thumb, noting the specific hours the armored patrol carriages clear the lower embankment. The clerk has already packed his inkwells into a leather satchel, leaving behind only the carbon copy of the dispatch and a silent nod of complicity. It is a precarious edge to walk, but knowing which switch-lever the Barons plan to drop next gives you a narrow channel through the grey waste.

exits.label: Step back out to the platform

nodes.title: Crate on the Embankment
nodes.brief: Hauling a heavy crate of coal up the embankment secures a bundle of dry waxed paper for lighting fires.
nodes.page:
Heavy black dust coats the ballast where the supply wagon tipped into the ditch. You dig your boots into the shifting grey shale, heaving your shoulders against the splintered pine of a dropped coal crate. The wood groans under your palms as greasy soot smears across your forearms, and the steep embankment threatens to slide beneath your weight back toward the tracks.

Wrenching the lid free reveals a nest of dry, paraffin-dipped paper wrappers packed tight against the damp, ready to coax the cold fire-bed back into a roaring furnace.

exits.label: Climb back down the ballast slope

nodes.title: Hauling the Heavy Coal
nodes.brief: Hauling a heavy crate of coal up the embankment secures a bundle of dry waxed paper for lighting fires.
nodes.page: Slipping fingers find no purchase on the slick, greasy timber of the crate as the loose ash embankment crumbles beneath your boots. You brace your legs against the steep grey slope, lock your spine, and throw your full weight upward to drag the load clear of the ditch before the shifting ground gives way. You strain against the dead mass of the crate, muscles burning in the thin mountain air as the shale slides out from under your heels.

nodes.title: Burden of the Slip
nodes.brief: Hauling a heavy crate of coal up the embankment secures a bundle of dry waxed paper for lighting fires.
nodes.page:
Gravity wins the struggle, and the crate rolls back down the embankment, dragging you through the abrasive grey grit and scraping your knuckles raw against the jagged ballast. You pull yourself up with a bruised shoulder and sore ribs, coughing up a mouthful of bitter dust while the timber settles deeper into the ash-dune.

The spilled fuel is lost to the slope, leaving you with only a torn coat and a bruised forearm to show for the effort.

exits.label: Return empty-handed to the engine cab

nodes.title: Securing the Waxed Paper
nodes.brief: Hauling a heavy crate of coal up the embankment secures a bundle of dry waxed paper for lighting fires.
nodes.page:
Muscle and grit carry the crate over the crest of the embankment as your boots find firm footing on the sleeper-ends just before the shale gives way. Inside the splintered casing lies a tight bundle of dry, waxed paper wrappers, perfectly preserved from the damp and smelling faintly of paraffin and old storage oil.

You tuck the bundle securely beneath your leather jacket, knowing it will coax the stubborn fire-bed into a roaring heat when the night closes in.

nodes.title: Dusty Dispatch Drawers
nodes.brief: Searching through dusty dispatch drawers yields an outdated schedule signed by the old Stationmaster-General herself.
nodes.page:
Rusted brass handles pull away from the rotting mahogany desk with a dry shriek that echoes through the abandoned station office. Inside the lowest drawer, buried beneath layers of grey silt and dead insects, lies a bundle of stiff parchment schedules bound with brittle twine.

You brush the soot from the uppermost page, revealing precise ink stamps and formal routing notes bearing the unmistakable, spidery signature of the old Stationmaster-General herself.

nodes.title: Ink on the Parchment
nodes.brief: Searching through dusty dispatch drawers yields an outdated schedule signed by the old Stationmaster-General herself.
nodes.page:
Faded red margin notes trace the forgotten running times of coal tenders and passenger expresses through sectors that have long since grown over with ash-grass. The paper crackles dryly between your fingers, smelling of old cellars and long-dead bureaucracy in a world that has forgotten what schedules mean.

You fold the brittle document carefully and slip it into your breast pocket, keeping the old rules close against your ribs.

nodes.title: The Stationmasters Signature
nodes.brief: Searching through dusty dispatch drawers yields an outdated schedule signed by the old Stationmaster-General herself.
nodes.page: Heavy oak drawers stick fast in the warped carcass of the brasswind desk, choked with fine grey dust and the brittle husks of dead beetles. You prise the bottom slide open with an iron poker, uncovering a sheaf of damp-rotted manifests and a calfskin ledger signed by the ancient Stationmaster-General with thick purple gall-ink. While the office timbers groan under the relentless pressure of the ash-dune outside, you trace the faded ink lines of a forgotten bypass freight run that might just spare No. 9 the Baron checkpoints ahead, your fingers hovering over the ink-smudged seal as the ceiling joists crack in the rising wind.

nodes.title: Caught in the Jam
nodes.brief: Searching through dusty dispatch drawers yields an outdated schedule signed by the old Stationmaster-General herself.
nodes.page:
A rusted iron binder snaps shut across your knuckles with a sharp bite, pinning your fingers to the rotting desk drawer and sending a jolt of pain up your arm. You jerk your hand back with a sharp hiss, leaving a smear of blood on the splintered wood while the scattered papers flutter uselessly into the grey dust.

You nurse your throbbing hand in the dim light, having lost precious minutes to the stubborn furniture.

exits.label: Gather your breath and move on

nodes.title: The Old Timetable
nodes.brief: Searching through dusty dispatch drawers yields an outdated schedule signed by the old Stationmaster-General herself.
nodes.page:
Nimble fingers untangle the rusted brass clasp of the desk drawer, however narrowly, slipping the prize free before the jammed runner can trap your knuckles. The prize is a stiff, official schedule bearing the rare stamp of the Stationmaster-General, outlining the hidden sidings and secret watering points of the upper line.

You tuck the parchment safely into your coat, securing a silent advantage for the road ahead.

nodes.title: The Eccentric Clerk
nodes.brief: Matching wits with the eccentric telegraph clerk wins a brass pocket-compass that points toward magnetic north.
nodes.page:
A solitary figure in a grease-stained telegrapher's visor sits behind the ticket grille, nodding rhythmically to the hum of dead wires. You match his dry riddles with a patient ear, trading old stories of the Ashgate yards for a brass pocket-compass that still spins true toward magnetic north despite the surrounding sulphur haze.

You pocket the cool metal instrument, tipping your cap to the silent clerk as he turns back to his silent sounder.

exits.label: Head back to the steaming engine

nodes.title: The Telegraph Clerks Bargain
nodes.brief: Matching wits with the eccentric telegraph clerk wins a brass pocket-compass that points toward magnetic north.
nodes.page: Across a littered counter of brass relays and damp tallow dips, the gaunt clerk taps a rhythmic tattoo with a lead weight while his mismatched eyes track every twitch of your soot-stained fingers. You match his dry, mocking cadence tap for tap on the dead brass key, trading old station gossip about the vanished Hesper Quill until his thin mouth twitches into a grudging grin and he shides an unpolished brass compass across the green baize. Just as your palm closes over the cold metal and the needle begins its erratic spin toward the magnetic pole, he slams the brass cover shut with a sharp click.

nodes.title: Outwitted by the Wire
nodes.brief: Matching wits with the eccentric telegraph clerk wins a brass pocket-compass that points toward magnetic north.
nodes.page:
A sharp retort from behind the brass grille catches you off guard, turning your clever argument into an awkward stutter as the clerk lets out a dry, rasping laugh. He refuses to hand over the compass, leaving you empty-handed and flustered while the telegraph sounder chatters mockingly in the background.

You swallow your pride and turn away from the counter with a sour taste in your mouth.

nodes.title: Winning the Compass
nodes.brief: Matching wits with the eccentric telegraph clerk wins a brass pocket-compass that points toward magnetic north.
nodes.page:
Sharp banter wins the day, however narrowly, as your quick tongue turns the clerk's own riddle back upon him until he grunts in grudging respect. He slides a brass pocket-compass across the scarred deal counter, its glass face clear and its internal needle trembling toward magnetic north.

You pocket the solid weight of the instrument, securing a reliable guide through the blinding ash-storms ahead.

nodes.title: Ascent Toward the Viaduct
nodes.brief: Locomotive No. 9 pants in the thin air as the gradient steepens toward the massive stone footings of the great viaduct.
nodes.page: Locomotive No. 9 pants in the thin, ash-laden air as the gradient steepens toward the massive stone footings of the great viaduct. Hot brass clicks and contracts in the cooling shadows, while the water gauge jitters against its glass mount with every shudder of the heavy boiler. Below the towering arches, the track narrows between drifts of grey gravel and rusted siding furniture abandoned by the Rail Barons' early work gangs. You shovel a fresh measure of low-grade coal into the roaring furnace, watching the orange glow wash over the soot-greased levers and your own tense knuckles. Every breath tastes of sulphur and old iron, reminding you that the ash-storm season is creeping closer across the flat miles of the Cinder Steppe behind.

exits.label: Climb into the shadow of the stone footings

nodes.title: Beneath the Great Arches
nodes.brief: Viaduct Foot: A shadow-drenched encampment tucked beneath the colossal stone arches where smugglers cache contraband goods.
nodes.page: Shadow-drenched encampments tuck deep beneath the colossal stone arches where smugglers cache contraband goods away from the prying eyes of the Rail Barons' patrol engines. Smouldering brazier pots cast long, flickering bars of orange light across stacked wooden crates, grease-stained canvas bundles, and rusted lengths of spare rail. Murmurs drift from behind a makeshift barricade of corrugated tin, and stagnant water taps from somewhere high in the masonry. The air is thick with the scent of cheap tobacco, roasting roots, and heavy lubricating grease. You stand beside the idling engine, weighing your options against the ticking of the storm clock in your chest.

exits.label: Search the gravel near the southern pier
Approach the huddled figures by the brazier
Repair the winch mechanism for the local gangers
Heave the regulator and push up the grade

nodes.title: The Hidden Iron Ring
nodes.brief: Spotting the hidden trapdoor in the gravel under the arch lets you recover a hidden keg of refined lamp oil.
nodes.page: Loose shale and fine grey dust shift beneath your heavy boot as you tread carefully near the moss-slick base of the primary pier. An iron ring crusted with salt and ancient soot lies flush in the packed earth under a drift of discarded ballast. With a sharp tug, you haul against the resistance of packed silt until an oiled wooden trapdoor gives way with a sucking pop. A dank, confined smell rises from the dark cavity below, promising shelter or perhaps something left behind by travelers who vanished long before the Cinder Prophets built their first shrines.

exits.label: Descend into the cool gloom of the cache

nodes.title: Vault of Refined Oil
nodes.brief: Spotting the hidden trapdoor in the gravel under the arch lets you recover a hidden keg of refined lamp oil.
nodes.page: Narrow wooden steps creak under your weight as you lower yourself into the dry masonry alcove beneath the viaduct floor. By the faint amber beam of your pocket lantern, stacked crates emerge from the gloom, their stencils weathered and illegible. Wedged neatly between a pair of water-logged timbers rests a stout tin keg, remarkably unblemished by the surrounding damp and grey rot. A cautious rap against its side produces a dull, heavy slosh that confirms the precious nature of its contents. You haul the sealed vessel free from the dust just as distant iron wheels groan on the rails above.

exits.label: Return to the track with the prize

nodes.title: Sifting the Dark Recesses
nodes.brief: Spotting the hidden trapdoor in the gravel under the arch lets you recover a hidden keg of refined lamp oil.
nodes.page: Deep shadows stretch long and deceptive across the earthen floor of the hidden cellar as you sweep your lantern beam along the stacked timber crates. A rusted tripwire, strung barely an inch above the floorboards, catches the amber light just as your leading boot sweeps forward into the gloom. You freeze mid-stride, your fingers hovering over the heavy brass canister of refined lamp oil while your mind races to calculate the tension of the concealed spring-lock linked to the bulkhead above.

check.label: Trace the wire and slip past the trap

nodes.title: A Clumsy Misstep
nodes.brief: Spotting the hidden trapdoor in the gravel under the arch lets you recover a hidden keg of refined lamp oil.
nodes.page: A sharp metallic snap shatters the silence of the vault as your boot heel clips the hidden wire, releasing a heavy iron toggle that brings a cascade of coarse gravel and sharp slate raining down onto your shoulder. You scramble backward into the dark, cursing under your breath as a jagged splinter of old oak gouges a stinging line across your forearm. The tin keg of lamp oil slips from your grip, denting heavily against the stone floor and leaking a fragrant golden puddle into the dust before you manage to plug the split with a rag.

exits.label: Climb back to the engine with your bruises

nodes.title: Salvaged Wealth
nodes.brief: Spotting the hidden trapdoor in the gravel under the arch lets you recover a hidden keg of refined lamp oil.
nodes.page: Quick wits and careful fingers get you past the hidden snare, and you hoist the tin keg without disturbing the precarious stack above. The sealed vessel yields to your pocket knife with a satisfying hiss of vacuum-sealed air, revealing clear, refined lamp oil that burns cleaner and hotter than anything issued by the Ashgate stores. You stow the prize securely in the cab locker alongside your spare gasket wire, feeling the quiet satisfaction of a debt settled against the bitter road.

nodes.title: Smoke by the Brazier
nodes.brief: Negotiating passage with the suspicious smugglers gains a bundle of dry oak kindling and a dry rag.
nodes.page: Hooded figures in patched greys sit in a loose circle around a smouldering iron brazier, roasting thin strips of salt-cured meat over glowing cinders of dried moss. They watch your approach with guarded, mismatched eyes, their hands resting casually near heavy spanners and grease guns tucked into their belts. A lean woman with an ash-scarred cheek gestures silently with a tin mug toward an empty crate, inviting you to share the warmth while your engine pants softly in the background. You trade quiet words about the road ahead, offering a pinch of genuine tobacco in exchange for small kindnesses and dry provisions.

exits.label: Accept the bundle of dry kindling

nodes.title: The Smuggler's Riddle
nodes.brief: Negotiating passage with the suspicious smugglers gains a bundle of dry oak kindling and a dry rag.
nodes.page: The scarred woman leans forward across the glowing brazier, her gaze fixing on the brass Water Key protruding from your coat pocket with calculating intensity. She poses a sharp riddle about the weight of unlaid rails and the price of water in a dying city, waiting to see if your tongue is as quick as your firing arm. You weigh the syllables carefully in your mind, seeking the precise turn of phrase that will satisfy their superstitious code without giving away the true destination of Locomotive No. 9.

check.label: Match wits with the cautious smugglers

nodes.title: A Costly Exchange
nodes.brief: Negotiating passage with the suspicious smugglers gains a bundle of dry oak kindling and a dry rag.
nodes.page: Your clever argument trips over an awkward stutter as the woman lets out a dry, rasping laugh that echoes sharply off the massive stone piers. The barter turns sour in an instant, and instead of friendly trade, you are forced to pay double for every scrap of dry oak kindling and coarse rag they toss across the ash-dusted ground. They strip a handful of copper wire from your tool roll as an impromptu toll, leaving you poorer in supplies but wiser to the sharp dealings of the lower line.

exits.label: Gather the remaining goods and depart

nodes.title: Kindling and Comradeship
nodes.brief: Negotiating passage with the suspicious smugglers gains a bundle of dry oak kindling and a dry rag.
nodes.page: Sharp banter wins the day however narrowly, turning the smuggler's own riddle back upon her until she grunts in grudging respect and tosses a bundle of dry oak kindling and a clean cotton rag into your lap. The small concession warms your hands as much as the brazier did, providing the vital dry fuel needed to coax stubborn boiler fires into a fierce, clean roar against the gathering damp. You nod your farewells as the camp sinks back into the shadows of the great stone piers.

exits.label: Heave the regulator and push up the grade

nodes.title: The Smuggler's Hoist
nodes.brief: Repairing the crank on a smuggler's hoist earns an iron pry-bar for opening stuck bulkhead doors.
nodes.page: Iron gears grind against their housing and protest every inch of the lift as you work the jammed winch alongside the scarred woman. Grease smears your knuckles, mingling with the stubborn grit of the steppe until your hands feel cast from the same dark metal as the machine. With a sharp snap of releasing tension, the rusted arm swings clear, freeing the payload platform and earning a begrudging nod from your taciturn host. She slides a thick, flat bar of forged iron across the timber floor toward your boots. You grasp the tool and tuck it firmly beneath your coat, knowing it will make short work of any stubborn bulkhead doors ahead.

exits.label: Slide the iron pry-bar into your coat pocket

nodes.title: Wrenching the Iron Lift
nodes.brief: Repairing the crank on a smuggler's hoist earns an iron pry-bar for opening stuck bulkhead doors.
nodes.page: Frost bites hard into your bare palms as you throw your weight against the frozen crank-handle of the smuggler's hoist, straining to force the buckled teeth back into alignment. The rusted iron shudders violently under the sudden torque, throwing a cascade of bitter red sparks against your oilskin coat while the central axle groans under the strain. Every muscle in your shoulders burns as you fight to drive the slipping gear home before the mounting pressure strips the teeth entirely. Your fingers lock around the jagged metal edge, muscles trembling under the load at the very brink of mechanical failure.

check.label: Force the jammed winch into place

nodes.title: A Bitter Toll
nodes.brief: Repairing the crank on a smuggler's hoist earns an iron pry-bar for opening stuck bulkhead doors.
nodes.page: Metal screams in protest as the crank-handle slips from your frozen grip, spinning backward with a brutal crack that catches the back of your knuckles and leaves a deep, weeping graze. Time bleeds away as you bind the torn skin with a dirty strip of rag, nursing a throbbing hand while the smuggler watches with a cold, dry smirk. The hoist remains stubbornly misaligned, forcing you to abandon the tricky repair and push onward through the biting cold without the tool you hoped to gain.

exits.label: Turn away from the stubborn machinery and press on

nodes.title: The Hoist Unlocked
nodes.brief: Repairing the crank on a smuggler's hoist earns an iron pry-bar for opening stuck bulkhead doors.
nodes.page: Iron teeth grind together with a sudden, satisfying shiver of alignment as the rusted hoist surrenders to your clever leverage, clicking smoothly into its proper channel. Whether achieved with effortless grace or through sheer stubborn persistence against the biting wind, the mechanism now turns true and easy under your palm. The scarred woman tosses a soot-stained bar across the planks in silent acknowledgment of your handiwork, and you leave better equipped for the miles ahead.

exits.label: Secure the heavy iron bar and move along

nodes.title: Ascending the Incline
nodes.brief: You heave the regulator forward as the wheels bite into the steep incline, sending sparks flying into the gathering gloom.
nodes.page: Exhaust pulses hard from the chimney. You haul the brass regulator forward and coax the laboring pistons into a rhythmic, pounding roar that shakes the soot from the cab roof. The driving wheels bite deep into the steep, ash-choked incline, sending a blinding flurry of golden sparks dancing wildly into the gathering gloom of the low sky. Steam hisses from the cylinder cocks, wreathing the boiler in a thick, hot fog that smells of scorching oil and ancient coal dust. You lean out from the gangway, watching the dark silhouette of the tracks vanish into the grey waste as the engine fights its way upward.

exits.label: Keep the fire hot and watch the tracks ahead

nodes.title: The Signal Box
nodes.brief: The Signal Box: A skeletal timber tower leaning precariously over the tracks with its semaphore arm jammed upright.
nodes.page: Skeletal timber walls lean precariously over the frozen tracks, holding a single rusted semaphore arm jammed rigidly upright against the low, bruised sky. A narrow ladder ascends into the creaking gloom of the cabin base, offering a dry refuge from the biting ash-choked wind that sweeps across the plateau. Below the landing, various dark openings and mechanical housings invite inspection, while the main iron road stretches onward into the looming shadow of the viaduct.

exits.label: Climb the ladder into the signal tower
Test your nerve on the storm-lashed rungs
Pick the padlock on the lower cabin door
Rewire the dead telegraph in the shelter
Kick open the rusted fire-door in the base
Fire the boiler and charge toward the viaduct

nodes.title: Greasing the Pulleys
nodes.brief: Greasing the rusted cable pulleys in the freezing wind lowers the jammed semaphore and earns a brass lantern.
nodes.page: Cold metal bites through your gloves as you smear thick, black tallow into the frozen teeth of the cable pulleys atop the wooden gantry. The rusted mechanism groans and shudders under the renewed lubrication, slowly yielding to the steady pull of the weighted chains. With a sharp metallic sigh, the jammed semaphore arm drops down from its defiant upright posture, signaling a clear road through the grey waste. A friendly local station hand tosses a battered brass lantern up to the platform as payment for your labor.

exits.label: Catch the brass lantern and descend the ladder

nodes.title: The Lowering Arm
nodes.brief: Greasing the rusted cable pulleys in the freezing wind lowers the jammed semaphore and earns a brass lantern.
nodes.page: Thick tallow smears across the frozen brass axles as you work the greasy lever back and forth until the squealing iron falls silent. The stubborn cables uncoil with a dull metallic clatter, easing the heavy wooden semaphore down into its horizontal resting place. A cold wind rattles the corrugated tin roof overhead, carrying the dry taste of sulphur from the nearby wells. You loop the handle of a sturdy brass lantern over your arm and step back down to solid ground.

exits.label: Carry the brass lantern back to the engine

nodes.title: Freezing Pulleys
nodes.brief: Greasing the rusted cable pulleys in the freezing wind lowers the jammed semaphore and earns a brass lantern.
nodes.page: Your fingers grow numb and clumsy as you attempt to pack hot tallow into the ice-locked bearings of the semaphore gantry while the wind howls across the steppe. The rusted cable housing refuses to turn, binding tight against the frozen spindle with every ounce of pressure you apply to the grease-gun. Frost forms thick and white across your knuckles, threatening to weld your skin to the cold iron if you slip another fraction of an inch. You brace your boots against the icy timber framework, putting your entire weight behind one final, desperate turn of the handle.

nodes.title: A Frozen Slip
nodes.brief: Greasing the rusted cable pulleys in the freezing wind lowers the jammed semaphore and earns a brass lantern.
nodes.page: A sudden gust of wind catches your shoulder, knocking your wrench against the iron housing and sending a sharp, jagged pain shooting through your frost-bitten fingers. The tallow tin slips from your grasp, tumbling down into the grey ash below as the jammed cable snaps back with a harsh metallic twang. You nurse your bruised hand inside your coat, shivering bitterly in the thin air while the semaphore remains stubbornly stuck in the air.

exits.label: Abandon the frozen pulleys and climb down

nodes.title: The Lantern Earned
nodes.brief: Greasing the rusted cable pulleys in the freezing wind lowers the jammed semaphore and earns a brass lantern.
nodes.page: Smooth grease coats the internal drums at last, and the iron cables slide through their channels with a soft hiss. Whether through steady patience or frantic effort against the freezing gale, the semaphore arm drops smoothly into place, clearing the line for the Marrowbone. A brass lantern comes up from the shadows below as a token of appreciation for your trouble.

exits.label: Return to the engine with your new lantern

nodes.title: Ladder in the Wind
nodes.brief: Keeping your nerve while climbing the rickety ladder in the ash-storm secures a roll of stout hemp rope.
nodes.page: Whistling gales tear across the ribbed iron plating of the boiler as you step out onto the swaying gantry. Below you, the Marrowbone puffs grey sulphur into the drifting dunes while the semaphore tower above stretches its rusted iron arms toward a leaden sky. Every handhold is slick with frozen grease and fine, biting grit that scours the skin. You grip the upright stanchion of the ladder, feeling the rusted rungs vibrate with the engine's distant thrum as the ash-storm gathers its full force around your ears.

exits.label: Climb higher into the howling gale

nodes.title: Gantry in the Storm
nodes.brief: Keeping your nerve while climbing the rickety ladder in the ash-storm secures a roll of stout hemp rope.
nodes.page: Jagged flakes of grey rime cling to your woollen collar as you hoist yourself another rung higher above the tender. The wind presses hard against your chest, trying to peel your fingers away from the freezing iron. Up here, high above the tracks, the vast expanse of the Cinder Steppe rolls away in monochromatic waves of ash and shale under a bruised, lowering firmament. You steady your breathing against the biting cold, eyeing the loose cable dangling from the upper pulley.

exits.label: Reach for the swinging hemp line

nodes.title: Ascending the Shivering Iron
nodes.brief: Keeping your nerve while climbing the rickety ladder in the ash-storm secures a roll of stout hemp rope.
nodes.page: Frost bites deep into your knuckles as you stretch your right hand out toward the swaying rope while the ladder lurches violently under a sudden gust of wind. The world drops away into a grey blur of churning ash and rusted iron spars below, testing the absolute limits of your nerve. You lock your jaw against the cold and steady your weight on the narrow rung, reaching out once more.

check.label: Keep your nerve on the ladder

nodes.title: Slips in the Rime
nodes.brief: Keeping your nerve while climbing the rickety ladder in the ash-storm secures a roll of stout hemp rope.
nodes.page: A vicious blast of wind strikes your shoulder mid-reach, knocking your knuckles hard against the iron housing and sending a jagged, white-hot pain shooting through your fingers. You lose your footing for a heart-stopping second, sliding a foot down the rungs before catching yourself with a bruised rib and a torn glove. The precious seconds tick away into the grey gale as you cling to the stanchion, panting heavily against the stinging ash.

exits.label: Secure the line with aching hands

nodes.title: Coil of Hemp
nodes.brief: Keeping your nerve while climbing the rickety ladder in the ash-storm secures a roll of stout hemp rope.
nodes.page: Numb fingers wrap around the thick fibrous coils of the hemp rope and secure the length against your belt. The fibres are rough and dry against your frost-bitten skin, smelling faintly of tar and old salt from some forgotten warehouse down the line. It is a sturdy piece of gear, capable of hauling weight or lashing down a stubborn valve when the storm closes in for good.

exits.label: Descend back to the warm deck

nodes.title: Signal Box Lock
nodes.brief: Picking the padlock on the signal box door reveals a stash of dry coal briquettes and tea leaves.
nodes.page: Timbers creak under the wind's press as you shelter in the recessed alcove of the abandoned signal box. Thick grey dust coats the iron padlock on the oak door, sealing its mechanism against years of neglect and blowing ash. You pull a thin steel wire and a small brass tension pick from your waistcoat pocket, tapping the frozen shackle to test the internal springs.

exits.label: Fit the pick into the keyway

nodes.title: Tumblers in the Rust
nodes.brief: Picking the padlock on the signal box door reveals a stash of dry coal briquettes and tea leaves.
nodes.page: Inside the iron housing, the rusted brass tumblers resist your delicate touch with a stubborn, unyielding grind that threatens to snap your thin wire. The wind howls against the warped window frames outside, rattling the glass panes while you listen closely for the faint, elusive click of the final pin falling into place. Every movement must be measured and precise in the gloom.

nodes.title: Jammed Shackle
nodes.brief: Picking the padlock on the signal box door reveals a stash of dry coal briquettes and tea leaves.
nodes.page: Your tension wire snaps with a sharp, dry ping inside the keyhole, leaving the broken steel wedged firmly in the mechanism and sealing the box tighter than before. Frustration flares hot in your chest as you hammer your gloved palm against the warped timber door in vain. The lost time weighs heavily upon you while the ash-storm whispers warnings across the rusted tin roof overhead.

nodes.title: Briquettes and Leaves
nodes.brief: Picking the padlock on the signal box door reveals a stash of dry coal briquettes and tea leaves.
nodes.page: The padlock at last gives way with a protesting screech and swings wide onto a dry, sheltered interior untouched by the grey tempest outside. Neap-tide stacks of compressed coal briquettes fill the lower bin, alongside a rusted tin canister packed with fragrant dried tea leaves left behind by some long-departed signalman. It is a welcome hoard against the creeping chill of the steppe.

nodes.title: Copper Strands
nodes.brief: Rewiring the electric bell circuit with copper strands brings the dead telegraph back to clicking life.
nodes.page: Inside the dim instrument shelter, the intricate network of brass terminals and faded cotton-wrapped wiring hangs in silent disarray. You draw a length of bright copper wire from your toolkit, stripping back the frayed insulation with your teeth to expose the clean, conductive metal underneath. The old telegraph equipment sits cold and dead upon the wooden desk, waiting for a spark of purpose.

nodes.title: Clicking Needle
nodes.brief: Rewiring the electric bell circuit with copper strands brings the dead telegraph back to clicking life.
nodes.page: You wrap the copper strand securely around the primary binding post, pressing the second end against the auxiliary coil while listening for any sign of current. A faint, electric hum vibrates through the wooden chassis, followed immediately by the rapid, rhythmic clicking of the telegraph needle as it dances back and forth behind its cracked glass cover. The distant line remembers its duty in the dark.

nodes.title: Current in the Wire
nodes.brief: Rewiring the electric bell circuit with copper strands brings the dead telegraph back to clicking life.
nodes.page: A sudden surge of static crackles through the copper binding, sending a sharp, tingling shock up your forearms as you attempt to balance the delicate circuit resistance. The needle swings erratically between old rail codes while the insulation begins to smoke softly from an unexpected short in the aged wiring harness. You must steady your hands instantly to prevent the whole relay from burning out.

nodes.title: Sparks in the Relays
nodes.brief: Rewiring the electric bell circuit with copper strands brings the dead telegraph back to clicking life.
nodes.page: A blinding flash of blue sparks leaps from the terminal block, scorching your knuckles and filling the small cabin with the acrid stench of melted shellac. The telegraph bell gives one violent, mournful clang before falling permanently silent, its copper coils fused into a useless lump of slag. You nurse your burned fingers in the dark, poorer by a length of wire but none the worse for the abrupt failure.

nodes.title: The Click of Truth
nodes.brief: Rewiring the electric bell circuit with copper strands brings the dead telegraph back to clicking life.
nodes.page:
Copper coils hum and settle as the restored current flows through the telegraph armature with a sharp, rhythmic chatter. The tiny brass lever taps out a steady sequence, bringing the dead line back to life despite the surrounding decay.

You pocket the resulting prize, knowing how narrowly you salvaged the connection from the soot-clogged terminals.

exits.label: Climb back down into the tender

nodes.title: Iron from the Ash
nodes.brief: Kicking open a jammed fire-door in the cabin base secures a heavy iron poker for the engine firebox.
nodes.page:
Shivering in the drafty recess of the cabin base, you set your boots against the jammed iron fire-door and throw your weight behind the push. It gives with a sharp, protesting shriek of rusted hinges, falling inward to reveal a thick, soot-blackened poker forged from solid boiler iron.

You haul the heavy tool free from the debris, testing its balance in your soot-stained grip before climbing back toward the deck plates.

nodes.title: Heaving the Iron Door
nodes.brief: Kicking open a jammed fire-door in the cabin base secures a heavy iron poker for the engine firebox.
nodes.page:
Resistance meets your every muscle as you lean your full weight into the warped iron frame, sweat cutting clean channels through the grime on your face. The frozen latch refuses to budge, holding fast against the dead-bolted seal while the cold wind howls through the gaps in the timber walls.

You brace your boots deeper into the ash-strewn flooring, drawing on every ounce of muscle to force the barrier open against the grip of rust.

check.label: Throw your weight against the iron door

nodes.title: The Wrenched Shoulder
nodes.brief: Kicking open a jammed fire-door in the cabin base secures a heavy iron poker for the engine firebox.
nodes.page:
A sudden slip sends your shoulder crashing violently into the iron jamb, driving the wind from your lungs in a sharp, ragged gasp. The jammed door remains obstinately shut, leaving you nursing a bruised joint and a deep, throbbing ache that settles heavily into your bones.

You shake off the dizziness, wiping sweat and grey dust from your forehead as you prepare to tackle the stubborn obstacle once more.

exits.label: Pick yourself up and try again

nodes.title: The Prize Within
nodes.brief: Kicking open a jammed fire-door in the cabin base secures a heavy iron poker for the engine firebox.
nodes.page:
Clearing the rust flakes aside, you slide your fingers into the recess and draw out a long iron poker stamped with the authentic mark of the Ashgate foundries. It is cold to the touch yet carries a reassuring weight, promising many hours of hard service at the firebox mouth.

You slide the implement into the deck rack, securing a valuable asset for the long miles ahead across the barren steppe.

exits.label: Return to the main engine deck

nodes.title: Crossing the Ridge
nodes.brief: The engine crests the ridge with a victorious whistle, leaving the grey ash-stepped wilderness behind as the great viaduct looms ahead.
nodes.page:
Steam hisses from the relief valves as Locomotive No. 9 gathers its remaining strength and begins the long, arduous climb toward the crest of the final ridge. Below you, the vast, grey expanse of the Ashen Steppe rolls away into the smoke-choked horizon, a desolate wasteland of stalled carcasses and grey grass-stubble.

With a final, triumphant shriek of the whistle, the engine breaks over the summit and begins its descent toward the lowlands. Far ahead, cutting sharply across the ash-dunes, the monumental iron spans of the Brasswind Viaduct loom through the yellow haze, their gantries bristling with the watchful lanterns of the Rail Barons.

exits.label: Crawl onto the great iron spans

nodes.title: Wits Across the Wire
nodes.brief: Matching wits with the eccentric telegraph clerk wins a brass pocket-compass that points toward magnetic north.
nodes.page:
Exchanging sharp, coded pleasantries with the weary operator across the desk, you match his dry humor with a steady stream of trackside gossip. He yields with a grudging grin and slides a brass pocket-compass across the scarred wood of the counter.

The needle spins lazily before settling true, pointing an unwavering finger toward magnetic north through the thick cabin air.

nodes.title: The Heat of Devotion
nodes.brief: Enduring the blistering heat of the prayer-fire without flinching wins the zealots trust and a heavy tin of fire-clay.
nodes.page:
Standing motionless within the blinding halo of the prayer-fire, you endure the searing wave of dry heat without flinching under the watchful gazes of the robed zealots. One of the elders nods slowly, recognizing your endurance, and presses a heavy tin of dense fire-clay into your open palm.

The sealant will patch the worst of the boiler leaks when the pressure climbs too high on the downgrade.

exits.label: Secure the tin and turn away

nodes.title: Whispers on the Line
nodes.brief: Decoding a flickering telegraph message about patrol movements earns an advance warning of Rail Baron blockades.
nodes.page:
The receiver clicks rhythmically in the dim light as you parse the fractured sequence of dashes and dots detailing armored patrols moving along the southern embankment. It is a vital advance warning of the blockades waiting near the lower junctions.

You memorize the sequence before clearing the slate, stepping back into the drafty corridor with your mind sharp and prepared.

exits.label: Head back to the cab deck

nodes.title: Greasing the Sheaves
nodes.brief: Greasing the rusted cable pulleys in the freezing wind lowers the jammed semaphore and earns a brass lantern.
nodes.page:
Frigid winds whip across the open scaffolding as you work tallow deep into the frozen cable pulleys of the upper signal bracket, your fingers numb against the metal. With a sharp groan, the rusted iron arm yields to your leverage and drops cleanly into the clear position.

A heavy brass signal-lantern, left behind by a vanished tender crew, hangs securely from the newly greased bracket as your reward.

nodes.title: The Grease Tin
nodes.brief: Sneak past the card-playing gangers to swipe a tin of beef fat without starting a brawl, earning an extra ration of cylinder oil.
nodes.page: Heavy canvas flaps snap in the sulfurous gale while you sidestep the circle of card-playing gangers hunched near the banked boiler. Their attention remains fixed on greasy cardboard tokens and disputed tallies of coal-scraps. Your fingers close around the dented rim of a tallow tin sitting half-concealed beneath an overturned crate. Slipping it into your coat pocket without a clink, you earn a rich, yellow paste of beef fat destined for the sliding rods of the valve-gear.

exits.label: Slide back into the coal dust

nodes.title: The Hoist Crank
nodes.brief: Repairing the crank on a smuggler's hoist earns an iron pry-bar for opening stuck bulkhead doors.
nodes.page: Rusted chains groan overhead as you lean your weight against the jammed iron spindle of a smuggler's cargo lift. Grit grinds inside the bronze housing until a sharp crack signals the gears finally biting home. The winch spins true once more, earning a heavy, notched iron pry-bar tossed from the shadows by a grateful handler. This solid wedge of cold metal will serve well enough when rusted bulkhead doors refuse to yield.

nodes.title: The Shared Valve
nodes.brief: Trickling extra water into the camp boiler while no one looks lets you siphon off a double ration of drinking water.
nodes.page: Steam hisses softly from the manifold while the camp guards turn their backs to warm their mittened hands over a brazier. You slip a copper feed-tube past the outer casing of the station boiler, listening to the satisfying gurgle of stolen fluid shifting through the lines. This quiet theft fills your canteens with double the allowance of murky, iron-tasting water before anyone notices the drop in pressure.

nodes.title: The Float Valve
nodes.brief: Calibrating the cistern's brass float-valve earns a handful of copper washers and a tin of anti-friction grease.
nodes.page: Copper scale flakes off the internal wall of the roadside cistern as you tap the jammed float-valve with a brass spanner. Water surges back into the trough with a clean, steady rush that satisfies the waiting tank crews. For your trouble, the foreman drops a handful of smooth copper washers and a sealed tin of dark anti-friction grease into your open palm.

exits.label: Secure the grease and press on

nodes.title: The Stolen Stream
nodes.brief: Trickling extra water into the camp boiler while no one looks lets you siphon off a double ration of drinking water.
nodes.page: Vapor curls thickly around the makeshift encampment while the watchmen argue over a spilled tin of chicory. You drop the flexible copper line into the auxiliary injector and watch the glass gauge climb steadily as the liquid transfers. Securing a double ration of drinking water lightens your immediate worries about the dry miles waiting beyond the dunes.

nodes.title: The Blind Reciter
nodes.brief: Listening to a blind prophet recite the schedule of the dead secures a whispered password for the iron gates ahead.
nodes.page: Hooded figures sway in unison around a rusted signal-mast while a blind prophet chants timetables of trains that vanished decades ago. You pause in the drifting ash, listening closely to the rhythmic cadence until the hidden pattern of arrivals and cancellations reveals itself. That whispered sequence of platform numbers forms a secret password for the guarded iron gates ahead.

nodes.title: The Iron Spans
nodes.brief: Locomotive No. 9 crawls onto the monumental iron spans of Brasswind Viaduct as toll-inspectors flash green signal-lamps.
nodes.page: Locomotive No. 9 crawls heavily onto the monumental lattice of the Brasswind Viaduct, trembling against the sheer drop above the grey expanse. Green signal-lamps blink rhythmically from the toll-gantries high above the boiler roof, challenging your right to cross the gorge. You check the steam pressure and ease the regulator forward, feeling the massive iron bridge hum beneath the wheels as the city of tolls looms out of the blowing ash.

nodes.title: The Iron Tollhouse
nodes.brief: The Iron Tollhouse: You must negotiate the initial customs barrier where Barons demand a heavy transit duty from unregistered engines.
nodes.page:
Rust flakes from the overhead gantry as the iron gates of the customs depot groan inward. Ledger-clerks and uniformed inspectors demand transit coin from every engine that dares roll its wheels upon Baronial iron. Steam hisses from the rail-mounts while greasy ledger-pages flutter in the downdraft, and you must decide whether to slip past the inspection booths through cunning, force your way through the bottleneck with brute leverage, or gamble your last drop of patience on a dangerous bribe.

The soot-stained tracks branch off toward the high-level scaffolding and the lower maintenance pits, each route offering its own sharp hazard and potential salvation under the cold gaze of the gantry-sentinels.

exits.label: Hide extra fuel cells inside the gauge housing
Hammer a loose rivet to distract the guards
Purge auxiliary steam lines to create a blinding fog
Surrender immediately to the regiment of gantry-guards

nodes.title: The Gauge Housing
nodes.brief: You dismantle the pressure-gauge housing to hide extra fuel cells, risking discovery by suspicious clerks to earn a hidden brass token.
nodes.page: Brass screws turn sluggishly under your screwdriver as you pry open the face of the pressure-gauge housing. The cramped cavity behind the dial offers just enough space to tuck away a pair of contraband fuel cells wrapped in oily rag. You slide the metal lid back into place just as heavy boots echo against the iron decking outside.

nodes.title: Beneath the Brass Dials
nodes.brief: You dismantle the pressure-gauge housing to hide extra fuel cells, risking discovery by suspicious clerks to earn a hidden brass token.
nodes.page:
Hot oil and bitter sweat drip onto your boots as you wrench the brass housing off the pressure-gauge, your fingers working entirely by feel in the cramped, trembling gloom beneath the cab floor. Outside the narrow inspection slit, a clerk's nailed boots echo on the iron plating, pausing just long enough for your heart to hammer against your ribs like a loose piston-rod.

You slide the spare fuel cells into the dark cavity behind the copper tubing and secure the rusted plate with a swift twist of the spanner just as a fist strikes the exterior steel with a hollow, demanding clang.

exits.label: Slip away into the shadow of the gantry

nodes.title: The Housing Check
nodes.brief: You dismantle the pressure-gauge housing to hide extra fuel cells, risking discovery by suspicious clerks to earn a hidden brass token.
nodes.page: Fingers trembling slightly against the vibrating brass bezel, you work the final retaining screw into the hollowed gauge housing. Boots clatter suddenly on the gantry stairs. The noise risks exposing the hidden fuel cells tucked inside the instrument panel. You hold your breath, relying on steady hands and quick adjustments to keep the inspectors from prying too closely into your work.

check.label: Wrenching the housing shut in time

nodes.title: The Inspector's Glance
nodes.brief: You dismantle the pressure-gauge housing to hide extra fuel cells, risking discovery by suspicious clerks to earn a hidden brass token.
nodes.page: A sharp rap of a brass ruler against the instrument casing shatters your concentration as the senior clerk spots the mismatched thread on the housing bezel. You absorb a stinging reprimand and surrender a small portion of your coal stores to satisfy their suspicion before they finally wave you onward. The delay leaves your knuckles throbbing and your fuel bunkers noticeably lighter.

nodes.title: The Smuggler's Token
nodes.brief: You dismantle the pressure-gauge housing to hide extra fuel cells, risking discovery by suspicious clerks to earn a hidden brass token.
nodes.page:
Your knuckles throb with a dull, persistent ache from the cramped labor inside the housing, yet your palm closes around a small, grease-slick token stamped with the private sigil of a sympathetic track-clerk. The hazardous gamble paid off, leaving you richer by one illicit credential even as the smell of hot sulphur and Baronial tobacco thickens in the damp gantry air around the Marrowbone.

You tuck the heavy brass disc safely into your waistcoat pocket, keeping your face turned toward the steam-shrouded rails as the path ahead clears enough for a cautious advance toward the viaduct gates.

exits.label: Advance toward the gantry-guards blocking the line

nodes.title: The Rivet Hammer
nodes.brief: You hammer a loose rivet into the chassis to distract the guards, risking a snapped knuckle to secure an illicit passage permit.
nodes.page:
Heavy iron tools lie scattered across the slick metal decking of the chassis, smelling sharply of machine oil and heated coal dust. You pick up the short-peen riveting hammer, its wooden haft worn smooth by years of greasy palms and vibration. The checkpoint guards are distracted by a shouting match further down the gantry, giving you a narrow window to secure the forged permit before the inspector returns

With calculated precision, you bring the flat face of the hammer down against the protruding iron pin, driving it deep into its socket with a sharp ring that pierces the ambient hum of the viaduct engines.

exits.label: Wedge the forged permit beneath the iron plate

nodes.title: The Rivet Hammer
nodes.brief: You hammer a loose rivet into the chassis to distract the guards, risking a snapped knuckle to secure an illicit passage permit.
nodes.page:
Iron boots clatter on the overhead gantry above the Marrowbone's coal bunker, drawing close to where you crouch in the soot-stained gloom. You grip the steel hammer, line its flat face against the protruding stem of a loosened structural rivet on the chassis plate, and strike. The ringing blow reverberates through the hollow girderwork like a church bell, echoing sharply across the viaduct to draw the suspicious inspectors away from your hiding place.

Your palm slips slightly against the greasy handle as the vibration jars your forearm, threatening to betray your position with a clumsy clatter.

nodes.title: A Mismatched Blow
nodes.brief: You hammer a loose rivet into the chassis to distract the guards, risking a snapped knuckle to secure an illicit passage permit.
nodes.page: The heavy hammer glancing off the iron bolt catches your knuckles against the sharp edge of the chassis plate with a sickening crunch. Pain lances up your forearm, leaving a dark, purple bruise that throbs in time with the pulsing steam pumps. You bite back a sharp curse as the guard's footsteps halt nearby, forcing you to snatch the forged permit from the gap and dive behind a rusted fuel tender while an angry whistle blows overhead.

exits.label: Crawl back toward the firebox deck

nodes.title: The Iron Tollhouse Reward
nodes.brief: You hammer a loose rivet into the chassis to distract the guards, risking a snapped knuckle to secure an illicit passage permit.
nodes.page: Silence returns to the rusted gantry rails as the frustrated inspectors' footsteps fade down the lower platform stairs. You are alone with the rhythmic dripping of oily condensation. Your right hand aches where the hammer-jar struck your thumb bone, yet tucked securely into your belt is a small brass token stamped with the private sigil of a sympathetic track-clerk who looked the other way. It is a heavy, grease-slick disk that grants an unrecorded right of way through the lower switches.

nodes.title: Hissing Valves
nodes.brief: You purge the auxiliary steam lines to create a blinding fog, risking scalded fingers to slip past the toll-gate unnoticed.
nodes.page:
Thick plumes of grey exhaust steam billow out from beneath the engine running board, curling around the rusted iron stanchions of the viaduct like waking serpents. The acrid taste of boiled lime coats your tongue as you twist the auxiliary release valve another half-turn, feeding raw pressure into the discharge pipes. Guards cough loudly through their linen scarves on the upper gantry, their vision completely blinded by the boiling fog rolling across the tracks

You keep your hand low against the vibrating brass pipework, feeling your way blindly toward the narrow maintenance ladder.

exits.label: Climb the ladder through the steam fog

nodes.title: Scalding Mist
nodes.brief: You purge the auxiliary steam lines to create a blinding fog, risking scalded fingers to slip past the toll-gate unnoticed.
nodes.page:
Heat radiates fiercely from the leaking joint of the auxiliary pipe, turning the surrounding air into a suffocating blanket of moisture and grease. You press your sleeve against your mouth to filter out the stinging vapor, squinting through the white gloom toward the dim silhouette of the toll-gate winch. Every movement requires absolute caution, for a single slip against the hot copper tubing will leave raw, weeping blisters across your skin

You reach out a trembling hand to test the tension of the heavy iron chain blocking the line.

exits.label: Slip beneath the lowered iron chain

nodes.title: Purging the Auxiliary Lines
nodes.brief: You purge the auxiliary steam lines to create a blinding fog, risking scalded fingers to slip past the toll-gate unnoticed.
nodes.page:
Scalding mist roars through the rusted drainage cocks, wrapping the Marrowbone's flanks in a dense, artificial squall that smells of boiled grease and alkaline scale. Your bare fingers brush the shrieking brass valve-wheel, every nerve screaming as escaping vapor licks the skin while you twist it further into the red zone of pressure. Beyond the swirling white curtain, the shouting of the toll-guards turns to confused curses as iron-shod boots stumble blindly on the wooden ballast.

You lean your full weight against the shivering pipework, coaxing one final, blinding hiss from the belly of the boiler to mask your stealthy descent into the shadows.

nodes.title: A Burned Palm
nodes.brief: You purge the auxiliary steam lines to create a blinding fog, risking scalded fingers to slip past the toll-gate unnoticed.
nodes.page: A sudden surge of scalding condensate spits past the packing rings, searing across the back of your hand with a sharp, blistering agony. You snatch your arm back with a sharp gasp, dropping your grip on the valve as the pressure blows back into the cab with a deafening shriek. The steam thins just enough for a nearby guard to spot you nursing your ruined skin, forcing a frantic scramble into the shadows of the tender.

exits.label: Retreat into the smoky engine cabin

nodes.title: Fog-Born Passage
nodes.brief: You purge the auxiliary steam lines to create a blinding fog, risking scalded fingers to slip past the toll-gate unnoticed.
nodes.page: Condensation drips heavily from your eyelashes as the artificial tempest slowly dissipates over the rusted iron plating of the viaduct deck, leaving you standing safely in the damp stillness beyond the customs perimeter. Your knuckles throb with a dull, persistent ache beneath a network of raw, pink scalds, but clutched tightly in your stiffening fingers is the proof of your silent trespass. It is a damp, ink-stamped slip of flimsy paper bearing the violet seal of the Baronial Transit Office, marked valid for one unauthorized coal-tender.

exits.label: Slip back toward the main span

nodes.title: The Gantry Ultimatum
nodes.brief: A regiment of Baronial gantry-guards drops iron chains across the rails, demanding immediate surrender of the brass Water Key.
nodes.page:
Iron links drop into place with a jarring clang that carries across the suspended platforms of the viaduct. A dozen Baronial gantry-guards step out from the shadows of the signal box, their polished brass breastplates catching the weak, yellow light of the hanging oil lamps. They form an unbroken wall of authority across the rails, demanding the immediate surrender of the brass Water Key under threat of immediate confiscation

You rest your hand quietly against the warm copper of the whistle lever, measuring the distance to the dark mouth of the cut ahead.

exits.label: Defy the gantry guards and pull forward

nodes.title: The Gantry Watch
nodes.brief: The Gantry Watch: You survey the suspended platforms where armed guards inspect every passing freight car for contraband.
nodes.page:
Heavy iron gantries stretch across the roaring void of the viaduct like skeletal ribs, dripping with greasy condensate and the bitter tang of coal-gas. Armed guards pace the suspended wooden duckboards, their bayonets catching the pale glare of acetylene lamps as they inspect every passing freight car for contraband and hidden passengers. Below this iron cage, the grey abyss drops away toward invisible river-beds where old steam-boilers rust in the mud. You linger in the shadow of a water crane, weighing the risk of forging the manifests against the danger of tampering with the electric signal-boxes.

Every path forward demands a price in sweat or nerve, and the storm clock above the toll-office ticks steadily closer to zero.

nodes.title: Ink And Ambition
nodes.brief: You forge a shipping manifest using stale soot-ink, risking a handwriting discrepancy to convince officers you carry official cargo.
nodes.page: Stale soot-ink cakes the bottom of your tin cup, thick and black as lamp-black grease. You dip a split nib onto the rough, fibrous surface of a confiscated Rail Baron bill of lading, pressing lightly to mimic the stiff, bureaucratic script favored by the toll-inspectors. Outside the cramped cabin, boots crunch on the iron grating as a patrol sergeant checks seals and signatures with bored hostility. Your hand trembles slightly from the heat of the firebox and the weight of old debts, but the strokes form legible lines that might just fool an exhausted clerk.

nodes.title: The False Seal
nodes.brief: You forge a shipping manifest using stale soot-ink, risking a handwriting discrepancy to convince officers you carry official cargo.
nodes.page: Sweat stings your eyes as you slide the freshly inked manifest across the zinc-topped counter beneath the flickering gas mantle. The sergeant's thumb traces the forged stamp with lazy suspicion, his gaze lingering on the peculiar slant of the capital letters where your pen hesitated. You hold your breath, forcing your shoulders to drop while your fingers curl around the brass valve-key hidden inside your coat pocket, ready for whatever alarm might follow.

nodes.title: Smudged Carbon
nodes.brief: You forge a shipping manifest using stale soot-ink, risking a handwriting discrepancy to convince officers you carry official cargo.
nodes.page: A greasy smear of black ink ruins the forged stamp just as the sergeant leans in closer with his magnifying glass. He curses softly, sniffing the paper for the raw stench of lamp-black and saliva before slamming a heavy brass rejection stamp onto the wood. You pay for the slip with a sharp cuff across the ear that leaves your temple throbbing and a three-hour delay logged in the station ledger while they strip-search the tender. The guards shove you back toward the maintenance ladder, poorer in time and temper but still breathing.

nodes.title: Accepted at the Gate
nodes.brief: You forge a shipping manifest using stale soot-ink, risking a handwriting discrepancy to convince officers you carry official cargo.
nodes.page: The sergeant grunts and plants a greasy red thumbprint square over your imitation seal, then tosses the manifest onto the stack of cleared cargo. The iron turnstile clanks open with a protesting groan and lets you past the customs barrier into the heart of the viaduct. The ledger-ghosts let you pass without a second glance. Tucked into your waistcoat pocket now rests a damp paper slip bearing the red wax mark of the toll-office.

nodes.title: Sparks in the Box
nodes.brief: You rewire the station signal-box to flash an emergency recall, risking short-circuit sparks to force the guards to abandon their posts.
nodes.page: Wires hiss and spit blue fire inside the cast-iron housing of the junction relay as you strip back the rubber insulation with a pocket knife. The signal-box smells of ozone, hot copper, and thirty years of accumulated dust from the ash-steppes. Outside, the patrol guards grumble as the semaphore arms above begin to twitch and jerk in an erratic rhythm, signaling a fictitious line blockage three miles up the track. You need only cross the open platform while they scramble to investigate the phantom warning.

nodes.title: The Flickering Semaphore
nodes.brief: You rewire the station signal-box to flash an emergency recall, risking short-circuit sparks to force the guards to abandon their posts.
nodes.page: Red signal lamps flicker and die along the iron gantry, plunging the lower walkways into a shifting gloom of shadows and steam. Guards scramble up the ladderways with heavy iron wrenches and curses on their lips, their attention fully absorbed by the sudden electrical failure in the signal-box. You keep your head down, moving with the rhythmic clank of distant shunting engines so you blend seamlessly into the cadre of harassed track-workers.

nodes.title: Rewiring the Relay
nodes.brief: You rewire the station signal-box to flash an emergency recall, risking short-circuit sparks to force the guards to abandon their posts.
nodes.page: Bare copper wires spark against the iron casing, showering your knuckles with white-hot droplets of solder that sear the skin. You bridge the gap between the main accumulator and the emergency klaxon with a hairpin, listening for the deep, resonant hum that means the circuit is holding. One wrong touch against the damp wall will ground the charge through your own boots, bringing the full voltage of the viaduct grid down upon your nervous system.

nodes.title: A Flash of Bad Wiring
nodes.brief: You rewire the station signal-box to flash an emergency recall, risking short-circuit sparks to force the guards to abandon their posts.
nodes.page: A blinding white arc leaps from the copper terminal, snapping against your wrist with the force of a hammer-blow and charring the sleeve of your wool coat.
