The rusted mechanism shudders, catches, and finally begins to turn with a deep, rhythmic groaning sound. You wipe the greasy sweat from your forehead with a soot-stained sleeve, catching your breath in the humid air.

exits.label: Follow the turning chain deeper inward

nodes.title: The Sluice-Chain's Turn
nodes.brief: You hammer the jammed sluice-chain back onto its sprocket with a heavy brass spanner, risking a crushed knuckle, and win a heavy brass oil-can.
nodes.page: Grease coats your fingers as you feed the iron links across the rattling gear teeth. The mechanism holds true against the relentless pull of the runoff. The air grows warmer here, thick with the smell of hot lard and friction, pressing against your chest with every breath. Drops of condensation drip rhythmically from the ceiling pipes onto your cap, splashing cold against the back of your neck. Ahead, a narrow maintenance hatch stands half-open in the bulkhead, spilling a dull yellow beam of light across the slippery floor plates. You plant your boots on the vibrating iron deck and press forward into the knock of the pumps.

exits.label: Step through the open maintenance hatch

nodes.title: The Sprocket's Grip
nodes.brief: You hammer the jammed sluice-chain back onto its sprocket with a heavy brass spanner, risking a crushed knuckle, and win a heavy brass oil-can.
nodes.page: The heavy brass spanner slips against the slick, grease-coated iron link, threatening to jam the entire secondary gear train in a shriek of stripped teeth. You throw your full weight against the lever arm, straining every muscle in your back while the ancient machine groans and fights back with sudden, violent jerks. Steam vents whistle shrilly beside your ear, blinding you with a sudden wall of white heat that smells of scorching oil. Your hands burn against the cold metal as you try to force the stubborn cog into alignment before the housing cracks.

check.label: Force the jammed gear mechanism home

nodes.title: The Slipping Cog
nodes.brief: You hammer the jammed sluice-chain back onto its sprocket with a heavy brass spanner, risking a crushed knuckle, and win a heavy brass oil-can.
nodes.page: The seized cog jumps violently under your weight, striking your knuckles hard against the sharp iron housing with a dull, sickening thud. A sharp ache shoots up your forearm, leaving your fingers throbbing and stiff as you snatch your hand back from the dangerous pinch-point. Hot water splashes across your boots from a ruptured gasket nearby, soaking your woolen socks with scalding runoff before you can retreat. You nurse your bruised hand against your chest, breathing heavily through your teeth while the machinery clatters on in rhythmic mockery of your clumsy failure.

exits.label: Retreat to the main drainage platform

nodes.title: The Oily Prize
nodes.brief: You hammer the jammed sluice-chain back onto its sprocket with a heavy brass spanner, risking a crushed knuckle, and win a heavy brass oil-can.
nodes.page: Despite the raw pain in your bruised fingers, the stubborn chain finally drops into its oiled groove with a satisfying clunk. The drainage pump coughs twice, spits a cloud of gray vapor, and falls into a strong rhythm that empties the sump below. Resting on the grease-splattered deck beside the mounting bracket is a heavy brass oil-can, its spout bright and polished from careful use. You pick it up, finding it nearly full of clean machine oil that gleams faintly in the gloom.

nodes.title: The Scalding Bilge
nodes.brief: You wade into the scalding bilge-water while holding your nerve against the rising dark, and salvage a dry woollen muffler.
nodes.page: Murky water swirls around your shins, carrying flakes of grey ash and globules of waste oil from the churning turbines deeper within the vault. You pick your way across the submerged floor plates, testing for hidden gaps in the grating with the toe of your boot. A discarded woollen muffler, caked in soot and wet grime, floats near a rusted stanchion and catches on a jagged rivet. You fish it out with your free hand, wringing out the foul-smelling water before stuffing the damp cloth into your coat pocket for later warmth. The low humming of the distant dynamos vibrates through the soles of your feet.

nodes.title: The Rising Dark
nodes.brief: You wade into the scalding bilge-water while holding your nerve against the rising dark, and salvage a dry woollen muffler.
nodes.page: The water level climbs steadily around your thighs as a sudden surge from the upper sluices pours into the chamber without warning. Pitch-black shadows lengthen across the dripping brick walls, distorted by the flickering amber glow of the emergency pilot lights overhead. You press your back flat against the cold masonry, fighting down the rising panic in your chest as the roaring tide laps against your belt line. Every instinct screams at you to turn and scramble back to safety before the darkness closes in completely.

check.label: Maintain nerve against the rising dark

nodes.title: The Chilling Tide
nodes.brief: You wade into the scalding bilge-water while holding your nerve against the rising dark, and salvage a dry woollen muffler.
nodes.page: The sudden rush of icy water knocks your feet out from under you, plunging you waist-deep into the filthy bilge with a sharp gasp. Your heart hammers against your ribs as you scramble frantically for purchase on the slick, weed-choked brickwork, scraping your palms raw against the stone. The dampness penetrates your woolen coat instantly, sending a bone-deep chill through your limbs that makes your teeth chatter. You haul yourself upright with a ragged breath, coughing up foul-tasting mist while the dark water swirls around your hips like a hungry animal.

exits.label: Drag yourself onto the higher platform

nodes.title: The Dry Keepsake
nodes.brief: You wade into the scalding bilge-water while holding your nerve against the rising dark, and salvage a dry woollen muffler.
nodes.page: You keep your footing through the surge, gritting your teeth against the biting cold until the water level drops back to a manageable trickle. Clutched in your fist is the damp woollen muffler you fished from the scum, smelling faintly of coal-smoke and old wool. Despite the soaking, the thick fabric offers a welcome layer of insulation against the raw draft howling through the drainage tunnel. You wrap it tightly around your neck, feeling its dry warmth begin to thaw the chill in your bones.

nodes.title: The Narrow Culvert
nodes.brief: You crawl through the narrow drainage culvert while choking soot fills the air, maintaining your composure, and find a hidden cache of tallow candles.
nodes.page:
Choking soot fills the air in a thick, greasy cloud as you push yourself forward into the cramped masonry of the drainage culvert. Your breath comes shallow and hot against your collar while you keep your composure amid the dripping rust and darkness. Groping along the slick stone floor, your fingers brush against a dry, bundled parcel wedged behind a supporting strut. You pull it free to discover a hidden cache of tallow candles, perfectly dry and smelling faintly of mutton fat.

Tucking the candles securely inside your jacket, you peer through the gloom toward the end of the tunnel where a faint, watery glow flickers against the wet brickwork. You press onward through the soot.

nodes.title: Smoke and Control
nodes.brief: You crawl through the narrow drainage culvert while choking soot fills the air, maintaining your composure, and find a hidden cache of tallow candles.
nodes.page: Thick, acrid smoke pours from the ruptured flue overhead, burning your throat and blurring your vision as you try to maintain your composure in the suffocating dark. You steady your breathing against the panic rising in your chest, reaching blindly along the hot brick wall for the emergency vent-chain while the ceiling groans above you. The air turns nearly solid with sulfur and soot, testing every ounce of your nerve as your fingers brush the cold iron link. You tighten your grip on the chain, bracing yourself for the sudden release of trapped steam.

check.label: Hold your nerve against the smoke

nodes.title: The Cost of Panic
nodes.brief: You crawl through the narrow drainage culvert while choking soot fills the air, maintaining your composure, and find a hidden cache of tallow candles.
nodes.page: The choking air defeats your resolve, and a sudden, violent fit of coughing breaks your concentration just as you reach for the vent-chain. You stumble backward into a heap of sharp scrap metal, scraping your forearm deep enough to draw a bright bead of blood through the soot. The precious minutes slip away in the haze while you catch your breath and bind the stinging scratch with a strip of oily rag. You emerge into the dim service corridor bruised and short of breath, carrying a fresh scar from the pit.

exits.label: Pick yourself up and press on

nodes.title: Steadfast in the Smokes
nodes.brief: You crawl through the narrow drainage culvert while choking soot fills the air, maintaining your composure, and find a hidden cache of tallow candles.
nodes.page: You take the choking air in measured breaths and keep your composure while soot swirls hard around your ears. You secure the venting valve with a firm, practiced pull, letting the noxious pressure bleed off safely into the lower drains. As the air clears just enough to see, a small tin box tumbles from a rusted bracket above, landing squarely at your feet with a hollow clink. You pocket the prize, knowing it will serve you well in the dark days ahead.

nodes.title: The Pressure Pit
nodes.brief: You stare down the twitching pressure gauges in the dark pit, waiting for the needle to settle, and earn the silent nod of an old drainage-man.
nodes.page:
You stare down the twitching pressure gauges in the dark pit, waiting for the needle to settle as the copper pipes hiss a warning song of superheated steam. Beside you, an old drainage-man in a grease-stained canvas coat watches the brass dial with heavy, tired eyes. The needle finally drops back into the safe green arc with a dull metallic click. The old man offers a silent nod of hard-won respect, acknowledging that you know how to hold a boiler's life in your hands.

Nodding back to the grey-haired worker, you turn away from the pit and follow the narrow walkway deeper into the subterranean maze.

nodes.title: The Silent Watcher
nodes.brief: You stare down the twitching pressure gauges in the dark pit, waiting for the needle to settle, and earn the silent nod of an old drainage-man.
nodes.page:
Deep within the concrete pit, you watch the erratic twitching of the pressure gauges while the damp air grows heavy with the scent of hot oil and old river silt. The iron needle trembles on the edge of the red zone before slowly settling back as the relief valve kicks in with a shudder. An old drainage-man standing in the shadows leans on his long-handled wrench and gives you a slow, silent nod of approval. Without a word spoken between you, he points a soot-blackened finger toward a narrow maintenance stair leading upward.

You leave the quiet pit behind and climb the steep iron steps toward the upper levels.

nodes.title: Watching the Needle
nodes.brief: You stare down the twitching pressure gauges in the dark pit, waiting for the needle to settle, and earn the silent nod of an old drainage-man.
nodes.page: Sweat cuts pale channels through the soot on your face as you stare down the twitching pressure gauges in the dark pit, waiting for the needle to settle below the danger line. The brass housing vibrates with a high, thin whine that sets your teeth on edge while the copper pipes groan under the strain of the rising flood. An old drainage-man watches from the shadows, his expression unreadable behind a thick mask of coal dust. You reach out a trembling hand toward the main bypass valve, needing absolute calm to turn it without snapping the rusted spindle.

check.label: Wait for the gauge to settle

nodes.title: A Slip in the Pit
nodes.brief: You stare down the twitching pressure gauges in the dark pit, waiting for the needle to settle, and earn the silent nod of an old drainage-man.
nodes.page: The screech of the overstressed brass dial breaks your focus just as you reach for the valve, and your hand slips on the greasy metal spindle. A sudden jet of scalding steam hisses past your knuckles, blistering your skin and forcing you to leap backward into the filthy bilge water. The old drainage-man shakes his head in silence, tossing you a greasy rag as you nurse your burned hand. You lose precious minutes wringing out your soaked coat and binding the angry red welt on your palm before you can resume your work.

exits.label: Tend your burn and move on

nodes.title: The Steady Hand
nodes.brief: You stare down the twitching pressure gauges in the dark pit, waiting for the needle to settle, and earn the silent nod of an old drainage-man.
nodes.page: You keep your grip on the screaming gauges until the trembling needle finally slips back into the safe zone with a dull thud. The old drainage-man lets out a low whistle through his teeth and offers a silent, grudging nod of respect for your nerve. As you step away from the vibrating panel, he presses a heavy iron token into your palm - a stamped brass check from the old Ashgate line, polished bright by years of carrying. It feels cool and solid against your skin.

nodes.title: The Choked Grate
nodes.brief: You clear the choked intake grate with a hooked poker, avoiding a dangerous pressure surge, and keep a heavy iron shackle-bolt.
nodes.page:
Sludge and matted river-weeds choke the drainage intake grate, threatening to back up the entire runoff channel with filthy grey water. You wedge a hooked iron poker into the mesh and heave with all your weight, tearing away a thick mat of foul debris. A dangerous pressure surge bubbles up from beneath the grates, but you manage to step clear just as the foul water drains away with a loud, sucking roar. Among the discarded iron scraps left behind on the grating, you spot a heavy shackle-bolt that has been forged by hand.

You pocket the iron piece and turn your back on the cleared intake.

nodes.title: Clearing the Intake
nodes.brief: You clear the choked intake grate with a hooked poker, avoiding a dangerous pressure surge, and keep a heavy iron shackle-bolt.
nodes.page:
Working by the dull amber glow of a wall-lamp, you clear the choked intake grate with a hooked poker, scraping away layers of calcified grease and ash-grit. The stagnant water behind the barrier ripples ominously, threatening a dangerous pressure surge if you work too fast. You work with careful deliberation, letting the water trickle through in controlled bursts until the blockage breaks with a wet thud. An iron shackle-bolt rolls free from the muck at your feet, still intact and threaded with a stout nut.

You pick up the bolt and wipe the black slime from your fingers.

nodes.title: The Rusted Sluice
nodes.brief: You clear the choked intake grate with a hooked poker, avoiding a dangerous pressure surge, and keep a heavy iron shackle-bolt.
nodes.page: The iron intake grate is wedged tight with a century of calcified ash and twisted wire, blocking the drainage flow while the water behind it swells dangerously high. You wedge your hooked poker into the mesh, testing the resistance against your muscles as the entire frame groans under the hydraulic load. A sudden pressure surge threatens to blow the entire assembly outward into the tunnel, and you must use every trick of your trade to pry the bars without snapping the tool in half. You brace your boot against the masonry and throw your weight onto the handle.

nodes.title: The Broken Poker
nodes.brief: You clear the choked intake grate with a hooked poker, avoiding a dangerous pressure surge, and keep a heavy iron shackle-bolt.
nodes.page: The rusted grate refuses to yield cleanly, and the sudden pressure surge catches your poker with a violent jerk that snaps the iron shaft right at the bend. You tumble backward into the greasy silt, winded and cursing as the foul water spills over your boots. The blocked intake remains only half-cleared, leaving you with a damaged tool and a bruised shoulder to show for your trouble. You salvage what you can of the broken metal and stagger away from the flooded channel.

nodes.title: The Sluice Cleared
nodes.brief: You clear the choked intake grate with a hooked poker, avoiding a dangerous pressure surge, and keep a heavy iron shackle-bolt.
nodes.page: Iron gives way under the bite of the hooked poker, sliding free with a long metallic groan that bounces off the damp brickwork. Black sludge and grey foam rush through the widened gap, tumbling down into the sump below as the water-level drops inches in a single breath. Amidst the swirling grit, your fingers close around a thick, oil-slicked shackle-bolt dropped by some long-dead gangers. You pull your arm back and wipe soot from your forehead with a soot-stained sleeve as the drainage settles into a roaring bass note.

exits.label: Climb back up to the sump-house

nodes.title: The Chanting Stair
nodes.brief: A delegation of Cinder Prophets blocks the vaulted stair, chanting old hymns of ash and offering a charred wooden box said to hold Hesper's confession.
nodes.page: Narrow stone steps spiral upward into the soot-stained vault, choked now by a knot of figures wrapped in grey wool and ash-stained canvas. The Cinder Prophets block the climb completely, their low voices rising in a rhythmic, drone-like hymn that speaks of burnt ties and absolute forgiveness. One elder steps forward, pressing a charred wooden box into your hands with fingers as dry as kindling, muttering that it holds the true confession of Hesper Quill. The scent of burnt paper and old lamp-oil clings thick to the grain of the wood as you stand hemmed in by the silent, watching zealots.

nodes.title: The Ash Shrine
nodes.brief: The Ash-Shrine: A hollowed-out passenger carriage serves as a smoky temple where hooded zealots burn railway timetables in iron braziers.
nodes.page: Stripped-down passenger carriages form the walls of this smoky vault, where iron braziers cast long, shivering shadows across rusted iron ribs and floorboards. Hooded figures tend the small fires, feeding torn strips of ancient railway timetables to the flames while acrid smoke collects against the curved ceiling. Every corner smells of dry dust and charred parchment, humming with the low murmur of prayers addressed to the iron line. From here, narrow service ladders and dark passages lead further into the heart of the terminus.

nodes.title: Words in the Soot
nodes.brief: You listen patiently to the high priest's rambling sermon about the cleansing fire, keeping your temper in check, and receive a blessed charcoal amulet.
nodes.page: Standing before the high pulpit, you endure the endless drone of the chief priest without losing your grip on the heavy brass key in your pocket. The speaker's sermon weaves through stories of the great fire that cleared the steppes, praising the purification of iron and the absolute justice of the ash. You nod at measured intervals, showing just enough deference to keep the hostile crowd from closing in. When the sermon finally trails off into a raspy cough, the priest shoves a small, soot-darkened lump into your palm as a token of uncertain truce.

nodes.title: The Smoldering Pew
nodes.brief: You listen patiently to the high priest's rambling sermon about the cleansing fire, keeping your temper in check, and receive a blessed charcoal amulet.
nodes.page: Ash drifts down from the iron ribs overhead like grey snow, settling into the creases of your coat as you move past rows of discarded compartment benches. A solitary zealot sits sharpening a piece of scrap iron against the floorboards, pausing only to watch you with eyes white against soot-stained cheeks. The air grows noticeably warmer here, thick with the smell of scorched upholstery and the distant, rhythmic throb of the reservoir pumps below. You keep your hand near your pocket, stepping carefully around a pile of smoldering railway manifests.

nodes.title: Silence in the Firestorm
nodes.brief: You listen patiently to the high priest's rambling sermon about the cleansing fire, keeping your temper in check, and receive a blessed charcoal amulet.
nodes.page: Sparks flare suddenly from a nearby brazier as a sudden draft rushes down the ventilation flue, showering red embers across the dry wooden floorboards right at your feet. The assembled crowd surges forward with a collective hiss of indrawn breath, their hungry eyes fixed on your coat and the heavy brass key hidden beneath it. Your pulse hammers hard against your ribs, but you force your limbs to remain completely still amidst the mounting panic, locking your jaw against the rising tide of heat and shouting.

check.label: Maintain steady composure against the sudden panic

nodes.title: The Smoke Breaks Through
nodes.brief: You listen patiently to the high priest's rambling sermon about the cleansing fire, keeping your temper in check, and receive a blessed charcoal amulet.
nodes.page: A sudden lungful of bitter ash catches in your throat, tearing a ragged cough from your chest that shatters your hard-won calm. The crowd surges inward before you can recover your footing, shoving you hard against the jagged iron ribs of a burned-out carriage wall. Your shoulder takes the impact with a sickening crunch, leaving a dull, throbbing ache and tearing your sleeve from wrist to elbow. You stumble away into the gloom, clutching your bruised arm while the zealots jeer from the smoke.

exits.label: Pick yourself up from the floor

nodes.title: Through the Smoke
nodes.brief: You listen patiently to the high priest's rambling sermon about the cleansing fire, keeping your temper in check, and receive a blessed charcoal amulet.
nodes.page: Footsteps ring hollow on the metal floor as you leave the turbulent alcove and the angry crowd behind. Bruised ribs and a raw throat mark what hesitation costs under these low, smoke-stained vaults. Your hand closes reassuringly around a smooth, blessed charcoal amulet tucked safely into your lining, its surface cool despite the ambient heat. Ahead of you, the dim light of the central shrine flickers across the tracks, drawing you toward the final ascent.

nodes.title: Sparks on the Altar
nodes.brief: You rewire the smoking altar-lamp before the sparks catch the dry wreaths, burning your fingertips, and pocket a heavy brass crucifix-wrench.
nodes.page: Exposed copper wires spit pale blue sparks across a heap of dry funeral wreaths, threatening to turn the whole provisional altar into a roaring fire-trap. You drop to your knees in the choking dark, fingers working fast to twist the live leads apart before the flames can catch. A sudden bright flash bites deep into your fingertips, searing the skin with a sharp, white-hot sting that leaves your hands trembling. Wiping the blood on your trousers, you pry a heavy brass crucifix-wrench loose from the mounting plate and pocket it.

exits.label: Move away from the sputtering altar

nodes.title: The Live Wire
nodes.brief: You rewire the smoking altar-lamp before the sparks catch the dry wreaths, burning your fingertips, and pocket a heavy brass crucifix-wrench.
nodes.page: Bare copper snakes across the wet iron framework of the altar-lamp, hissing softly as stray moisture shorts out the circuit in a shower of violet sparks. The brass crucifix-wrench stretches in your hands as you try to wedge the live lead away from the timber frame before the whole structure goes up in flames. The metal tool vibrates violently in your grip, humming with a dangerous current that threatens to jump straight through your gloves at any second.

check.label: Rewire the live circuit without grounding yourself

nodes.title: The Bitter Shock
nodes.brief: You rewire the smoking altar-lamp before the sparks catch the dry wreaths, burning your fingertips, and pocket a heavy brass crucifix-wrench.
nodes.page: A violent shock runs up your forearms, throwing you backward onto the iron grating with a choked cry as the wrench sparks brightly. The smell of burned leather and singed hair fills your nose, and your right hand hangs limp and numb, stinging fiercely from fingertip to palm. You lie there for a long moment watching soot drift down through the pale beam of a distant signal-lamp, gathering your breath before you manage to push yourself up.

exits.label: Gather your tools and move on

nodes.title: The Wrench Secured
nodes.brief: You rewire the smoking altar-lamp before the sparks catch the dry wreaths, burning your fingertips, and pocket a heavy brass crucifix-wrench.
nodes.page: Cool brass rests in your coat pocket, clear of the sputtering altar wiring that nearly fried your fingers. The small burn on your palm throbs in rhythm with your pulse, a dull reminder of how thin the margin is between a functioning engine and a heap of scrap. Around you, the murmur of the Cinder Prophets rises and falls like distant surf against a shingle beach. You grip the cold metal of your rail-pass and step past the smoking woodwork toward the wider corridor.

nodes.title: Pouch of Dried Leaves
nodes.brief: You spin a clever tale about the engine's sacred duty to the line, convincing the elders, and obtain a pouch of dried bitter-leaf.
nodes.page: Smoke hangs low beneath the soot-blackened rafters while the elders murmur among themselves, squinting through the haze at your grease-stained coat. You lean against a scarred timber pillar and spin a careful tale about the engine's sacred duty to the iron line, invoking old timetables and the binding weight of ancient debts. Gradually, the skepticism in their lined faces softens into grudging respect for a fellow traveler of the rails. One of the robed figures reaches into a leather sack and produces a small, coarse pouch filled with dried bitter-leaf, thrusting it into your calloused palm.

exits.label: Take the leaf and press onward

nodes.title: The Elder Council
nodes.brief: You spin a clever tale about the engine's sacred duty to the line, convincing the elders, and obtain a pouch of dried bitter-leaf.
nodes.page: Shadows flicker across the rough-hewn benches as you weave a plausible story regarding the engine's vital mission to keep the line moving through the encroaching ash-storm. The senior elder leans forward, his milky eye catching the dull glow of the brazier, weighing every word against the bitter memory of broken promises and abandoned depots. You must draw upon your sharpest wits and quickest tongue to maintain the illusion of absolute authority before the council picks apart your narrative and demands to see your clearance papers.

check.label: Talk your way past the elders

nodes.title: A Costly Deception
nodes.brief: You spin a clever tale about the engine's sacred duty to the line, convincing the elders, and obtain a pouch of dried bitter-leaf.
nodes.page: Your tongue trips under the unforgiving gaze of the council elders, and the thread of your story snaps mid-sentence. Someone scoffs from the back of the carriage, and an iron poker jabs toward your ribs to drive you out into the soot and cold. You scramble backward over a stack of discarded luggage, scraping your knuckles raw against a rusted bracket while the bitter-leaf pouch is snatched away by a greedy hand. You limp out into the grey corridor with a throbbing wrist and a lighter pocket, nursing your bruises in the gloom.

nodes.title: The Bitter Leaf Secured
nodes.brief: You spin a clever tale about the engine's sacred duty to the line, convincing the elders, and obtain a pouch of dried bitter-leaf.
nodes.page: The council accepts your sacred purpose, and the transaction closes with a hard thump of approval on the bench. You slip the coarse pouch into your inner pocket, feeling the dry rustle of the leaves against your ribs as a reminder of the narrow escape. The elders turn back to their cold braziers without another word, leaving you free to navigate the smoky aisles back toward the waiting iron.

nodes.title: The Broken Burner
nodes.brief: You repair the broken copper incense-burner with a quick tap of the hammer, preventing a panic, and secure a bundle of resinous pine-splints.
nodes.page: Sparks dance across the iron floor as the copper incense-burner splters and threatens to shower the assembled crowd with burning embers. With practiced speed, you draw your heavy workshop hammer and deliver a sharp, precise tap to the dented rim, reseating the loose metal just as a murmur of alarm begins to rise among the travelers. The flame settles back into a smoky glow, and the travelers stop rising toward panic in the confined carriage. A grateful attendant shoves a bundle of resinous pine-splints into your arms as a token of thanks.

exits.label: Secure the splints and move on

nodes.title: The Rusted Incense
nodes.brief: You repair the broken copper incense-burner with a quick tap of the hammer, preventing a panic, and secure a bundle of resinous pine-splints.
nodes.page: The copper burner shudders violently in your grip, venting a jet of black smoke that threatens to choke the narrow compartment while the surrounding passengers edge away in sudden terror. You must rely entirely on your precise knowledge of riveted seams and heat expansion to strike the fractured casing in the exact right spot before the entire vessel ruptures and scatters live coals across the wooden floorboards.

nodes.title: The Smoking Ruin
nodes.brief: You repair the broken copper incense-burner with a quick tap of the hammer, preventing a panic, and secure a bundle of resinous pine-splints.
nodes.page: The hammer blow lands a fraction too hard, splitting the fatigued copper seam wide open and showering your boots with sparks and hot ash. You curse under your breath as smoke billows thick and blinding through the cramped carriage, driving the panicked passengers out into the freezing draft of the corridor. You salvage what you can from the smoking ruin, coughing violently and nursing a nasty burn across your knuckles, leaving the wrecked burner behind in the haze.

nodes.title: Resinous Pine Splints
nodes.brief: You repair the broken copper incense-burner with a quick tap of the hammer, preventing a panic, and secure a bundle of resinous pine-splints.
nodes.page: The fractured burner settles, and the crisis fades into a manageable hiss of escaping steam and curling smoke. You sweep the remaining debris into a corner with your boot and tuck the bundle of resinous pine-splints securely beneath your arm, feeling their sticky weight against your jacket. The grateful attendant nods silently from the shadows, granting you passage through the crowded aisle without further delay.

nodes.title: The Final Bronze Door
nodes.brief: The Stationmaster-General blocks the final bronze door to the Water Gate, her pocket-watch ticking like a death-clock in the quiet gloom.
nodes.page: The Stationmaster-General bars the way before the massive bronze portal of the Water Gate, her ancient frame wrapped in wool and grease-stained ribbons of office. Her silver pocket-watch rests upon an upturned crate between you, ticking with a cold, metronomic persistence that seems to swallow the distant roar of the gathering ash-storm. She does not look up as you approach, her bony fingers resting lightly upon the heavy iron ring of her keys as if the passage of time itself were hers to command. The low groan of stressed metal echoes through the vaulted chamber overhead, warning that the storm clock is running down to its final ticks.

exits.label: Step forward to face the stationmaster

nodes.title: The Cinderfall Terminus
nodes.brief: The Final Platform: The high, vaulted terminus echoes with the whistle of the inbound storm, and every faction waits in the shadows for the outcome.
nodes.page: The vast, arched roof of the terminus shudders under the rising howl of the wind, trapping the smell of hot brass, old coal-dust, and impending disaster in the high rafters. Down on the oil-slicked platforms, every faction lingers in the gloom like dark birds waiting for the last signal to drop. The massive doors loom at the far end of the tracks, while emergency lights flicker and die one by one against the encroaching dark. Every shadow hides a watchful eye, and every choice pulls you deeper into the final reckoning of the line.

exits.label: Adjust the main feed valve overhead

nodes.title: The Hissing Generator
nodes.brief: You patch a ruptured steam line on the emergency generator under a hail of falling soot, and secure a heavy brass cylinder-cock.
nodes.page: Flakes of soot drift down from the high iron beams and coat your shoulders in a gritty shroud as you crawl beneath the auxiliary dynamo. The emergency generator coughs, sputtering greasy smoke into the cramped recess while a fractured steam line releases a frantic, scalding jet. Blinded by the wet heat and the dark grease smearing your forehead, you reach for the spanner wedged in your belt.

nodes.title: Securing the Cock
nodes.brief: You patch a ruptured steam line on the emergency generator under a hail of falling soot, and secure a heavy brass cylinder-cock.
nodes.page: Scalding mist billows around your knuckles, but the wrench bites hard into the stubborn threading of the brass valve-cock. With a sharp wrench and a muttered curse against the low sky, you heave your weight against the iron bar until the leaking joint groans and holds. The shriek of escaping vapour dwindles to a wet, disgruntled hiss, leaving only the smell of hot oil and scorched copper in the gloom.

exits.label: Crawl back from the dynamo recess

nodes.title: The Final Valve-Turn
nodes.brief: You patch a ruptured steam line on the emergency generator under a hail of falling soot, and secure a heavy brass cylinder-cock.
nodes.page: A sudden tremor shakes the iron floorplates under your knees as the wind outside hurls another fistful of ash against the siding walls. The generator's main housing bulges, threatening to blow its gasket entirely if you do not seat the final cylinder-cock home against the rising pressure. You steady your breathing, grip the vibrating brass wheel with both palms, and commit every ounce of leverage you possess to forcing the thread straight.

check.label: Force the vibrating brass valve home

nodes.title: Scalded and Bent
nodes.brief: You patch a ruptured steam line on the emergency generator under a hail of falling soot, and secure a heavy brass cylinder-cock.
nodes.page: Hot iron bites into your palm as the valve slips sideways with a vicious screech, spraying boiling water across your sleeve and leaving a bright, angry burn along your forearm. You stagger backward out of the recess, coughing violently as the generator clanks to a sullen, limping idle. It costs you dearly in precious skin and precious minutes, but the pressure drops enough to keep the machine from tearing itself apart in the dark.

exits.label: Drag yourself clear of the wreckage

nodes.title: The Seated Seal
nodes.brief: You patch a ruptured steam line on the emergency generator under a hail of falling soot, and secure a heavy brass cylinder-cock.
nodes.page: Once the obstinate valve yields, the emergency generator settles into an even knock that travels up through the soles of your boots. You wipe the stinging sweat from your eyes with a blackened wrist, catching your breath as the metal cools just enough to touch. For your trouble, you pocket a piece of salvaged gear that will serve you in the dark days ahead.

nodes.title: The Old Woman's Gaze
nodes.brief: You weather the bitter reproaches of the ancient stationmaster without flinching, standing your ground, and win her heavy iron seal-ring.
nodes.page: The Stationmaster-General stands like a monolith of grey wool and bitter judgment, her ancient eyes fixed upon you with the unyielding weight of an expired timetable. Every harsh word she hurls carries the accumulated frost of decades spent guarding a sealed gate against desperate men. You keep your jaw set, refusing to offer the easy compliance or the frightened excuses she expects from her subordinates.

nodes.title: Standing Fast Against Reproach
nodes.brief: You weather the bitter reproaches of the ancient stationmaster without flinching, standing your ground, and win her heavy iron seal-ring.
nodes.page: Silence stretches between you like a rusted coupling under tension, broken only by the whistling gale rattling the distant glass roof. She tests your resolve with another barbed reminder of the debts owed to the line, but you hold your ground without flinching an inch. Slowly, grudgingly, the rigid lines around her thin mouth soften into something resembling exhausted respect.

exits.label: Accept the weight of her seal

nodes.title: The Test of Nerves
nodes.brief: You weather the bitter reproaches of the ancient stationmaster without flinching, standing your ground, and win her heavy iron seal-ring.
nodes.page: Her gaze bores into you like a cold drill, searching for the crack in your composure that will let her dismiss you back into the ash-dunes. You feel the temptation to look away, to break the silence with a placating murmur or a nervous shuffle of your boots against the grit. Instead, you lock your jaw, steady your breath against the rising panic in your chest, and stare straight back into those unforgiving eyes.

check.label: Hold your ground against her stare

nodes.title: Cracked Composure
nodes.brief: You weather the bitter reproaches of the ancient stationmaster without flinching, standing your ground, and win her heavy iron seal-ring.
nodes.page: Her sharp tongue cuts through your defenses like a fresh cold chisel, driving a sudden flush of hot humiliation up your neck and forcing you to blink away the stinging salt of your own frustration. You stumble slightly on your footing, losing your balance for a heartbeat before you manage to clamp your mouth shut. It leaves you bruised in pride and shaken to your core, but you refuse to yield the ground beneath your boots.

nodes.title: The Iron Token
nodes.brief: You weather the bitter reproaches of the ancient stationmaster without flinching, standing your ground, and win her heavy iron seal-ring.
nodes.page: Your stubborn endurance earns you a grudging measure of ground in her esteem. She reaches into the folds of her heavy woollen shawl and presses a cold, weighty piece of metal into your open palm with a dry, papery snap. It is a token of authority that opens doors others must batter down, carrying the silent weight of the old administration.

nodes.title: The Drafty Spans
nodes.brief: You endure the freezing draft from the breached roof-lights while adjusting the main feed-valve, and retain an oiled leather ledger-cover.
nodes.page:
High above the stone flags of the terminus, the breached roof-lights rattle in a gale straight off the Cinder Steppe, spilling freezing drafts down your neck as you reach for the main feed-valve. Frost rimes the copper seams and turns the metal slick under your calloused fingers, so you keep a firm grip and a level head while the wind's shriek climbs. Tucked safely inside your greasy boiler-jacket, the oiled leather ledger-cover presses against your ribs like a flat, dry shield, keeping the damp at bay while the great hall groans in iron agony around you.

Stepping carefully across the vibrating iron walkway, you test the securing bolts on the auxiliary pipework, listening for any sign of a pressure drop that might betray the engine's labored rhythm to the watchers below.

nodes.title: Adjusting The Feed
nodes.brief: You endure the freezing draft from the breached roof-lights while adjusting the main feed-valve, and retain an oiled leather ledger-cover.
nodes.page:
Frost continues to coat the overhead ribs of the station skeleton, but your attention remains fixed on the brass wheel of the main feed-valve, which turns with a deep, protesting grind of dry threads. A sudden gust billows through the broken panes overhead, carrying the bitter taste of old soot and frozen alkali straight into your teeth, yet your hands keep their hold on the spoke. Against your chest, the stiff edges of the oiled leather ledger-cover shift with every breath, reminding you of the records you carry through the gathering storm.

Pausing to wipe a smear of black grease from your brow, you peer through the dim haze toward the distant platform edge where the shadows bunch thickest.

nodes.title: Keeping A Steady Head
nodes.brief: You endure the freezing draft from the breached roof-lights while adjusting the main feed-valve, and retain an oiled leather ledger-cover.
nodes.page: Bitter drafts whistle through the shattered glass above, biting deep into your fingers as you work the main feed-valve to keep the stubborn boiler from choking on the rising cold. A sudden clatter of loose slate from the roof-lights startles the shadows below, and out of the corner of your eye you catch the glint of brass buttons shifting in the gloom, waiting for any sign that your resolve is slipping. You clamp your teeth together, forcing your breathing into a slow, measured rhythm while your hand stays clamped to the metal wheel, shielding the oiled leather ledger-cover pressed tight against your ribs.

check.label: Keep your nerve against the cold

nodes.title: The Bitter Frostbite
nodes.brief: You endure the freezing draft from the breached roof-lights while adjusting the main feed-valve, and retain an oiled leather ledger-cover.
nodes.page: The sudden screech of twisting iron overhead breaks your concentration, sending a sharp shiver through your arms that wrenches the main feed-valve too far to the left, flooding the chamber with scalding steam and bitter damp. As you stumble backward against the bulkhead, a jagged edge of the breached roof-frame catches your shoulder, tearing through your canvas coat. A long welt burns like hot coal along the cut. The loss of precious moments leaves your chest aching and your temper frayed, but you drag yourself upright with a dry cough, clutching the damp leather ledger-cover tighter as the engine settles into a heavy, uneven cough.

exits.label: Drag yourself upright and move on

nodes.title: Through The Draft
nodes.brief: You endure the freezing draft from the breached roof-lights while adjusting the main feed-valve, and retain an oiled leather ledger-cover.
nodes.page: Whether you weathered the biting gale with steady hands or fought your way through the sudden shriek of freezing air, you manage to secure the main feed-valve before the pressure dips into dangerous ground. The oiled leather ledger-cover remains tucked securely against your ribs, its stiff corners dry and intact despite the biting frost that coats the rest of the ironwork. With the valve locked into position, you catch your breath in the dim gloom and feel a hard knot of stubborn pride settle in your chest as the platform looms closer through the haze.

nodes.title: Shadows On The Siding
nodes.brief: You trick the remaining platform guards into checking the wrong siding with a false whistle-signal, and pocket a heavy silver pocket-watch.
nodes.page:
Slipping past the silent coal hoppers, you pull a short, sharp blast from the brass signal-whistle hung at your hip, mimicking the distinct code of an incoming ballast train. The remaining platform guards instantly snap to attention in the gloom, turning their lanterns toward the deserted dead-end siding on the far side of the yards where the echo dies against the rusted buffer-stops. While their backs are turned and their boots crunch hurriedly across the gravel toward the phantom noise, you drop flat against the side of the tender and slip your fingers into the unattended watchman box.

Beside an empty tin cup sits a silver pocket-watch, its cold metal ticking slow defiance of the dead air around you.

nodes.title: The False Alarm
nodes.brief: You trick the remaining platform guards into checking the wrong siding with a false whistle-signal, and pocket a heavy silver pocket-watch.
nodes.page:
Echoes of your false whistle still hang in the cold air above the tracks, drawing the remaining platform guards further down the line toward the wrong siding with shouts of rough annoyance. You crouch low behind a rusted coal-tender, letting the confusion swallow the sound of your boots as you sweep your hand across the deserted watchman desk. Your fingers brush against a heavy silver pocket-watch left behind in the scramble, its hinged case cold and weighty as you lift it into the safety of your coat pocket.

Waiting until the last bobbing lantern disappears into the foggy distance, you stand up straight and check the clear strip of track ahead.

exits.label: Step out onto the clear track

nodes.title: A Risky Diversion
nodes.brief: You trick the remaining platform guards into checking the wrong siding with a false whistle-signal, and pocket a heavy silver pocket-watch.
nodes.page: False whistles echo off the rusted iron sheds, drawing the remaining guards away from the main platform, but one broad-shouldered watchman hesitates and turns his lantern back toward your hiding place with a suspicious squint. You freeze against the side of the tender, holding your breath while your fingers slide silently toward the heavy silver pocket-watch resting on the watchman box, knowing that a single metallic clink or scrape of gravel will bring his boots straight down your way. The distance between you narrows as he takes a slow, deliberate step in your direction, his eyes scanning the gloom.

check.label: Trick the guard and snatch the watch

nodes.title: Caught In The Glint
nodes.brief: You trick the remaining platform guards into checking the wrong siding with a false whistle-signal, and pocket a heavy silver pocket-watch.
nodes.page: The broad watchman catches the sudden silver flash of your movement in the dark and barks an abrupt challenge, so you snatch the pocket-watch and scramble backward through a narrow gap between two rusted carriages. As you squeeze past a jagged iron latch, it tears a deep, bleeding gouge across your forearm, stealing your breath and costing you precious minutes in the shadowed maze. You bite down hard on a curse, clutching your wounded arm as you dive into the shelter of the coaling stage, leaving the angry shouts of the guard behind you in the ash-choked fog.

exits.label: Slip away into the coaling stage

nodes.title: The Silver Prize
nodes.brief: You trick the remaining platform guards into checking the wrong siding with a false whistle-signal, and pocket a heavy silver pocket-watch.
nodes.page: Whether you slipped away cleanly in the confusion or snatched the prize right from under the watchman's nose despite the sudden scrape, the heavy silver pocket-watch now rests safely in your greasy palm. Its cold, engraved casing bears the worn monogram of the Rail Barons' logistics branch, a neat little piece of stolen property that might buy you a moment of hesitation from the gate guards if played just right. With the watch tucked securely into your waistcoat, you turn your face toward the vaulted arches of the terminus where the final platform waits.

nodes.title: The Rule of Ink
nodes.brief: You outwit the stationmaster's clerk with a swift reading of the old railway rule-book, and claim a signed bill of indemnity.
nodes.page: The clerk's fountain pen hovers above the ledger like a dead crane's leg, twitching at every rattle of distant rolling stock. You slide the dog-eared manual across the grease-stained counter, pointing a soot-blackened finger directly at Paragraph Twelve of the Emergency Transit Act of Ninety-Four. He squints through thick, grease-smeared spectacles, his thin lips moving silently as he traces the obsolete clauses regarding emergency cargo clearance. The weight of your silence presses heavily against the small wicket window until he finally mutters a curse beneath his breath. With a sharp scratch of steel nib on yellowed parchment, he scrawls his signature across the bill of indemnity and slams an iron stamp into the wax. You snatch the paper before the ink can dry, tucking the cold proof of passage securely into your waistcoat pocket as the platform bell tolls once for departure.

exits.label: Slip away into the gathering steam

nodes.title: Ink and Iron Law
nodes.brief: You outwit the stationmaster's clerk with a swift reading of the old railway rule-book, and claim a signed bill of indemnity.
nodes.page: Pages flutter like trapped sparrows under the clerk's nervous fingers as you lay the open manual flat upon the counter, pressing down hard on the binding with your knuckles. The binding cracks with a dry snap that mimics a distant rail-joint breaking under frost, silencing the petty clerk's rising objections before they can take root in the stale air. You trace a soot-darkened nail along the margin notes scribbled by some long-dead superintendent, demanding the immediate issuance of the mandated indemnity. Defeated by the iron logic of the text, he dips his pen and scratches his signature across the yellowed slip.

exits.label: Pocket the signed permit and leave

nodes.title: Reading the Fine Print
nodes.brief: You outwit the stationmaster's clerk with a swift reading of the old railway rule-book, and claim a signed bill of indemnity.
nodes.page: Dust motes dance in the narrow beam of the tallow candle as you lean across the high mahogany counter, pressing the stationmaster's clerk with a rapid recitation of obscure bylaws that even the old hands have forgotten. Your voice remains low and level, cutting through the distant groan of settling ironwork and the rising whine of the wind against the eaves. Every word is weighed against the risk of an alarm, your eyes fixed on the clerk's twitching thumb as he hovers indecisively over the call-bell on his desk.

check.label: Recite the emergency clauses before he rings

nodes.title: A Costly Dispute
nodes.brief: You outwit the stationmaster's clerk with a swift reading of the old railway rule-book, and claim a signed bill of indemnity.
nodes.page: A slip of the tongue mangles a clause in the tariff code, and the clerk's face hardens from hesitation into outright defiance as he slams the wooden shutter in your face. You curse under your breath, dropping to one knee just as a brass inkwell comes flying through the high grille to shatter against the stone bulkhead beside your ear. The delay costs precious minutes in the suffocating dark, and when you finally wrench the wicket open from the side and snatch the signed paper, a sharp shard of glass has carved a bleeding crescent across the back of your hand.

exits.label: Gather your papers and press onward

nodes.title: The Stamped Indemnity
nodes.brief: You outwit the stationmaster's clerk with a swift reading of the old railway rule-book, and claim a signed bill of indemnity.
nodes.page: Whatever doubts troubled the clerk dissolve beneath the unyielding pressure of your calculated interpretation, and he signs and stamps the paper with an iron die. The parchment is thick and smells faintly of stale pipe-smoke and damp wool, but the ink is fresh and the official seal is unbroken. You tuck the precious document securely inside your waistcoat pocket, feeling its reassuring stiffness against your ribs as the distant storm growls through the iron framework of the terminus roof.

exits.label: Take the slip and move deeper

nodes.title: The Outer Terminal
nodes.brief: The storm strikes the glass roof with the roar of a thousand shovels, plunging the terminus into absolute darkness save for the glow of the firebox.
nodes.page:
Gale-force ash strikes the high glass roof of the grand terminus with the deafening roar of a thousand shovels emptying coal into an iron tender, plunging the cavernous platforms into absolute twilight. Only the cherry-red glare of the Marrowbone's firebox keeps the immediate darkness at bay, casting long, writhing shadows across the stacked crates of abandoned baggage and rusted signal gantries. The air tastes of sulphur and wet soot, sticking to the roof of your mouth with every labored breath you draw in the freezing draft.

Somewhere above, in the iron rafters, a loose sheet of corrugated iron screeches against its bolts like an injured animal, while ahead lies the final descent to the bronze pillar of the Water Gate. Every muscle in your back aches from the long run, and the storm clock ticks down its final merciless minutes in the engine's housing.

exits.label: Approach the bronze pillar with purpose

nodes.title: Through the Culvert
nodes.brief: You crawl through the narrow drainage culvert while choking soot fills the air, maintaining your composure, and find a hidden cache of tallow candles.
nodes.page: Narrow and black as a boiler flue, the drainage culvert offers a desperate passage beneath the sprawling weight of the administrative offices while the ash-storm batters the corrugated iron above. You drop to hands and knees, crawling through a gritty soup of old coal-dust and grease while keeping your breathing slow and even to conserve the stale air in your lungs. Your fingers brush against something cold and cylindrical tucked behind a limestone block, revealing a small bundle of dry tallow candles wrapped in oily rag.

exits.label: Crawl on with the dry candles

nodes.title: The Ancient Stationmaster
nodes.brief: You weather the bitter reproaches of the ancient stationmaster without flinching, standing your ground, and win her heavy iron seal-ring.
nodes.page: Granite-faced and smelling of dry tea and coal-smoke, the old woman who rules this terminal branch sits behind a barricade of ledgers that reach almost to the soot-stained ceiling. You stand your ground against her bitter, rattling reproaches without shifting your weight, letting her sharp tongue wear itself out against your stubborn silence like waves against a breakwater. At last, seeing that neither threats nor insults will dislodge you, she pulls a heavy iron seal-ring from her wrinkled thumb and drops it onto the blotter with a dull thud.

nodes.title: The Watchmaker's Tin
nodes.brief: You ignore the screech of tearing iron in the dark sheds, keeping your breathing slow and deliberate, and pocket a small tin of watchmaker's oil.
nodes.page: Metal screeches against metal in the shadowed bays of the repair shed, but you keep your stride measured and your elbows tucked tight against your ribs, ignoring the phantom hazards in the dark. Your fingers sweep along the edge of a carpenter's workbench until they strike the familiar tin lid of a watchmaker's oil-can left behind by some vanished fitter. You lift it gently without a single metallic click, testing its weight to find it still half-full of clear, pale lubricant.

exits.label: Pocket the tin and keep moving

nodes.title: The Pressure Pit
nodes.brief: You stare down the twitching pressure gauges in the dark pit, waiting for the needle to settle, and earn the silent nod of an old drainage-man.
nodes.page: Steam hisses from a fractured seal nearby, filling the sunken inspection pit with a blinding white shroud that smells of boiled grease and old scale. You stand motionless on the iron grid, staring down at the twitching brass needle of the drainage pressure gauge until its erratic oscillations finally settle into a steady, rhythmic thrum. A stooped old drainage-man squatting in the recess watches you from beneath his grease-blackened brows, then gives a slow, wordless nod of grudging respect.

exits.label: Accept the nod and move ahead

nodes.title: The Narrow Drain
nodes.brief: You crawl through the narrow drainage culvert while choking soot fills the air, maintaining your composure, and find a hidden cache of tallow candles.
nodes.page:
Squeezing your shoulders through the iron-bound masonry of the drainage culvert, you swallow the alkaline taste of soot that coats your tongue like dry plaster. The storm rages against the surface above, but down here the silence is absolute save for the slow drip of stagnant condensate. Steadying your breath against the rising panic in your chest, you reach into the dark alcove and your fingers brush the cold wax and rough wick of a hidden cache of tallow candles.

Tucking the salvage safely into your oilskin pocket, you turn your boot toward the junction ahead.

nodes.title: The Iron Switch
nodes.brief: You force the jammed switch with a heavy grease-bar, risking a scalded arm if the pressure backfires, and secure a spare copper gasket.
nodes.page:
Leaning your full weight against the heavy grease-bar, you force the rusted switch-point as it shrieks in protest against decades of accumulated coal-dust and scale. A sudden hiss of superheated steam spits from the failing joint beside your knuckles, threatening to scald your skin if the pressure backfires into the pit. Grit your teeth against the blistering heat, you throw your hip into the lever until the tongue snaps home with a satisfying iron thud.

Slipping the spare copper gasket from the spindle-slot, you secure your prize in your pocket.

nodes.title: The Clerk's Ledger
nodes.brief: You outwit the stationmaster's clerk with a swift reading of the old railway rule-book, and claim a signed bill of indemnity.
nodes.page:
Sliding the dog-eared railway rule-book across the scarred oak counter, you tap a grease-stained thumb against paragraph four of the emergency schedule. The clerk blinks behind his spectacles, his pen hovering uncertainly over the ledger as he weighs your authority against the rising fury of the storm outside. You hold his gaze without blinking until he sighs, dips his nib in the violet ink, and stamps the paper with the station seal.

Folding the signed bill of indemnity, you tuck it inside your waistcoat.

nodes.title: The Drainage Culvert
nodes.brief: You crawl through the narrow drainage culvert while choking soot fills the air, maintaining your composure, and find a hidden cache of tallow candles.
nodes.page:
Choking soot fills the narrow iron-ribbed culvert as you force your way forward on hands and knees, every breath scraping your throat like dry pumice. Maintaining your composure against the rising panic of the dark, your fingers brush against a rough wooden crate wedged deep beneath the masonry. You pry the lid open to find a hidden cache of thick tallow candles, smelling faintly of rendered mutton and dry cellar dust.

Shoving a pair of the candles into your canvas jacket, you press on through the gloom toward the faint grey glimmer of light at the far end of the pipe.

exits.label: Crawl through to the outlet below the tracks

nodes.title: The Bronze Pillar
nodes.brief: You stand before the bronze pillar of the Water Gate with the heavy brass key in your hand, ready to make the final choice for Cinderfall.
nodes.page:
Standing before the immense bronze pillar of the Water Gate, you feel the cold heft of the brass key in your palm as the storm clock ticks down its final, hollow beats. Cinderfall holds its breath behind the titanic bulk of the dam, while the low rumble of the approaching ash-tempest shakes the foundations of the terminal cliff. From the shadows every faction watches the spindle that can wash the grey steppes or seal the doom of the iron road forever. The gear awaits your hand.

Turn the great brass key.

exits.label: Strike a bargain with the barons
Let the deep waters drown all

nodes.title: The First Turn
nodes.brief: Ending "Open the Water Gate"
nodes.page:
The brass key engages the bronze tumblers with a shriek that echoes off the vaulted limestone ceiling of the terminal. Old scale flakes away from the ancient threads, falling like black snow onto the soot-stained flags beneath your boots. You throw your entire weight against the long arm of the valve, feeling the immense hydraulic pressure of the reservoir straining against decades of neglect. Water begins to weep from the cracked seals, smelling of mountain moss and pristine snow.

The heavy pillar shudders, groaning as the long-stalled mechanism finally breaks its rust-bound sleep.

nodes.title: The Rushing Tide
nodes.brief: Ending "Open the Water Gate"
nodes.page:
A white plume of pent-up spray bursts from the high gallery, instantly washing away the choking grey ash that has smothered Cinderfall for generations. Down in the gulley, the rusted rails gleam under the sudden deluge, turning from dull iron to glistening silver as the fresh current scours the tracks clean. The people of the city crowd the iron balconies, pressing their faces into the cool, damp wind with shouts of disbelief and weeping laughter. You lean against the trembling pillar, watching the grey desert transform beneath the rushing tide.

The great basin empties its heart into the dry valleys below, drowning the dust.

exits.label: Watch the water claim the line

nodes.title: The Cleansing Wash
nodes.brief: Ending "Open the Water Gate"
nodes.page:
Torrents of crystal water roar through the lower viaducts, sweeping away the stranded wrecks and the burnt-out hulks of the Grey Bazaar like drifted straw. The low sky cracks open above the terminal, letting a pale, true sunlight pierce the broken clouds for the first time since the Long Fire began its reign. Steam rises in thick white billows where the cold flood meets the hot cinders of the steppes, wrapping the valley in a clean, breathable fog. The iron road is flooded, but the land finally drinks.

Stand firm as the deluge surrounds the engine.

exits.label: Step down into the cool flow

nodes.title: The Last Arrival
nodes.brief: Ending "Open the Water Gate"
nodes.page:
Locomotive No. 9 rests quietly in the wash of the great spillway, her boiler cooling at last as the fires within her belly die down to a peaceful, embers-glow. You leave the brass key where it rests in the turned valve, its teeth gleaming bright against the dark green metal of the gate. The Marrowbone has brought her charge home through ash and iron, fulfilling the old debt under a sky washed clear of soot. There are no more schedules to keep, no more signals to read in the dark, and the water runs deep and cold through the streets of Cinderfall.

The journey is finished, and the long road rests beneath the water.

nodes.title: The Ledger of Iron
nodes.brief: Ending "The Baron's Bargain"
nodes.page: Ledger books bound in pigskin slide across the mahogany counter with the weight of tombstones, closed by men whose cuffs are stiff with dried ink and coal dust. The Rail Barons do not shout; they negotiate in the quiet click of brass abacuses and the steady scratching of nibs that record every gallon of water now flowing down the masonry. Your boots leave wet prints upon their patterned carpet, smelling of river silt and old grease, entirely out of place among the velvet and polished rosewood. They offer you a desk near the high windows, a silver watch on a heavy chain, and a title that sounds remarkably like a life sentence served in comfortable slippers.

exits.label: Sign your name in black ink

nodes.title: Silence in the Boardroom
nodes.brief: Ending "The Baron's Bargain"
nodes.page: Outside, the great iron city hums with a new rhythm, slow and measured like the heartbeat of a tethered beast that has forgotten how to run. Hesper Quill would have spat upon their ledgers and thrown the inkwell through their leaded glass, preferring the bite of the cinders and the fierce wind of the open steppe. You turn the brass valve-key in your pocket one last time, feeling its cold ridges against your palm before placing it upon the polished cedar table as a final, silent payment. The directors do not look up from their columns of figures, too busy calculating the tariff on every drop that slakes the thirst of the lower wards.

exits.label: Step back into the grey corridor

nodes.title: The Unpaved Horizon
nodes.brief: Ending "The Baron's Bargain"
nodes.page: Down in the yards, Locomotive No. 9 stands cold and silent on the siding, her firebox grey and dead, her brass dull beneath a skim of dried spray. No smoke rises from her stack, and the gangers have already begun unbolting her side-rods to salvage the metal for other, more profitable lines of transit. You walk away through the damp ballast, leaving the station behind without a backward glance as the low grey clouds part just enough to show an empty, unpaved horizon stretching out beyond the reach of any track. There are no more timetables to keep, and the road ahead belongs entirely to whatever is left of your own worn boots.

exits.label: Walk out into the wide ash

nodes.title: The Great Unmaking
nodes.brief: Ending "Burn the Iron Road"
nodes.page: Flames lick along the creosoted ties with a dry, rattling roar that dances across the steppe like an army of crimson spiders devouring the past. Behind you the viaduct's timbers groan and twist under the unbearable heat. Decades of greasy soot and iron scale peel off into the boiling flood below. The Rail Barons' telegraph wires snap one by one in the fierce updraft, singing high and mournful notes into the grey sky before falling silent in the ash. No engine will ever run these rails again, and the rust can finally have its way with the bridges that once held a starving world in chains.

nodes.title: Footsteps in the Cinders
nodes.brief: Ending "Burn the Iron Road"
nodes.page: You walk away from the burning line across ground suddenly free of ballast, ties, and the watchful eyes of signal boxes. The air smells of scorched willow-wood and sweet, damp earth where the liberated water has found its own ancient channels through the dust. Other gangers join you from the embankments, carrying empty oil-cans and worn shovels, their faces smeared with charcoal and something resembling genuine laughter for the first time in years. You share a final twist of salt-beef and watch the smoke from the ruined tracks drift away into the vast, empty distance where no trains can ever follow.

nodes.title: The Last Engine
nodes.brief: Ending "Burn the Iron Road"
nodes.page: Darkness falls slowly over the grey flats, unmeasured by whistles or the harsh glare of headlamps cutting through the choking ash-storms of the old days. The Iron Road is gone, reduced to twisted ribbons of red-hot metal cooling slowly in the mud and black skeletons of trestle bridges spanning empty air. Yet beneath your boots, the earth feels soft and damp with the promise of green shoots pushing up through the crust of the long fire's legacy. The brass valve-key stays in your pocket. It opens no gate now; it marks a journey that ended the only way a good road should. The night is quiet, the wind is clean, and the long walk home has finally begun.

nodes.title: The Iron Fellowship
nodes.brief: Ending "The Gangers' Republic"
nodes.page: Ash settles thick upon the discarded ledgers of the Rail Barons, sealing their ledgers in a grey shroud of rust and cancelled debt. You stand on the footplate of the Marrowbone. The brass valve-key rests in its cradle, a plain tool now for the people who mend the ties. Around you, the gangers of the Union gather with their shovels and oil-cans, their laughter tasting of grease and bitter tea as they pull down the high semaphore gates that once dictated every heartbeat on the line. The iron does not fall with a crash; it yields slowly to the crowd's pull, bending like old grass under a late autumn frost. Every signal box between Ashgate and the high wall of Cinderfall stands dark tonight, its glass empty of watchers, leaving the road wide and unmeasured beneath a low, indifferent sky.

exits.label: Watch the semaphore blades fall into the dust

nodes.title: Without a Master
nodes.brief: Ending "The Gangers' Republic"
nodes.page: No whistle blows to mark the passing hours, because time has ceased to belong to the men in tall hats who kept the clocks in the back offices. You shovel fine coal into the belly of the Marrowbone, watching the orange glow reflect in the wet eyes of companions who have traded their rations for a share in the road. Cinderfall's great Water Gate remains unlatched at last, its heavy bronze gears turned by many hands rather than a single tyrant's decree, letting the cool mountain water run free through the rusted sluices to refresh the gray flats below. There is no applause from the parapets, only the steady hiss of steam escaping into the dusk and the sound of hammers ringing against the iron plates as the unions carve their own names into the tender-frames. Old debts are paid in sweat and shared bread, leaving the slate clean enough to write upon with chalk.

exits.label: Sit upon the iron bench as evening falls

nodes.title: The Last Fire
nodes.brief: Ending "The Gangers' Republic"
nodes.page: Night settles deep over the Ashen Steppe, but the darkness is no longer lonely or watched by cold electric eyes from distant gantries. The Marrowbone idles at the platform's edge, its furnace breathing a steady, warm red into the drafty air while the grease-lamps flicker along the open corridor where no tickets are ever checked again. You leave your heavy leather gloves on the grease-board and step down into the grey dust, your boots crunching on ballast that now belongs to nobody and everybody all at once. Far down the track, a single signal arm stays fixed half-raised in an eternal, useless greeting to the empty horizon, too stubborn to drop and too tired to care. The road stretches out before you toward the hills, silent, patient, and entirely your own.

nodes.title: Ashes of the Law
nodes.brief: Ending "The Prophets' Pyre"
nodes.page: Flames leap high from the burning station-house at Ashgate, casting long, writhing shadows of soot across the ruined platforms where the old schedule-books feed the pyre. You watch the charred pages drift into the grey upper air like flocks of black swallows seeking a season that never comes. The Cinder Prophets gather around the blaze with their faces smeared in grease and red clay, chanting low hymns that celebrate the great burning as a sacred clearing of the ground. The heavy iron of the rails glows cherry-red in the heat, twisting and warping until no engine could ever travel upon them again, returning the metal to the earth from which it was dragged so many years ago. Every ledger, ticket-punch, and iron desk is consumed by the cleansing heat, leaving nothing behind but the clean smell of wood-smoke and the dry rattle of cinder-dust in the wind.

exits.label: Feed another ledger to the hungry flames

nodes.title: The Teacher's Voice
nodes.brief: Ending "The Prophets' Pyre"
nodes.page: Smoke rolls thick across the steppe, blotting out the stars and turning the pale moon into a dull brass button pinned to a dirty coat. You stand among the burning ties with the brass Water Key held high in your bare hand, feeling the metal grow hot not from steam, but from the fierce conviction of the crowd surrounding you. Cinderfall's high walls loom through the haze, their shuttered windows blind to the red glow that dances along the base of the great masonry. The prophets whisper of a world reborn from ash, where no trains run to bind the hours and no signals dictate the rhythm of a man's breathing. Every barrier falls before the heat, and the massive gates of the reservoir groan as the fire licks at their ancient timbers, demanding a reckoning that no timetable can postpone or forgive.

exits.label: Watch the great gates char and crumble

nodes.title: A Clean Slate
nodes.brief: Ending "The Prophets' Pyre"
nodes.page: Silence follows the great fire, a vast and heavy quiet that settles over the blackened plain like a blanket of cold wool. The Marrowbone stands cold upon its dead track, its brass fittings dulled by soot and its boiler silent forever, a monument to the age of iron that burned itself out to the last coal. You walk away from the smoking ruins toward the open hills, leaving the brass key half-melted in the embers of the great pyre where the old world held its final class. There are no roads left to follow and no schedules to keep, only the endless expanse of grey dust stretching out beneath a sky that has forgotten the color of smoke. The prophets have gone ahead into the dark, singing their ragged songs to the wind, and you walk behind them into a morning that has no need of whistles or destinations.

nodes.title: The Lanterns Below
nodes.brief: Ending "Signalman Eternal"
nodes.page: Cold iron beneath your palms has the familiar weight of a service long kept, each rivet singing the same low tune against the vibration of the rail. You pull the heavy brass lever two notches back, letting the green signal-arm drop into its slot with a hollow clatter that echoes off the tunnel walls. Above you, in the high timber of the roof, the Hollow Signalmen move without sound, their lanterns swinging in slow, deliberate arcs that map a road no living man was ever meant to walk alone. The smoke from the firebox drifts back through the cab, tasting of old coke and damp earth, mingling with the grease on your sleeves until you cannot tell where your coat ends and the engine begins. Every red eye along the permanent way turns green as you pass, acknowledging the hand that never left the iron.

exits.label: Step into the green light of the junction

nodes.title: The Permanent Way
nodes.brief: Ending "Signalman Eternal"
nodes.page: Night has no beginning here, only a deeper shade of soot that settles between the sleepers and coats the ballast in a fine, grey powder. You tend the fire, casting shovelfuls of dry slack into the amber roar of the belly while the pressure needle hovers at the exact red mark the old timetables demanded. Down the line, past the rusted gantries and the silent water-towers, the rails stretch out like twin threads of polished silver under a sky that has forgotten how to clear. No schedule is posted on the wall of this cab, for time has stopped ticking in the brass clock, leaving only the rhythm of the exhaust and the quiet company of those who watch from the shadows of the telegraph poles.

exits.label: Ride the rhythm of the endless rail

nodes.title: Signalman Eternal
nodes.brief: Ending "Signalman Eternal"
nodes.page: Far ahead, where the cuttings narrow into the eternal dark of the final range, a single yellow lamp burns steady through the drift. You do not whistle for the crossing, because there is nothing left to warn and no one left to pay the toll at the gate. The Marrowbone rolls on through the quiet dark, its cylinders ticking as they cool, carrying its fireman deeper into the service of the line where no train ever stops and no journey ever reaches an end. Here, among the ghosts of old gangers and forgotten engines, you tend the fire and watch the signals change from red to green, forever bound to the iron road and the long night of the steppe.

nodes.title: Beyond the Water Gate
nodes.brief: Ending "The Last Train Out"
nodes.page: Rushing water thunders through the great brass sluices as the valve-key turns with a long, protesting groan of ancient threads. At last the iron gates of Cinderfall swing inward. They part the thick yellow smog of the steppe, and a cold, clean wind sweeps across the dry cobbles of the lower wards. Down below, the crowds press close against the low stone walls, staring in silence at the steam-plume rising from the stack of Locomotive No. 9 as it breaks through the barricades. The Rail Barons' clerks drop their ledgers in the mud, too astonished to speak, while the gangers on the embankments raise their hammers in a slow, hard salute that needs no words.

exits.label: Open the regulator for the open plain

nodes.title: The Smoke Clear
nodes.brief: Ending "The Last Train Out"
nodes.page: Behind the engine, the great walled city opens its dry throat to the flood, drinking deep from the black reservoirs while the steam whistle blows a long, triumphant blast that rattles the glass in every window from the market square to the summit. You wipe the grease from your forehead with the back of a blackened hand, feeling the heat of the firebox die down to a steady, manageable glow as the pressure eases in the copper tubes. The ash-storm season breaks against the battlements and falls away like spent coal, leaving the tracks clear toward the western horizon where the sky finally shows a pale, washed strip of blue.

exits.label: Drive the engine past the final signal

nodes.title: The Last Train Out
nodes.brief: Ending "The Last Train Out"
nodes.page: Out past the suburbs and the abandoned sidings, the open steppe stretches away under a morning that smells of wet earth and rusted iron. The Marrowbone rolls easy on the jointed track, its bell ringing a slow, clear note for every mile of newly opened road, leaving the high walls and the old debts far behind in the grey smoke. There are no schedules left to keep and no Barons to ask for your pass, only the endless twin lines running west toward the sunrise and the clean smell of steam on the wind. You bank the fire for the last time today, pull your cap low against the morning chill, and let the engine carry you home.

nodes.title: The Missing Driver
nodes.brief: Ending "Hesper's Return"
nodes.page:
Smoke drifts lazy from the regulator box as a familiar figure leans against the tender rail, oil-stained cap pulled low against the morning glare. Hesper Quill looks neither surprised nor triumphant, merely tired in the way of someone who has walked a long circle back to where the coal-dust settles thickest. A grease-rag comes out of a pocket, wiping dark smears from knuckles that have held no throttle for days.

There are no explanations offered for the empty depot at Ashgate or the sealed orders left upon the brass gauge-stand. The engine breathes a low-pressure sigh between you, and hot tallow and wet cinders fill the cab once more as if no miles of ash-steppe had ever rolled beneath the wheels.

exits.label: Step back from the regulator handle

nodes.title: A Seat Returned
nodes.brief: Ending "Hesper's Return"
nodes.page:
Weight settles onto the driver's bench with the familiar creak of old ash-wood and worn springs. Hesper reaches out a thumb to test the needle on the steam pressure gauge, tapping the glass lightly until the brass pointer settles true. The water glass shows a full gauge, clear and green where the injector feeds the boiler from the newly opened mains below the city.

Not a single word passes between the cab sides about the empty miles or the closed signals that waited in the dark cuts. There is only the routine of the line, the shared knowledge of firebox temperatures, and the slow, heavy settling of iron cooling after a hard run through the passes.

nodes.title: The Line Remembers
nodes.brief: Ending "Hesper's Return"
nodes.page:
Outside the footplate windows, the morning mist lifts from the flooded suburbs to reveal the long, shining parallel of the rails stretching back toward the ash-dunes. Signals along the embankment drop their arms with a sharp, clean click of iron wire, acknowledging a road that is open from the mountain roots to the central platforms. The Marrowbone stands easy in her harness, no longer a fugitive engine carrying a stolen brass key through hostile territory, but a scheduled working on a cleared metal road.

A vibration runs through the deck plates as the injector keeps its rhythm, feeding clean water into the belly of the machine while the fire glows quiet and red behind the iron doors.

nodes.title: Ash and Steam
nodes.brief: Ending "Hesper's Return"
