nodes.page: Hesper takes the heavy brass valve-key from your palm, turning the cold metal over once in calloused fingers before tossing it carelessly onto the tool-shelf beside the grease-pot. The firebox door clicks shut, sealing the white heat inside where it belongs, and the whistle cord hangs quiet above your head. Out across the station apron, the water from the open gates runs clear through every street and alley of Cinderfall, splashing against stone walls and soaking deep into the dry earth until the whole valley smells of wet dust and iron. There are no medals waiting on the platform, no speeches from the Rail Barons or the Stationmaster-General, only the smell of good Welsh coal and the long, straight road home waiting under a quiet sky. The regulator eases forward with a gentle hiss of steam, and the world begins to move again.

nodes.title: Water in the Streets
nodes.brief: Ending "The Flooded Terminus"
nodes.page:
Through the open cab windows comes the roar of a thousand long-dry fountains drinking their fill at last, splashing cold and loud against the masonry of the central plaza. The engine stands upon the terminal bridge like a monument of soot and brass, surrounded by people who have dropped their buckets and copper dippers to stare at the grey spray rising from the old stone basins. Water curls around the driving wheels, washing away the stubborn crust of the Ashen Steppe that has baked into the iron since the Long Fire first scorched the lowlands.

A great cheer goes up from the crowded platforms, thin and cracked with old thirst, echoing off the iron roof timbers until the soot flakes down like black snow upon the waiting crowds.

nodes.title: The Stationmaster's Ledger
nodes.brief: Ending "The Flooded Terminus"
nodes.page:
High on the gallery above the terminal tracks, the Stationmaster-General closes her heavy leather ledger with a sharp crack that can be heard over the rushing of the water. The gold-nibbed pen is laid aside in its groove, and the great brass timetable clock on the wall ticks forward into an hour that was never written in the schedules. Down on the footplate, the fire settles into a contented glow that needs no shovel, burning clear on the draft from the open bay doors.

The Marrowbone has brought her train through every block and signal without a single yellow caution, running strictly to a time that only the old tracks know.

nodes.title: The Last Schedule
nodes.brief: Ending "The Flooded Terminus"
nodes.page: There are no more orders to collect from the ticket-widow, no sealed envelopes left behind on empty desks in the depot at Ashgate, and no red flags waving from the cuttings. The water runs deep and sweet through the conduits beneath Cinderfall, filling every cellar and cistern until the city floats upon its own bright lake like an iron ship anchored in the ash. Hesper Quill is gone again, slipped away down the platform while the steam hissed loud from the cylinders, leaving the engine in your sole care with the fire burning red and clean. You pull the brass whistle cord once, a long, deep roar that shakes the glass in the station roof and rolls out across the grey steppe where the rails run straight into the morning mist. The Marrowbone rolls forward into the cool air, keeping her own time down the long road.

nodes.title: The Quiet Siding
nodes.brief: Ending "The Quiet Siding"
nodes.page: No signals fall to green for you now, nor do the Barons' ledger-clerks come running with warrants or ink-horns. Locomotive No. 9 sets her iron ribs against the rusted buffers of a forgotten siding, firebed cooling to a dull honest ember under the grey drift of the Cinderfall sky. You set the brass valve-key down on the timber deck and watch faint steam lift from the regulator valve. The long road from Ashgate is behind you, its iron miles bitten through by ash and time, and the water you let loose still pounds against the masonry of the central plaza like a heart finding its beat after decades of stone-still drought.

exits.label: Step down onto the quiet ballast

nodes.title: Beyond the Last Buffer
nodes.brief: Ending "The Quiet Siding"
nodes.page: Silence settles over the cab, thick with the smell of scorched oil, burnt coal-dust, and the sharp copper tang of a journey well-run. Hesper Quill is nowhere in the ash-grey shadows, yet the empty seat beside the fire-door feels less like an abandonment and more like a place kept warm for another shift that never quite arrives. Outside, the soot-stained roofs of the last walled city stretch out beneath a low, unmoving cloud-blanket, indifferent to the history you have dragged through their gates on ten tons of steel and boiler-plate. You wipe your palms on a greasy rag, leaving dark smears of soot that will take weeks of hard scrubbing - or perhaps no scrubbing at all - to wash away from your skin.

exits.label: Leave the engine to the ash

nodes.title: The End of the Line
nodes.brief: Ending "The Quiet Siding"
nodes.page: There are no more timetables to keep, no sealed orders tucked beneath greasy cushions, and no frantic gangers waving red flags from the cuttings. You walk the length of the silent train one last time, your boots crunching softly upon the fallen ash that drifts across the tracks like grey snow. The iron road ends here, swallowed by the great grey steppes and the quiet persistence of a world that remembers its own dead. You pull your collar high against the rising chill, turning your face toward the open track beyond the buffers, where the horizon dissolves into a seamless wash of earth and sky, and wait for whatever morning chooses to find you.

nodes.title: The Stationmaster's Heir
nodes.brief: Ending "The Stationmaster's Heir"
nodes.page: Oak doors swing shut hard enough to shake dust from the arched cornices above the gallery, sealing you within the cool, paper-scented shadows of the keep. The Stationmaster-General sits motionless in her high-backed chair of carved mahogany, her ancient hands folded over the leather spine of the great ledger as if holding down the very floorboards of Cinderfall. She does not offer praise, nor does she ask for the names of the gangers who fell beside the iron road, for the ledgers of the city record only balances struck and debts cleared. You lay the heavy brass Water Key across her desk, its metal still warm from the long run through the ash-storm.

nodes.title: Ink and Iron
nodes.brief: Ending "The Stationmaster's Heir"
nodes.page: A dry rustle of parchment fills the high room as the old woman opens the heavy book to a blank page near the end of the volume, her quill dipping once into an ink-pot that has stood in the same place for fifty winters. She writes your name in a small, cramped hand that brook no argument, fitting it neatly between a cancelled tariff for anthracite and an uncollected fine from the Rail Barons. In the quiet gallery you watch the iron-nib scratch the paper and know your days of shovelling coal and watching signals loom out of the murk are gone for good. The city outside drinks its fill from the restored fountains, but here inside the keep, time moves only by the scratch of ink.

exits.label: Sign away your last free mile

nodes.title: The Last Ledger
nodes.brief: Ending "The Stationmaster's Heir"
nodes.page: The pen is laid aside in its groove of polished bone, and the ink dries dark and dull against the page while the city below settles into a cautious, water-rich peace. You are no longer the guard of the Marrowbone, nor a ganger running from the Barons' tally-men on the Cinder Steppe, but part of the machinery now - fixed as firmly to the wall as the brass dials and the pendulum clocks that govern the gates. Through the tall window, the grey sky hangs low over the ramparts, and somewhere far down the line, a solitary whistle blows three short blasts into the ash. You shut the ledger covers yourself: the line is run and the books are balanced until the next fire starts.

nodes.title: The Ledger Closes
nodes.brief: Ending "Dead Steam"
nodes.page:
Silence settles over the high vaulted room like a blanket of grey wool among unreadable debts and dry parchment. The Stationmaster-General watches the dark ink settle into the grain of the page, her ancient fingers resting entirely still beside the bone-handled pen. Below your boots, the deep thrum of the engine dies away into a faint, shivering rattle as the last measure of pressure bleeds from the regulator and leaves the brass cold to the touch. There is no water rising in the dry basins, and the massive valves remain stubbornly bolted against the dust of the steppes.

You stand alone in the quiet gloom with a brass key that has lost its purpose and a furnace that will never draw another breath, while the low sky outside darkens toward an endless winter of ash and iron.

exits.label: Leave the silent keep by the heavy oak doors

nodes.title: Cold Ash and Iron
nodes.brief: Ending "Dead Steam"
nodes.page: Outside the gallery windows, the great walled city of Cinderfall lies mute beneath a low, yellowish sky that threatens to bury the remaining rooftops in drifts of dry grit. You walk down through the narrow, unlit stairwells where the smell of stale coal smoke clings stubbornly to the stonework, past ticket-windows that will never open again and signal-boxes whose levers have rusted fast in their iron beds. No steam whistles greet the twilight, and no gangers walk the platform with their oil-lamps swinging in the gloom. The Marrowbone waits on the dead siding outside the walls, her boiler stone-cold and her fire-box choked with the grey leavings of a journey that ended just short of salvation. You fold your heavy coat against the rising wind from the steppes and set off down the track on foot, leaving the engine to rust among the weeds while the ash-storms close their grey fingers over the last road.

nodes.title: The Water Rises
nodes.brief: Ending "Open the Water Gate"
nodes.page: A long, deep groan shakes the foundations of the ancient masonry as the massive brass valves finally turn under the leverage of your tired arms, biting through decades of green scale and dried grease with a sharp, metallic shriek. For a breathless moment nothing moves. Then a subterranean shudder runs through the stone channels beneath your boots, and dark water leaps from the deep mountain springs into the empty reservoirs with a sudden roar. The spray catches the dim light of the high clerestory windows, turning the drifting dust to gold as the cool, sweet scent of wet earth and living river fills the damp galleries. Down in the city below, distant shouts rise from the courtyards as the dry fountains begin to gush and the garden beds drink their fill after years of thirst. You wipe the black grease from your forehead with a soot-stained sleeve and lean against the massive wheel, listening to the music of the rushing water that has finally come home.

nodes.title: Schedule and Sovereign
nodes.brief: Ending "The Baron's Bargain"
nodes.page: The ledger lies open on the polished walnut desk, pages ruled in neat columns of black and red ink that account for every ton of coal and every gallon of water left in the hills. The Rail Barons' agent nods once, a curt tip of a chin above a stiff linen collar, and sets his thumb over the brass key you have placed on the green baize. Outside the high tall windows, the marshalling yards begin to shift with the smooth, oiled precision of a well-kept timetable as fresh locomotives back into the sidings to haul away the surplus. You receive your sealed discharge and a modest purse of minted copper, the legal price of an engine surrendered and a debt duly paid according to the rule of the line. The Marrowbone is someone else's property now, her fire drawn and her brass polished for a master who cares nothing for the ash-storms, leaving you to turn your back on the tracks and find your way into a city that runs by someone else's clock.
